searchDocs.title: CannonServer
searchDocs.content: CannonServer This item only works when running on the server. Server Authority for the manned cannon (Perk Spec 5). Discovers placed cannons in workspace.PlacedObjects (by the PlaceableName attribute), validates mount/fire requests, and simulates an authoritative explosive arc shell via a FastCast2 cast with a gravity Acceleration (the rocket pattern from WeaponServer). Damage is scaled by the CannonDamage party perk and applied through CombatService.ApplyAOE. Heat is tracked per cannon and published as Heat/Overheated attributes on the placed Model (no extra packet). Client aim is never trusted for damage.

searchDocs.title: CharacterCollisionService
searchDocs.content: CharacterCollisionService This item only works when running on the server. Server Places every BasePart of every player character into the Character collision group (see CollisionGroups). This is what lets physics projectiles (WeaponProjectile) and dropped materials (DroppedMaterial) pass through players while still colliding with world geometry — all three previously shared the Default group, so they could not be told apart by the physics solver. Parts that stream in after spawn (R15 limbs, accessories) are caught viaDescendantAdded; the connection is owned by a per-character Janitor torn down when the character is destroyed.

searchDocs.title: CombatService
searchDocs.content: CombatService This item only works when running on the server. Server Single server-side damage router. Resolves a hit (part or Model) to a target and routes damage: a Player's character goes through HealthManager (keeps the HUD-tracked record correct); a faction-tagged NPC (EnemyNPC / FriendlyNPC, see Factions) with a Humanoid takes direct Humanoid damage. Anything else is ignored. This is the ONLY place weapon code applies damage. NPC contract: a Model containing a Humanoid, tagged with EITHER the CollectionService tag "EnemyNPC" or "FriendlyNPC" (see Factions). That same tag also places the NPC's parts in the Character collision group (see NpcCollisionService), so thrown charges pass through it. Friendly-fire is enforced here via Factions.canDamage: only Player<->Enemy damage lands, so players never hurt players or friendly NPCs and enemies never hurt enemies or friendly NPCs. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt. A nil attacker is treated as environmental and bypasses the faction gate. Enemy AI/spawning is supplied elsewhere; this module only deals damage.

searchDocs.title: CollisionGroups
searchDocs.content: CollisionGroups This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative registrar for every physics CollisionGroup in the game and the single place their collidability matrix is defined. Requiring this module (cached, so it runs exactly once) registers the groups and applies the relationships below; consumers then assign part.CollisionGroup using the exported name constants. Groups (besides the built-in Default): Character — every BasePart of a player character (see CharacterCollisionService) or of a faction-tagged model ("EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC", see NpcCollisionService). WeaponProjectile — thrown charges / physics projectiles (see ServerProjectile). DroppedMaterial / DroppableSurface — the proximity/drop item system. Relationships (only non-default entries; new groups collide with everything by default, so we only turn the wrong pairs OFF): A B Collidable Why DroppedMaterial Default ✗ drops pass through characters/walls/untagged world DroppedMaterial DroppableSurface ✓ …and only land on tagged surfaces DroppedMaterial Character ✗ preserve pass-through now that characters left Default WeaponProjectile Character ✗ charges pass through ALL players (AOE handles damage) WeaponProjectile WeaponProjectile ✗ charges don't knock each other around WeaponProjectile DroppedMaterial ✗ loose junk doesn't stop a charge mid-flight Everything else stays default-true: WeaponProjectile collides with Default DroppableSurface (so it bounces/sticks on arbitrary world geometry), and Character collides with Default/DroppableSurface/Character (players collide with world, platforms, and each other exactly as before).

Drives a caller-authored button that has an Option (TextLabel) and Arrow (ImageLabel) child, building a selectable option list directly beneath it. searchDocs.title: EnemyBrain
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain This item only works when running on the server. Server Centralized enemy AI director. Ticks every armed enemy at TICK_HZ through two independent concerns: MOVEMENT (pathfind toward the nearest player to a comfort distance) and FIRING (burst/cooldown, run-and-gun — added in later tasks). One Janitor per enemy record. PathfindingService:ComputeAsync is budgeted across enemies so 40 enemies stay affordable. Deliberately simple: no cover, no coordination, no target leading.

searchDocs.title: EnemyCombatConfig
searchDocs.content: EnemyCombatConfig Per-archetype enemy combat profiles. Keyed by the archetype name used in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes. An archetype with NO entry here stays passive (EnemyBrain only arms archetypes it finds a profile for). Enemies have NO ammo/reload: ranged cadence is a burst-then-cooldown rhythm. Ranged fire is PROJECTILE (dodgeable), never hitscan. All combat tuning lives here.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawner
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner This item only works when running on the server. Server Generic, server-authoritative combatant spawner. Places enemy/friendly NPC Models at attachment-authored spawn points (tag EnemySpawnGroup / point tag EnemySpawnPoint), with radial jitter, SpawnVerification, cumulative-inverse weighted point selection, drip-feed waves, and a tracked WaveHandle. Spawned Models are tagged EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPC so CombatService/NpcCollisionService pick them up automatically. Owns spawning only — orchestrators decide when.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnerConfig
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnerConfig Tuning + archetype registry for the EnemySpawner service. Mirrors the JunkConfig pattern: archetype Model names are resolved against ServerStorage.EnemyAssets at load (warn on missing). All spawner tuning lives here — no magic numbers in spawner code.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWave
searchDocs.content: EnemyWave This item only works when running on the server. Server Factory for a WaveHandle: a Janitor-backed tracker over a set of spawned enemy Models. Watches each enemy's Humanoid.Died and removal; when the live count reaches 0 AND the wave has been marked complete (all drip-feed spawns attempted), fires OnCleared exactly once. Returned by EnemySpawner.SpawnWave.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWeapon
searchDocs.content: EnemyWeapon This item only works when running on the server. Server The enemy attack action. Reuses the player damage layer: FastCast2 projectiles, ServerProjectile lobs, WeaponValidation melee hitbox, and CombatService routing with attacker = enemyModel (Factions already allows Enemy -> Player). Enemy ranged fire is a TRAVELLING projectile (damage on FastCast2 Hit), never hitscan, so a moving player can dodge. Timing/ammo is owned by EnemyBrain, not here.

searchDocs.title: SetJumpPaused​
searchDocs.content: </> EventOrchestrator.SetJumpPaused(paused: boolean) → () Suspends event scheduling for the duration of a jump. Pausing force-finishes any Active channel through its existing activeFinish, the same path the MaxActiveDistance watchdog and Reset use. Because PirateAttackEvent registers its wave as ctx.janitor:Add(wave, "Destroy"), that despawns any surviving attackers — jumping mid-raid leaves them behind, which is what makes "players are safe inside the wormhole" actually true. The odometer is suspended, not reset, so encounter pacing resumes unchanged. Caveat: EventConfig.Enabled is currently false, so Init returns before ever subscribing to OnJumpPhaseChanged and this whole path is dormant. It is still wired correctly so it isn't the thing that breaks when the master switch is flipped on.

searchDocs.title: Factions
searchDocs.content: Factions Combat faction policy shared by client and server. Resolves a Player or a Humanoid-bearing Model to a Faction, and decides whether one faction may damage another via a default-deny hostility table. Faction comes from: a Player (or a Model that is a player's character) → "Player"; a Model tagged EnemyTag → "Enemy"; a Model tagged FriendlyTag → "Friendly". These two tags REPLACE the former single "NPC" tag — being either tag marks a Model as a combatant (damageable + collision pass-through; see NpcCollisionService). Only Player<->Enemy damage is allowed. Every other ordered pair is denied, so there is no player-vs-player or enemy-vs-enemy damage, and friendly NPCs (e.g. the trader) cannot be damaged by anyone. The actual block is enforced server-side in CombatService; this module is shared so the client can reuse resolve for UI (e.g. hitmarker suppression).

searchDocs.title: GrabHook
searchDocs.content: GrabHook This item only works when running on the client. Client Tool script for the Grabhook item. On activation it spherecasts from the handle attachment toward the mouse cursor to find aimed junk, firesSignals.TryClaimJunk (handled by JunkController), then plays the outgoing beam and retraction animation via GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile before firing Signals.TryFinalizeJunk on retract completion. Looping and cooldown ready sounds are scheduled around the animation timeline. A per-frame force-field highlight tracks the currently aimed junk with a short grace period to prevent flicker. Equip and unequip toggle aim-mode camera via Signals.RequestShootingCamera.

searchDocs.title: CreateBeam​
searchDocs.content: </> GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam( att0: Attachment ,-- Origin attachment (typically on the tool handle). att1: Attachment ,-- Target attachment (typically on the junk part). parent: Instance -- Where to parent the created Beam. ) → Beam -- The newly created beam. Creates a Beam between att0 and att1, applies all visual properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals, and parents it to parent.

searchDocs.title: AnimateProjectile​
searchDocs.content: </> GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile( beam: Beam ,-- The beam created by CreateBeam. startAtt: Attachment ,-- The origin attachment (handle side). targetPart: BasePart ,-- The junk part being reeled in. hitPos: Vector3 ,-- The world position where the hook latched. onCleanup: (() → ())?-- Optional callback invoked when the animation ends. ) → RBXScriptConnection -- The RenderStepped connection driving the animation. Drives the three-phase grabhook animation for the tool user onRunService.RenderStepped: FLIGHT — the hook attachment lerps toward hitPos over a duration derived from distance and GrabHookConfig.Physics.Speed, with a sinusoidal rope wave that decays as the hook approaches. LATCH — a single transition frame that flattens the curve and records the retract distance. RETRACT — targetPart.Position is lerped back to the handle each frame. When retraction completes (or if targetPart leaves workspace), the beam and junk attachment are destroyed and onCleanup is called. Returns the RBXScriptConnection so the caller can disconnect early if needed.

searchDocs.title: AnimateObserver​
searchDocs.content: </> GrabHookVisuals.AnimateObserver( beam: Beam ,-- The beam to animate. startAtt: Attachment -- The origin attachment to clean up when done. ) → RBXScriptConnection -- The RenderStepped connection driving the animation. Drives a simplified rope-wave animation for spectating clients. Since the observer receives the event after server confirmation the hook is already assumed latched; the wave simply decays over time using a standard 1 / (1 + elapsed * decay) envelope. Automatically disconnects and destroys startAtt when the Beam is destroyed by the owning controller.

searchDocs.title: JumpDriveConfig
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveConfig Single tuning surface for the Jump Drive: bench interaction, charge values, phase durations, the biome registry, and arrival rewards. Edit gameplay here, never in manager or controller code. Studio setup required: Tag one Model JumpDriveBench with its PrimaryPart set. Give it a BasePart JumpPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt (opens the GUI). Give it a BasePart DepositPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt (feeds Energy tools). Tag one BasePart WormholeAnchor marking where the black hole appears. Create ReplicatedStorage/JumpDriveVfx holding Models Wormhole and Lightspeed. Create ReplicatedStorage/GuiAssets/JumpDriveGui and .../JumpVoteBanner (see plan Task 11).

searchDocs.title: JumpDriveGuiController
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives both jump-drive GUI surfaces from the single JumpStateSync payload, so the two can never disagree: Jump Drive panel — opened by the bench ProximityPrompt. Shows the charge gauge, the destination, a Jump button, and the full named vote roster. Vote banner — pushed to every player the moment a vote opens, wherever they are on the train. Non-modal and must never capture input: abstaining is neutral in the resolution rule, so a vote nobody sees is a vote that always passes on the initiator's lone yes. Both countdowns are extrapolated from the server's phaseEndsAt rather than counted down locally, so a late joiner and a player present the whole time see the same number.

searchDocs.title: JumpTransitionController
searchDocs.content: JumpTransitionController This item only works when running on the client. Client Renders the jump transition: the wormhole growing ahead of the train, the lightspeed rig, and a post-processing wash — plus the one-shot and looped SFX. This is not a cutscene. Nothing here takes camera or movement control; the player keeps playing while the world changes around them. Lighting is captured before anything is applied and restored through the jump Janitor, so a disconnect, an error, or a phase packet arriving out of order can never leave a player's Lighting permanently altered. That restoration is the one part of this controller where failure is not merely cosmetic.

searchDocs.title: JunkController
searchDocs.content: JunkController This item only works when running on the client. Client Manages all client-side visuals for floating junk. Pooled model instances are spawned and moved each PreSimulation step at a shared speed that ramps smoothly via smoothstep whenever the server sends a SetJunkSpeed packet. When a claim succeeds the junk is removed from simulation and tracked as retracting — other players see it slide toward the collector, while the collecting player's animation is driven by GrabHook's AnimateProjectile. JunkCollected returns the model to its pool. All junk-related network calls (ReqJunkClaim, ReqJunkFinalize) are owned here and triggered via Signals.TryClaimJunk / TryFinalizeJunk.

searchDocs.title: MeleeHandler
searchDocs.content: MeleeHandler This item only works when running on the client. Client Category handler for melee combo weapons. On left-click it runs the sharedresolveComboSwing to pick the next combo step (buffering the click while the current hit is still in recovery), then predicts that step: plays its swing sound + optional animation, runs the step hitbox for an instant hitmarker (Signals.WeaponLocalHit), draws the debug box, fires Signals.WeaponComboChanged, and sends the payload-less Packets.ReqMeleeSwing for the server to apply authoritative damage. Combo state is per-equipped-Tool (cleared on unequip), so it resets correctly on respawn/weapon-switch.

searchDocs.title: JunkService
searchDocs.content: JunkService This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative server script that drives the junk economy for Endless Journey. Runs a timed spawn loop that performs two-stage weighted selection — first a tier roll (multiplied by live GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers), then a type roll within that tier — with an energy-pity counter that guarantees an Energy item after ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD consecutive non-energy spawns. All active junk is tracked by a global distance odometer; a piece despawns automatically once it has travelled past DESPAWN_DISTANCE, keeping memory and network traffic bounded without a per-frame scan of every client. Claim/finalize follows a two-step reservation protocol: ReqJunkClaim checks server-side proximity (reconstructed from the shared odometer) and sets a timed reservation, while ReqJunkFinalize validates the reservation and hands the junk Tool to the player's Backpack via JunkToolManager.

searchDocs.title: NpcCollisionService
searchDocs.content: NpcCollisionService This item only works when running on the server. Server Places every BasePart of every faction-tagged Model ("EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC", see Factions) into the Character collision group (see CollisionGroups), so thrown charges (WeaponProjectile) and dropped materials (DroppedMaterial) pass through NPCs exactly as they pass through players. This is the non-player sibling of CharacterCollisionService: players are handled by Players events there, NPCs are handled by the faction tags here. Those same faction tags gate direct Humanoid damage and friendly-fire in CombatService (see Factions), so one tag makes a Model both projectile-pass-through and damageable. Parts that stream in after tagging (R15 limbs, accessories) are caught via a per-model DescendantAdded connection owned by a per-model Janitor. The Janitor is torn down when the tag is removed OR the model is destroyed — GetInstanceRemovedSignal fires in both cases, so no separate Destroying backstop is needed.

searchDocs.title: Packets
searchDocs.content: Packets Typed network packet registry. All client↔server traffic in the game goes through packets defined here — do not use raw RemoteEvent instances for new channels. Reliable packets use Packet(name, ...) directly; high-frequency positional packets (ghost updates) use makeUnreliable which wraps an UnreliableRemoteEvent for lower latency. The full networking map (direction, payload types, and which scripts send/receive each packet) lives in the Reference → Networking map inDocumentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md. Register new packets there whenever you add one here.

searchDocs.title: PerkConfig
searchDocs.content: PerkConfig Single tuning surface for the perk system. Each perk declares its category (Personal buffs the owner; Party buffs the whole server but only the highest level held by any player is active), its cap, the buff attribute key it publishes, and a linear per-level value (published value = PerLevel * level). Per project convention, tune perks here, not in code.

searchDocs.title: PerkClient
searchDocs.content: PerkClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client-side read model + command surface for the perk system. Owns NO GUI. Caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot, watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder, exposes queries returning PerkView descriptors, commands (Allocate/Respec) with optimistic prediction, and a Changed signal consumers subscribe to in order to repaint. Call Init() once from a bootstrap; any GUI then requires this module and reuses the singleton.

searchDocs.title: PerkController
searchDocs.content: PerkController This item only works when running on the client. Client Thin bootstrap. Initializes the PerkClient read model once on join so the perk data layer is warm before any perk GUI opens. Owns no GUI — the perk screens (Active / Upgrade) are authored separately and consume PerkClient.

searchDocs.title: PerkEffectsDispatcher
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher This item only works when running on the server. Server The single writer of the perk buff folders. Personal buffs go toReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId> (per-player attributes); party buffs go to ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs as the per-perk MAX level across all players in the server (the "only highest active" rule). Recomputes on allocate/respec (Signals.OnPerkStateChanged), player join, and player leave. Bridges the Junk Rarity party perk onto the existing ApplyTierMultiplier signal (which JunkService already listens for).

searchDocs.title: bind​
searchDocs.content: </> PlaceableActions.bind( model: Model ,-- The placed object whose actions are being bound. gui: Instance -- Root GUI instance containing MoveButton and/or StashButton. ) → Binding-- Binding handle; call :Unbind() to clean up. Wires MoveButton and StashButton inside gui to their respective server packets (ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable) for the given model. Button clicks are debounced: only one request may be in-flight at a time. When the server succeeds, the corresponding signal is fired: Move success → Signals.OnPlaceableMoved Stash success → Signals.OnPlaceableStashed The returned Binding has a single method: binding:Unbind() — disconnects all button listeners and suppresses any pending success signal. Call this when the GUI closes. Safe to call multiple times (subsequent calls are no-ops). Model destruction When model is destroyed by the server (which happens on success before the response arrives), button listeners are disconnected automatically. The in-flight success-signal path is preserved so callers still receive the OnPlaceableMoved / OnPlaceableStashed event.

searchDocs.title: PlacementCameraController
searchDocs.content: PlacementCameraController This item only works when running on the client. Client Takes exclusive ownership of the camera while build mode is active: a fixed-height, fixed-pitch, yaw-locked-at-entry top-down view that follows the player. Restores Enum.CameraType.Custom on exit. Independent of CameraController (Enum.CameraType.Custom + CameraOffset spring), which is harmlessly inert while this module owns the camera — it never touches Camera.CFrame or Camera.CameraType. Because this camera is Scriptable and driven entirely by hrp.Position plus a fixed yaw/pitch/height, it does not rotate in response to mouse delta the way the normal locked third-person camera does. The placement raycast aims from the mouse cursor's actual on-screen position, so on PC this module also frees the cursor (via Signals.RequestMouseIcon) while build mode is active so the player can aim. Entry and exit both ease the camera angle via an exponential chase-lerp (PlacementConfig.CameraTransitionSpeed) instead of snapping instantly. On exit there's no live Custom-camera CFrame to blend toward, so it eases toward an approximation reconstructed from the camera's offset relative to hrp at the moment build mode was entered, then hands off to Enum.CameraType.Custom once that blend has settled.

searchDocs.title: CalculatePlacement​
searchDocs.content: </> PlacementSystem:CalculatePlacement( rayOrigin: Vector3 ,-- World-space ray origin (typically the camera or mouse position). rayDirection: Vector3 -- World-space ray direction (magnitude determines max distance). ) → Vector3? -- Resolved surface position, or nil if no valid build area was hit. The raycast uses an include-filter limited to build-area parts, so placed objects are transparent to the ray. Overlap with placed items is handled separately by CheckValidity. searchDocs.title: QuestSourcesLoader
searchDocs.content: QuestSourcesLoader This item only works when running on the server. Server Gameplay progress sources for the quest system. Translates server-authoritative events into QuestManager progress calls: EnemyKills (Party): an EnemyNPC-tagged Humanoid dies. DistanceTravelled (Party): the train is in its "go" state, per tick. JunkCollected (Personal): a player finalizes a junk grab. BiomeJumps (Party): a jump arrives at its destination (not when it starts). Mirrors XPSystemLoader. searchDocs.title: ResearchEffectsDispatcher
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher This item only works when running on the server. Server On every Signals.OnResearchLevelUp, (1) marks the node unlocked in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked (BoolValue named by nodeId, at level >= 1), which the Workbench reads to ungrey recipes, and (2) recomputes leveled buffs from scratch into ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs. Recompute-from-levels (not delta accumulation) keeps totals correct with no drift.

searchDocs.title: ResearchService
searchDocs.content: ResearchService This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative owner of the shared, session-only Research Bench state. Handles ReqResearchEnqueue / ReqResearchCancel / ReqResearchRefuel / ReqResearchSnapshot, runs a Heartbeat tick that advances the active job and burns fuel, auto-starts the next queued job on completion (firing Signals.OnResearchLevelUp), refunds cancelled jobs via MaterialEjector, and broadcasts ResearchStateUpdate. Boot is split from definition (like PerkManager): require() this ModuleScript, then call Initialize() once — see ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau.

searchDocs.title: ResearchGuiController
searchDocs.content: ResearchGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Generates the Research Bench GUI entirely in code (no Studio template), opens it via the bench's ResearchPromptPart ProximityPrompt, and keeps a local state cache synced from ReqResearchSnapshot + ResearchStateUpdate. Node rows are grouped by Category (fixed order Train/Player/Equipment/ Recipes) and sorted by prereq depth then DisplayName; each row lets the player enqueue the next level. A queue panel shows the active job (with a MotionMaster-spring-driven progress bar) plus pending jobs, each cancellable. A fuel gauge shows bench fuel (also spring-driven) with a paused badge and a Refuel button. While a snapshot's authoritative values only change on ResearchStateUpdate broadcasts, interpolated() fast-forwards the active job's elapsed time and fuel locally between broadcasts using the known burn rate + synced server clock, so the bars move smoothly every frame.

searchDocs.title: prepareAssembly​
searchDocs.content: </> ServerProjectile.prepareAssembly( clone: Instance , root: BasePart , physics: PhysicalProperties ) → () Prepare a cloned throwable to fly as one rigid, falling body and land predictably: un-anchor every part (an assembly with ANY anchored part is immovable); keep the root massed (so gravity arcs it) while making cosmetic descendants massless; apply the low-elasticity / high-friction physics (small bounce, no slide); and weld every descendant to the root so a multi-part model flies + lands as one piece. For a single-part asset (the current grenade + C4) there are no descendants, so the weld and massless-child steps are inert.

searchDocs.title: spawnThrowable​
searchDocs.content: </> ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable( templateName: string, origin: Vector3 , direction: Vector3 , speed: number, rest: "Stick"landsdeadwithnobounceandplantswhereitsettles(C4);, ignore: instanceswhosedescendantsnevercountasalandingsurface ) → Instance?  Spawn a physics-driven, replicated throwable. Returns the cloned instance (BasePart or Model) or nil if the template is missing/invalid. Every throwable shares one arc — prepareAssembly + launch — and one mover (installSettle): arc, then plant flat once it has contacted a world surface and come to rest. The rest mode only sets bounciness: "Bounce" keeps one small hop before settling (grenade). Both arc, plant only at rest (never mid-flight), and pass through every character via the WeaponProjectile collision group. (e.g. the thrower's character; characters are skipped regardless).

searchDocs.title: spawnRocket​
searchDocs.content: </> ServerProjectile.spawnRocket( templateName: string, cframe: CFrame ) → BasePart?  Spawn an anchored, replicated rocket cosmetic at cframe. The caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the authoritative FastCast cast and destroys it on hit. CanQuery=false so the authoritative ray never hits the cosmetic itself.

searchDocs.title: ComputeHoldDuration​
searchDocs.content: </> ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration( junkCount: number,-- Number of junk items being shredded (≥ 1). config: HoldDurationConfig-- Duration and count thresholds (from Configs/ShredderConfig). ) → number-- Required hold duration in seconds. Linearly interpolates the required hold duration based on how many junk items the player is shredding. The duration scales from config.MIN_HOLD_DURATION (when junkCount = 1) to config.MAX_HOLD_DURATION (when junkCount >= config.MAX_JUNK_COUNT). junkCount is clamped to [1, MAX_JUNK_COUNT] before interpolation. When MAX_JUNK_COUNT is 1, MAX_HOLD_DURATION is returned immediately.

searchDocs.title: ShredderClient
searchDocs.content: ShredderClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client controller for workbench shredding interactions. Discovers placed workbenches via CollectionService tags, then wires each bench's ProximityPrompt to a nonce-guarded two-step handshake: PromptButtonHoldBegan fires ReqShredderStart to timestamp the session on the server, and the completed Triggered fires ReqShredderComplete only if the nonce is still valid. The prompt's HoldDuration is kept in sync with the player's current non-Energy junk count so the progress ring reflects the expected shred time. An info notification is shown (rate-limited) when the player attempts to shred with no eligible junk.

searchDocs.title: ShredderResultCodes
searchDocs.content: ShredderResultCodes Frozen enum-style table of integer result codes shared by ShredderServer and any client code that interprets shredder outcomes. The table is table.freezed — treat it as read-only at all times. Codes Name Value Meaning NONE 0 No result / default unset state. INVALID_WORKBENCH 1 The target workbench does not exist or is not a valid shredder. TOO_FAR 2 The player is too far from the workbench. WORKBENCH_BUSY 3 Another session is already active on this workbench. COOLDOWN 4 The workbench is on cooldown from a previous shred. NO_JUNK 5 The player has no junk items to shred. NO_SESSION 6 No active shredding session exists (hold-complete arrived with no matching session). SESSION_MISMATCH 7 The session token sent by the client does not match the server session. HOLD_TOO_SHORT 8 The player released the hold before the required duration elapsed. NO_MATERIAL_OUTPUT 9 The shred succeeded but produced no material (e.g. empty loot table).

searchDocs.title: Signals
searchDocs.content: Signals In-process client-side event bus. Provides typed Signal objects that any controller or service can fire and connect to without direct module coupling. All signals are created at module load time and shared as a single table — require this module and index the signal you need. The full per-signal list (what fires each signal, who listens, and the payload types) lives in the Reference → Signals map inDocumentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md. Register new signals there whenever you add one here.

searchDocs.title: ShredderServer
searchDocs.content: ShredderServer This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative server script that owns the Workbench Shredder flow for Endless Journey. On ReqShredderStart the server validates workbench proximity, per-player cooldown, and junk availability, then returns a hold duration computed by ShredderMath. On ReqShredderComplete it re-validates proximity and timing (anti-exploit: elapsed ≥ duration − tolerance), consumes all non-Energy junk Tools from the player's Backpack and equipped slot, computes the Wood/Metal yield via JunkConfig.MaterialRules, and spawns the outputs. Material output follows a two-path strategy: up to MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS pieces fly a MotionMaster.SplineMove arc from the workbench spawn point to a scatter-disk landing zone, where they register with ProximityPickupServer for nearby collection; overflow pieces are granted directly to the Backpack in yield-sized batches. An auto-collect loop reclaims any unclaimed arc pieces after AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY seconds so materials never pile up indefinitely.

searchDocs.title: GetRandomPoint​
searchDocs.content: </> SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() → Vector3? -- A random world-space position, or nil. Returns a uniformly random Vector3 point inside one of the enabled spawn volumes. Volume selection is weighted by world-space volume so larger parts are proportionally more likely to be chosen. Volumes in disabled groups are excluded. Returns nil if Init has not been called or no enabled volumes remain (e.g. every group is disabled).

searchDocs.content: </> SpawnHelper:Init() → () Scans workspace.SpawnVolumes and rebuilds the internal weighted cache from all BasePart children, reading each part's optional SpawnGroup attribute. searchDocs.title: CanHumanoidSprint​
searchDocs.content: </> SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint( humanoid: Humanoid ,-- The humanoid to evaluate. rules: Rules-- Threshold values that define valid sprint conditions. ) → boolean-- true if all sprint conditions are satisfied. Returns true when humanoid is in a state that permits sprinting under the given rules. Checks applied (all must pass): humanoid.Health > 0 — character is alive. humanoid.MoveDirection.Magnitude > rules.MinMoveDirection — character is actually moving. The local-space move direction's Z component is not greater than rules.MaxBackwardComponent — character is not moving backwards. The horizontal speed of RootPart.AssemblyLinearVelocity is at least rules.MinHorizontalSpeed — character has reached the minimum speed (prevents sprint activation while standing still due to input lag).

searchDocs.title: ThrowableHandler
searchDocs.content: ThrowableHandler This item only works when running on the client. Client Category handler for thrown weapons (grenade + C4). On activate it gates on the throw cooldown, plays the throw sound, and sends ReqThrowProjectile. The projectile instance is server-spawned and replicates to every client (no local cosmetic). Manual detonation (C4) is handled globally by ThrowableDetonateController, which sends ReqDetonate on G regardless of the equipped Tool. Damage + detonation are server-side.

searchDocs.title: TrainFuelGuiController
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the authored TrainFuelGui HUD without issuing any additional network packets. On every RenderStepped frame it extrapolates the current fuel level from the last Signals.OnTrainStateChanged snapshot using the drain rate and elapsed server time, then eases the displayed bar value toward that prediction with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing so refuel jumps animate smoothly. The fuel bar color reflects running, braked, or stalled state.

searchDocs.title: TrainClient
searchDocs.content: TrainClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client-side controller for train interaction. Discovers engine and brake lever instances via CollectionService tags and wires their ProximityPrompts: engine prompts send ReqRefuelTrain (with early-out notifications for missing energy items or a full tank), and lever prompts send ReqToggleBrake while keeping their ActionText in sync with the current brake state. Incoming TrainStateSync packets are bridged into Signals.OnTrainStateChanged so downstream controllers (e.g. TrainFuelGuiController) never touch the network layer directly.

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.Initialize() → () Initialises (or resets) all internal fuel state and wires up the server-side packet handlers for refuelling and brake toggling. Must be called exactly once by the owning server script before any client requests arrive. The function: Resets fuel to TrainConfig.INITIAL_FUEL and sets isBraked to TrainConfig.INITIAL_BRAKED. Binds Packets.ReqRefuelTrain.OnServerInvoke and Packets.ReqToggleBrake.OnServerInvoke. Connects Players.PlayerAdded to send the current snapshot to each new joiner so their HUD extrapolates immediately. Fires the initial TrainStateSync broadcast and schedules the first deterministic transition.

searchDocs.title: SetJumpFreeze​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.SetJumpFreeze(frozen: boolean) → () Suspends fuel drain and fuel damage for the duration of a jump. Both edges call commitEvent() so the algebraic model re-snapshots under the old rate before switching — without it, every client's extrapolated bar would keep draining straight through the transition. The not hasStarted or TrainGameOver.HasFired() guard applies ONLY to the freeze edge (frozen == true): it exists so a jump signal can't disturb the pre-game freeze or restart a settled game-over timer. It must NOT guard the unfreeze edge — do not "restore symmetry" by moving it above the if frozen check. If it did, isJumping could get set true by a freeze that then completes after game-over fires, and the corresponding unfreeze would be silently dropped, leaving isJumping stuck true forever. That's inert today (the round is dead and HasFired() independently blocks ApplyFuelDamage), but would silently zero fuel drain/damage after a future TrainGameOver.Reset()-based round restart. Unfreezing after game over is always safe: commitEvent() just recomputes the rate, which rateForState() still pins to 0 via isStalled, and onGameOver is idempotent.

searchDocs.title: ApplyFuelDamage​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage( amount: number, _source: any? ) → () Combat fuel-damage sink, called by TrainShieldManager once the shield is down. amount is fuel units already converted by TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR. If the hit leaves fuel above 0 it commits the new level (the natural stall timer simply shortens). Reducing fuel to 0 this way is an immediate game over (FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK) — no GAME_OVER_DELAY grace. No-op before the round is live or after game over has fired.

searchDocs.title: HasFired​

searchDocs.title: Trigger​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainGameOver.Trigger(reason: number?) → () Fires the game-over sequence once, recording reason (a TrainGameOverReason code, default NONE) and broadcasting it via Signals.OnTrainGameOver. Subsequent calls are no-ops, so the first recorded reason wins.

searchDocs.title: TrainShieldController
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldController This item only works when running on the client. Client Discovers shield-console instances via CollectionService tags and wires their ProximityPrompt to send ReqRechargeShield (mirroring TrainClient's refuel prompt, including the "hold with no energy" early-out). On a successful recharge it plays a SoundManager SFX. Incoming TrainShieldSync packets are bridged into Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged so the HUD controller never touches the network layer directly.

searchDocs.title: TrainShieldGuiController
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the diegetic TrainShieldGui SurfaceGui on each tagged TrainShieldMonitor part. Discovers monitors via CollectionService, clones the GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui template onto each (client-locally, so every player drives an independent copy on the shared surface), and updates two readouts on its CRT face each frame: the train shield (Online/Critical, eased toward Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged snapshots) and the train fuel reserve (extrapolated from Signals.OnTrainStateChanged, mirroring the on-screen fuel HUD). Each monitor owns a Janitor that destroys its clone and disconnects its render loop when the tag is removed.

searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.GetShield() → ( number, number ) Returns (currentShield, maxShield).

searchDocs.title: SetJumpFreeze​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.SetJumpFreeze(frozen: boolean) → () Suspends shield damage for the duration of a jump. The shield has no continuous drain, so unlike the fuel freeze there is nothing to re-snapshot.

searchDocs.title: ApplyDamage​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage( amount: number, source: any? ) → () The single damage sink — future enemy AI / hazards call this. While the shield holds, it absorbs the hit and clamps at 0; the hit that empties the shield discards its excess (no fuel damage that hit). Once the shield is already at 0, further hits convert to fuel damage viaTrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR and route to TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage, which may end the round. No-op before the round is live or after game over.

searchDocs.content: </> TrajectoryPreview.hide() → () Stop showing the arc and destroy the whole pool. Safe to call when nothing is showing.

searchDocs.title: WeaponConfig
searchDocs.content: WeaponConfig Central tuning registry for every weapon, keyed by weapon name (which must equal the in-game Tool's Name). Edit stats here, never in handler/server code. Covers melee, gun, and throwable (grenade + C4) entries.

searchDocs.title: WeaponController
searchDocs.content: WeaponController This item only works when running on the client. Client Bootstrap that drives every equipped weapon. Watches the local character for Tool equip (Tool parented to character) / unequip (removed), looks up the Tool's WeaponConfig entry by name, and dispatches to the category handler. Connects Tool.Activated to the handler's OnActivate. One Janitor per equipped Tool; one per character. Fires Signals.WeaponEquipped/Unequipped for the HUD, and drives the aim/shooting camera via Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip (same intent as GrabHook).

searchDocs.title: WeaponDebug
searchDocs.content: WeaponDebug Hitbox/volume visualizer for tuning weapons, required by every weapon handler. Flip the single ENABLED flag below and save — Rojo syncs it in. No command bar, no attributes. When on, every weapon swing/shot draws a bright Neon box matching the exact query volume (green = the attack found a target, red = it whiffed) that auto-removes after LIFETIME seconds, and prints a line to the console so you can confirm the code path ran even if the part is off-screen. Reused by later plans for gun rays / AOE spheres.

searchDocs.title: WeaponEffectsController
searchDocs.content: WeaponEffectsController This item only works when running on the client. Client Receives replicated combat-FX packets and renders them for the local player: tracers for OTHER players' shots (WeaponFired), and impact FX/sound for all melee/gun hits (WeaponImpact). The shooter draws its own tracer locally in GunHandler, so WeaponFired is ignored for the local player to avoid doubles.

searchDocs.title: WeaponFx
searchDocs.content: WeaponFx Shared resolver mapping a weapon name to its client FX sound keys. Player weapons live in WeaponConfig; enemy weapons live in EnemyCombatConfig. The client FX controller uses this so a single packet path (WeaponFired / WeaponImpact / ExplosionAt) renders BOTH player and enemy weapon names. Returns a table with optional keys; callers nil-check before playing sound.

searchDocs.title: WeaponServer
searchDocs.content: WeaponServer This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative weapon server. Plan 1 handles ReqMeleeSwing: it infers the weapon from the requester's equipped Tool, gates the swing on the server-side cooldown (WeaponState), re-runs the melee hitbox from the server's character CFrame, and routes damage through CombatService. Broadcasts WeaponImpact per hit so all clients render impact FX. Never trusts client aim or client-claimed hits. Plan 2 adds authoritative hitscan fire (ReqFireWeapon), authoritative reload (ReqReloadWeapon), and ammo initialisation on gun equip (WeaponMagSync pushed to the owning client immediately; the shared ammo pool is owned by AmmoManager and synced via AmmoPoolSync). Plan 3 adds server-side rocket (projectile) cast via FastCast2. Throwable weapons (grenade fuse + C4 manual) are handled via ReqThrowProjectile and ReqDetonate.

searchDocs.title: WeaponState
searchDocs.content: WeaponState This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative per-player weapon state. Plan 1 tracks last-fire timestamps per weapon name for server-side fire-rate gating. Later plans extend the record with ammo ({ mag }) and reload timing. Call WeaponState.Initialize() once from a server bootstrap to clear state on player leave.

searchDocs.title: WeaponTypes
searchDocs.content: WeaponTypes Shared type definitions for the weapon system. Runtime value is an empty table; consumers use the exported types. Melee weapons are combo-driven: aMeleeWeaponConfig carries weapon-level defaults plus a Combos map keyed by input (Primary = LC; Secondary reserved for future RC). Throwables (grenade, C4) carry Detonation/Rest discriminators distinguishing fuse-timed bouncers from manually-detonated stickies.

searchDocs.title: WeaponValidation
searchDocs.content: WeaponValidation Pure-ish shared helpers run on BOTH client (prediction) and server (authority) so the two agree. Holds the fire-rate gate, the melee hitbox query, and part→Humanoid-model resolution. No networking; the only world access is the deterministic spatial query in queryMeleeTargets.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchGuiController
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the Studio-authored WorkbenchGui. Opens via a placed Workbench station's CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt (CollectionService tag Workbench, shared with the Shredder on the same station Model), builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig, fills the detail pane on selection, sends ReqCraft on Accept, and wires Stash/Move via PlaceableActions. Greys recipes the player can't afford or that are gated by a locked Tech node; repaints live on Backpack and Tech-unlock changes. The recipe grid is filtered by category; the DropdownButton (driven by the reusable SharedModules/Gui/Dropdown widget) selects the category and fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory. The CloseButton calls close().

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchConfig
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchConfig Single tuning surface for the Workbench crafting station: interaction constants, output template folders, and the recipe table. Edit gameplay here, never in service/controller code. The GUI is fixed to two material rows (Wood/Metal), so recipe Cost is limited to those two materials. Studio setup required: Tag the ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench Model with CollectionService tag Workbench (shared with the Shredder, which lives on the same station); give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model) holding a ProximityPrompt, and set its PrimaryPart. Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates holding craftable weapon Tools (e.g. clones of Pistol, SMG) — separate from StarterPack. Each craftable placeable needs its ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> Tool. Wood/Metal reuse ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchResultCodes
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchResultCodes Frozen reason-code enum returned by ReqCraft and produced by WorkbenchValidation. Shared by client and server so string literals never appear in business logic; the client maps codes to notification messages.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchService
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchService This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative handler for ReqCraft. Validates (recipe membership, target is a tagged Workbench station, proximity, per-player cooldown, Tech Tree gate, output feasibility, then materials), consumes Wood/Metal Tools from the crafter's backpack, and dispatches the recipe output via CraftOutputDispatcher. Any failure returns a reason code and consumes nothing. Client input is never trusted: proximity and gate are re-checked from server-owned state.

searchDocs.title: XPController
searchDocs.content: XPController This item only works when running on the client. Client Bridges XP replication into the client. On XPStateSync it re-fires Signals.OnXPChanged (reserved for a future XP HUD bar). On XPLevelUp it raises a level-up toast via the existing NotificationManager (through Signals.RequestNotification). Runs in both the lobby and gameplay places.

searchDocs.content: XPCurve Pure functions deriving level and progress from a single cumulativetotalXP value. Cumulative thresholds are precomputed once at require time from XPConfig. Used server-side by XPManager; safe to require anywhere.

searchDocs.title: AddXP​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.AddXP( player: Player , amount: number ) → () Award amount XP to a single player. No-op if amount <= 0 or the player's profile is not loaded. Fires XPLevelUp when the level increases, then replicates the new snapshot.

searchDocs.title: AddPartyXP​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number) → () Award amount XP to every player in the server with a loaded profile. XP is party-shared and one party occupies one server, so this is the primary award path for both kills and distance.

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.Initialize() → () Wire up the profile lifecycle. Call exactly once per server (from a loader).

searchDocs.title: GetLevel​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.GetLevel(player: Player ) → number Current level for player, derived from stored TotalXP. Returns 1 if the profile is not loaded (safe default for point derivation).

searchDocs.title: XPSystemLoader
searchDocs.content: XPSystemLoader This item only works when running on the server. Server Gameplay-place entry point for the XP system. Initializes XPManager (profile lifecycle + replication), then wires the two earning sources: Distance: while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), award XPConfig.DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK to the whole party every XPConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS. Go-state is read from Signals.SetTrainState (the train starts braked, so no XP accrues pre-start). Kills: award XPConfig.KILL_XP to the whole party whenever an EnemyNPC-tagged model's Humanoid dies (attribution-agnostic — shared XP). Do NOT run this in the lobby place; the lobby runs XPManager.Initialize only (for display + session handoff), without earners.

searchDocs.title: Client Predicts / Server Authoritative​
searchDocs.content: All gameplay systems in Endless Journey follow a single authority model: the client predicts the outcome of player actions to keep the experience responsive, while the server is the source of truth and rejects or corrects any result that fails validation.  The key structural tool is a shared validator module — a module in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ that runs the same logic on both sides. The client uses it during prediction so its local view stays consistent with what the server will accept. The server uses it during validation before committing any state change. When changing a rule, you must edit the shared module so both sides agree; changing only the client or only the server creates a mismatch.  When touching any system that follows this pattern, change the client controller, the server module, and the shared module together. Protocol changes go through Packets.

searchDocs.title: Placement​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityShared validator	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlacementSystem.luau	Grid snapping, free-placement math, collision helpers Client	PlacementClient.client.luau	Runs PlacementSystem locally to render the placement preview Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau	Re-runs PlacementSystem + additional anti-exploit checks before finalizing  PlacementServer adds server-only anti-exploit layers on top of PlacementSystem: origin distance check, raycast re-validation, and a per-player cooldown. These thresholds are sensitive — see the caution below.

searchDocs.title: Stamina / Sprint​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityShared helpers	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau	Validation predicates shared by both sides Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau	Predicts drain/regen and drives FOV locally Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau	Authoritative stamina value; syncs to all clients at 10 Hz via StaminaStateSync packet  The high sync rate (10 Hz) keeps the client HUD and sprint-gating responsive without giving the client write access to the stamina value. Sprint logic changes must be mirrored on both SprintController and StaminaManager.

searchDocs.title: Junk​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityClient	JunkController.client.luau	Renders junk movement, visuals, and rope effects using pooled instances Pooling	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/GenericPoolInstance.luau / GenericPoolObject.luau	Instance pooling for client-side rendering Server	JunkService	Spawns weighted junk items; validates all collection requests  The client never spawns junk — it only renders what the server tells it exists. Collection is validated server-side before any inventory change occurs.

searchDocs.title: Grabhook​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityClient	src/StarterPack/Grabhook/ tool script	Drives the raycast, rope visuals, and swing physics locally Server	Server script	Receives the collection request, validates proximity and legality, then awards the item  The client's visual result is speculative. The server is the only side that awards currency or items.

searchDocs.title: Shredder​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityShared math	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderMath.luau	Computes dynamic hold duration from junk inputs Shared result codes	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderResultCodes.luau	Enum of result codes used by both client and server Client	ShredderClient.client.luau	Attaches ProximityPrompts to workbenches; drives the two-step handshake (start → complete) Server	src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau	Validates proximity, timing, junk availability, and anti-exploit; consumes junk; ejects material Tools with bezier arc animation; auto-collects unclaimed drops after 45 s  Both ShredderClient and ShredderServer call ShredderMath with the same inputs, so the displayed hold-duration progress bar matches the server's acceptance window.    Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive The server-side anti-exploit checks in PlacementServer (origin distance, place distance, cooldown) and ShredderServer (INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN) are tuned against real network latency. Tightening them without testing under realistic ping conditions will cause legitimate actions to be rejected. Loosening them creates exploitable windows. Always test against real latency before shipping threshold changes.

searchDocs.title: Signals​
searchDocs.content: What. An in-process event bus that decouples controllers and services from each other without direct require chains. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau.  Why. Direct module coupling creates a tangle of dependencies and makes load order fragile. Signals let a controller fire a named event (Signals.RequestShootingCamera) without knowing which other controllers are listening. This is the preferred pattern for gameplay events and UI intents.  How to use. require the module, then fire or connect named events. Signals are client-only and in-process — they do not cross the network. For cross-boundary traffic, use Packets.  See the full event catalogue in Signals Map.

searchDocs.title: Packets​
searchDocs.content: What. Typed network packet definitions. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau.  Why. Raw RemoteEvent / RemoteFunction usage scatters network contracts across the codebase, making it impossible to audit traffic or catch type errors. Packets centralises every channel in one place with defined types.  How to use. All client↔server traffic must go through Packets — never create ad-hoc RemoteEvent instances. When adding a new network channel, register it in Packets/init.luau and update the Networking Map in the Maintenance Guide.

searchDocs.title: Configs​
searchDocs.content: What. A directory of tuning tables at src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/. Modules cover: Placement, Junk, Stamina, GrabHook, ShiftLock, Health, Shredder, JunkTool, Sound, and Notification.  Why. Keeping tunable values in config modules separates design decisions from code logic, makes auditing changes straightforward, and avoids touching behaviour code for what are purely numerical adjustments.  How to use. Prefer config changes over code changes when tuning gameplay numbers. require the relevant config module; do not hard-code magic numbers in controllers or server scripts. See the Config Map for the full list of tunables per module.

searchDocs.title: SoundManager​
searchDocs.content: What. The single entry point for all client-side audio — SFX, BGM, ambience, and looped sound beds. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/init.luau.  Why. Ad-hoc Sound instance creation leads to untracked audio, duplicate playback, and no central volume control. SoundManager owns all audio state.  How to use. require the module and call PlaySFX, PlaySFXAt, PlayLooped, PlayMusic, SetAmbience, or SetVolume. Never create Sound instances directly. Asset IDs, volumes, pitch ranges, playlists, and ambience beds all live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau. The client bootstrap script (SoundController.client.luau) calls SoundManager.Init() once on startup.  For a full guide see Sound System.

searchDocs.title: NotificationManager​
searchDocs.content: What. A signal-driven toast notification system. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/NotificationManager/init.luau.  Why. Centralising toast creation prevents duplicated UI code in every system that needs to surface feedback to the player (e.g., refuel errors on the train, collection results, stamina warnings).  How to use. Fire the relevant Signal to request a notification; NotificationController.client.luau listens and delegates to NotificationManager for rendering. Do not construct toast UI frames directly in other controllers.  For a full guide see Notification System.

searchDocs.title: Janitor​
searchDocs.content: What. The project's cleanup primitive, provided by the howmanysmall/janitor Wally package at Packages/Janitor.  Why. Hand-rolled { RBXScriptConnection } arrays and manual disconnect loops are error-prone, easy to forget, and hard to audit. Janitor provides a single, consistent cleanup API for any scope that owns connections or instances.  How to use. Create one Janitor per lifecycle scope. Add connections, instances, and callbacks with :Add. Call :Cleanup to disconnect and destroy everything when the scope ends (e.g., on character removal or session teardown). For keyed collections, store one Janitor per entry under entry.cleaner. Call :Destroy only when the Janitor object itself will not be reused — :Cleanup preserves the Janitor for reuse.  See Janitor Patterns for Cleanup vs Destroy guidance and common lifecycle recipes.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster​
searchDocs.content: What. The project's animation library. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/MotionMaster.luau.  Why. TweenService does not support springs, splines, or composable sequences, and scatters animation logic across controllers. MotionMaster provides a unified, expressive API for all client-side motion.  How to use. Do not use TweenService for client-side animations — use MotionMaster instead.  Key entry points:  -- Fire-and-forget tween MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad" }) -- Manual lifecycle control local tween = MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "Spring" }) tween:Play() -- Spring driven by a named preset MotionMaster.fromPreset("UIPanel", target, "Position") -- Chained sequence MotionMaster.Sequence({ tweenA, tweenB }) -- Catmull-Rom spline movement MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, { Duration = 2 }) -- Model pivot animation MotionMaster.PivotMove(model, targetCFrame, { Duration = 0.4, Model = "EaseInOutQuad" })   Key config fields: Duration, Model (easing name), TimeWarp, Delay, Repeat, RepeatDelay, From. Sixteen named spring presets are available under MotionMaster.Presets (e.g., "UIPanel", "CameraFollow", "DoorBouncy").  For the full API reference and preset list see MotionMaster Cheatsheet.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: Client code lives under src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ (controllers, *.client.luau) and src/StarterPack/Grabhook/ (tool scripts). Controllers own local prediction, UI, camera, and visual rendering. They never write game state directly — they send Packet requests and react to Packet syncs or Signal events.  Notable scripts:  Script	ResponsibilityBuildModeGuiController.client.luau	Build-mode HUD and input PlacementClient.client.luau	Placement preview and request dispatch HealthStaminaGuiController.client.luau	Health and stamina bar rendering SprintController.client.luau	Predictive stamina drain/regen and FOV CameraController.client.luau	Third-person, aim, and free-look camera modes; mouse-look sensitivity, scroll zoom, and occlusion SoundController.client.luau	Bootstraps SoundManager.Init() JunkController.client.luau	Pooled junk visual rendering and rope effects TeleportToSpawn.client.luau	Spawn teleportation ShredderClient.client.luau	ProximityPrompts and two-step shredder handshake HealthController.client.luau	Forwards HealthStateSync to HUD MobileGeneralGuiController.client.luau	Mobile-specific UI NotificationController.client.luau	Toast notification rendering StarterPack/Grabhook/	Grabhook tool — client raycast and visuals WeaponController.client.luau	Weapon equip/fire input and client-side prediction AmmoHudController.client.luau	Ammo HUD rendering XPController.client.luau / CoinController.client.luau	XP/level and coin balance HUD QuestController.client.luau / BattlePassController.client.luau / PerkController.client.luau	Read-models for quest, battle pass, and perk GUIs SettingsController.client.luau	User preference UI and apply SessionClient.client.luau	Party lock / mid-run rejoin client hooks

searchDocs.title: Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared code lives under src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ and is require-able from both the client and the server. This layer contains the cross-cutting backbone modules, typed packet definitions, config tables, pooling utilities, and shared validators used by both sides of the authority pattern.  Notable modules:  Signals/init.luau — in-process event busPackets/init.luau — typed network packet registryConfigs/ — all gameplay tuning tablesPlacementSystem.luau — shared placement validation logicSprintValidation.luau — shared sprint validation helpersCameraRig.luau — stateless camera CFrame compositionShredderMath.luau — shared hold-duration computationShredderResultCodes.luau — shared result-code enumSoundManager/init.luau — unified audio APINotificationManager/init.luau — signal-driven toast systemMotionMaster.luau — animation library (replaces TweenService)GenericPoolInstance.luau / GenericPoolObject.luau — instance poolingWeaponValidation.luau / WeaponTypes.luau — shared weapon fire validation and type definitionsFactions.luau — faction/team identity helpers used by combatQuestState.luau — shared quest period/bucket mathBattlePassState.luau — shared season/tier mathPerkState.luau — shared perk point/level mathXPCurve.luau — shared level curve derivation

searchDocs.title: Server​
searchDocs.content: Server authority modules live under src/ServerScriptService/ (entry-point scripts) and src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ (authority modules required by server scripts). The server validates every state-changing request, owns the source of truth, and syncs relevant state back to clients via Packets.  Notable scripts and modules:  Script / Module	ResponsibilityPlacementServer.server.luau	Placement validation, anti-exploit, finalization JunkService	Junk spawn authority and collection validation StaminaManager.luau	Stamina source of truth; syncs at 10 Hz StaminaBuffManager.luau	Stamina buff application ShredderServer.server.luau	Shredder validation, junk consumption, material ejection HealthManager.luau	Health regen and HealthStateSync ReplicatedSoundService	Sound replication relay WeaponServer.server.luau	Weapon fire validation and damage authority CombatService.luau	Shared damage routing (melee/hitscan/projectile/AOE) EnemyCombatSystemLoader.server.luau / EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau	Enemy AI and spawner bootstrap XPSystemLoader.server.luau / CoinSystemLoader.server.luau	XP and coin authority bootstrap QuestSystemLoader.server.luau / BattlePassSystemLoader.server.luau	Quest and battle pass authority bootstrap PerkSystemLoader.server.luau / ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau	Perk and research authority bootstrap SessionSystemLoader.server.luau	Party lock + mid-run rejoin bootstrap (SessionCoordinator, SessionStore) SettingsSystemLoader.server.luau	User-preferences authority bootstrap (SettingsManager)

searchDocs.title: Where Content Lives​
searchDocs.content: There are two sources of documentation:  Narrative pages (docs/) — the files you are reading now. Written by hand in Markdown and checked into this repository. Covers architecture, playbooks, getting-started guides, and everything that isn't a raw API reference.API reference — generated automatically by Moonwave from doc-comments (--[=[...]=] blocks) in the Luau source under src/. Moonwave extracts these at build time; no separate documentation file is needed for module APIs.

searchDocs.title: Local Preview​
searchDocs.content: Install Moonwave globally once:  npm i -g moonwave@latest   Then, from the repo root:  Command	Effectmoonwave dev	Starts a live-reload local server. Edit any docs/ page or source doc-comment and the browser updates instantly. moonwave build	Produces a static output in build/ for inspection. The CI pipeline runs this automatically — you rarely need it locally.

searchDocs.title: Publishing​
searchDocs.content: Pushing to main triggers a GitHub Action that:  Runs moonwave build.Pushes the static output to the separate endless-journey-docs repository.GitHub Pages serves the result from that repo.  You do not need to run the build or push to endless-journey-docs manually.

searchDocs.title: The Discipline Rule​
searchDocs.content: When a code change touches a system, the same commit must also update:  That system's narrative page under docs/.Any affected playbook in docs/playbooks/.The networking map or signals map if a new packet or signal was added.  This extends the project's existing "record any new signal/packet" rule (see old guide § Recommended Update Process) to cover the Moonwave site. Keeping documentation and code in the same commit makes it easy to find the change context later and prevents the docs from silently drifting out of date.  tip If the change is large (e.g. a new system), write the narrative page first as a draft, then implement the code, then finalize both in the closing commit. This forces you to articulate the design before you are buried in implementation details.

searchDocs.title: System page template​
searchDocs.content: Every page under docs/systems/ follows this H2 skeleton, in this order:  # <System Name> <1 short paragraph: what it does, why it exists, authority model.> ## At a glance | Layer | File | Role | |---|---|---| | Client | `src/...` | ... | | Server | `src/...` | ... | | Shared | `src/...` | ... | | Config | `src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/...` | ... | **Packets:** `PacketA`, `PacketB` — see [Networking Map](../reference/networking-map.md) **Signals:** `SignalA` — see [Signals Map](../reference/signals-map.md) ## How it works ### <one H3 per mechanism> <paragraphs ≤ 4 sentences; show code for any call/shape being described> ## Data flow <Mermaid sequenceDiagram> ## Tuning <Config module link + relevant playbook links, bullet list> ## API <Bullets linking Moonwave classes, e.g. [`QuestManager`](/api/QuestManager)>   Prose rules: paragraphs ≤ 4 sentences; enumerable facts in tables; anything invocable as code; bold sparingly; relative links between doc pages (../systems/foo.md style, matching existing pages); Mermaid over ASCII for any diagram.

searchDocs.content: Every page under docs/playbooks/ follows this skeleton:  # <Task Name> **Goal:** <one sentence> ## Steps 1. <one action per step; exact file paths; code blocks for edits> ## Verify <How to confirm the change works in Studio.> ## Related - <system page link> - <API class links>

searchDocs.title: Adding a page or class (checklist)​
searchDocs.content: New doc page → add its id to .moonwave/sidebars.js in the right family (pages not listed there do not appear).New @class in source → add it to the fitting [[classOrder]] section in moonwave.toml in the same commit (unlisted classes sink to an unsorted lump; a typo fails the build).Adding a packet or signal → update docs/reference/networking-map.md / signals-map.md in the same commit.Run moonwave build before pushing docs changes.

searchDocs.title: Initial Setup​
searchDocs.content: After cloning the repo, run this once:  rokit install   This installs the pinned versions of Rojo, Wally, wally-package-types, and selene into your local toolchain.

searchDocs.title: Common Commands​
searchDocs.content: Command	Purposerojo serve	Start the live-sync server for Studio editing. rojo build -o "Game Instance.rbxlx"	Emit a static place file from src/. rojo sourcemap default.project.json -o sourcemap.json --include-non-scripts	Regenerate the sourcemap used by Luau LSP. Re-run after adding or moving files. wally install	Fetch Wally dependencies into Packages/ (shared) and ServerPackages/ (server). wally-package-types --sourcemap sourcemap.json Packages/	Regenerate type exports for Wally packages. Run after every wally install so Luau type-checking sees package types. selene src	Lint Luau source against the Roblox standard library (std = "roblox", config in selene.toml).

searchDocs.title: After wally install — Manual Studio Step Required​
searchDocs.content: TweenPlus TweenPreallocations After every wally install, you must manually re-set the TweenPreallocations attribute in Studio — or TweenPlus will crash on load. wally install deletes and regenerates the entire Packages/ directory. The TweenPlus package (Packages/_Index/alexanderlindholt_tweenplus@<ver>/tweenplus) reads a TweenPreallocations number attribute from its own script instance at require-time with no nil fallback (table.create(script.Parent:GetAttribute("TweenPreallocations"))). When the attribute is absent the package throws: invalid argument #1 to 'create' (number expected, got nil) This error cascades: TweenPlus → PlacementSystem → SprintController → every consumer fails to load. Steps to fix after wally install: Open Studio with rojo serve running.In the Explorer, navigate to:ReplicatedStorage → Packages → _Index → alexanderlindholt_tweenplus@<ver> → tweenplusIn the Properties panel, add an attribute: Name: TweenPreallocationsType: numberValue: 256 Save the place file. The attribute persists until the next wally install.  A default.project.json $properties override cannot be used here: in live Rojo sync, Rojo recreates the path-synced instance instead of patching it, so the attribute would be wiped on every sync cycle.

searchDocs.title: No Automated Tests​
searchDocs.content: note There is no automated test suite. All verification happens by playtesting in Studio. See the How-To Playbooks for the manual smoke-test steps specific to each system.

searchDocs.title: Core Loop​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesPlacement	Grid and free-placement of world objects; client previews, server validates. Placeable Actions	Stash returns a placed item to the Backpack, Move re-equips it; both server-validated. Junk	Server spawns weighted floating debris; client renders pooled visuals and simulates movement locally. Grabhook	Tool-driven traversal; client drives raycast and rope visuals, server validates the claim and awards it. Proximity Pickup	Dropped craft materials and shredder-ejected items auto-register for proximity claim or delayed auto-collect. Shredder	Two-step server handshake converting non-Energy junk into crafting materials at a Workbench. Workbench Crafting	Server-authoritative, instant crafting of weapons/armor/placeables from config-defined recipes. Research Bench	Server-wide, session-only research: enqueue, advance, complete, refuel, and cancel jobs gated by shared fuel.

searchDocs.title: Train​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesTrain Fuel	Single global fuel value computed algebraically by the server; clients predict the bar locally. Train Shield	Global, event-driven shield pool depleted by damage and restored with Energy tools. Cannon	Grid-placeable, manned cannon firing server-authoritative explosive arc shells. Events Orchestrator	Server-authoritative scheduler deciding when and which in-game events fire per channel. Disruption / Maintenance	Notifies players, force-saves progress, and teleports to the lobby on shutdown or maintenance.

searchDocs.title: Combat​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesWeapons	Client-predicted / server-authoritative combat with a shared validator; all damage applies server-side. Enemy Combat	A centralized AI director ticks every armed enemy, reusing the player weapon and damage stack. Enemy Spawner	Generic server-authoritative spawner selecting weighted spawn points and validating placement. Health	The server is the single source of truth for health; it drives regen and syncs the client HUD. Damage Numbers	Client-only, render-only floating world-space damage numbers; never computes or applies damage.

searchDocs.title: Player​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesStamina & Sprint	Client-predicted, server-authoritative stamina simulation synced at up to 10 Hz. Camera	A fully script-owned third-person camera computing Camera.CFrame every frame. Settings	Generic server-authoritative user-preferences registry for audio volumes and sensitivity.

searchDocs.title: Progression & Economy​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesProgression (XP & Level)	Server-authoritative, party-shared XP & Level system persisted with ProfileStore. Economy (Coins)	Server-authoritative coin wallet persisted with ProfileStore, shared across lobby and gameplay places. Quests	Rotating ProfileStore-backed quest system with four buckets plus a Season scope feeding the Battle Pass. Battle Pass	Monthly ProfileStore-backed 60-tier track with Free and Premium reward rows. Perks	Level-driven permanent progression spending Personal/Party points on persistent buffs.

searchDocs.title: Platform​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesSound	A layered client audio system; all game audio flows through the SoundManager facade. Notifications	A signal-driven client toast stack; NotificationManager is the sole subscriber. Party Lock + Mid-Run Rejoin	Server-enforced party lock and mid-run rejoin guarantees for a live run.

searchDocs.title: Design philosophy​
searchDocs.content: Every gameplay system follows a client predicts / server authoritative pattern with a shared validator. The client runs local prediction (placement preview, stamina drain, fuel bar interpolation) so interaction feels instant, while the server re-validates every request and broadcasts the authoritative result. Protocol changes must go through src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau; cross-module events go through src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau. When in doubt, the server wins.

searchDocs.title: How to read these docs​
searchDocs.content: Getting Started — install the toolchain, run a build, and understand the one manual step that trips everyone up (TweenPreallocations).Architecture — runtime layers, cross-cutting modules, and the authority pattern.Systems — one page per system, grouped by family (Core Loop, Train, Combat, Player, Progression & Economy, Platform); the API sidebar sections mirror these same families.How-To Playbooks — step-by-step safe-change guides, grouped the same way (plus a Backbone group for packets/signals).Reference — the networking / signals / config maps, Janitor and MotionMaster cheat-sheets, plus the Moonwave-generated API docs for every annotated module.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Choose a notification type. The canonical types are defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau: "success" | "info" | "warn" | "alert" | "default" Each type has a pre-configured background color (NotificationConfig.Colors), icon image (NotificationConfig.ImageIds), and stinger SFX (NotificationConfig.SfxNames). If an existing type fits, skip to step 3. (Optional) Add a new type. If none of the five built-in types fit, extend NotificationConfig (file: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau) by adding the new lowercase key to every relevant table: -- 1. Register the type name NotificationConfig.Types = { "success", "info", "warn", "alert", "default", "mytype" } -- 2. Background color NotificationConfig.Colors.mytype = Color3.fromRGB(80, 40, 120) -- 3. Background transparency (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) NotificationConfig.BaseTransparency.mytype = 0.5 -- 4. Icon asset ID NotificationConfig.ImageIds.mytype = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" -- 5. SFX stinger — must match a key in SoundConfig.Sfx NotificationConfig.SfxNames.mytype = "NotifDefault" If you add a custom stinger, first register it in SoundConfig.Sfx (see Add a Sound). Fire the signal from any client controller. local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) -- Basic timed toast (disappears after the default duration): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("success", "Item placed!") -- Custom duration (seconds): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("warn", "Low fuel!", 5) -- Executed-function toast (stays until the function returns, then closes): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("info", "Loading...", nil, function() -- async work here; toast closes when this returns task.wait(2) end) -- Dismiss all active toasts: Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() Signal signature (from src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau): RequestNotification : Signal<string, string, number?, (() -> ())?> arg1 notificationType (lowercase, must be in NotificationConfig.Types) arg2 message (display text, wraps automatically) arg3 duration? (seconds; nil = config default per device) arg4 executedFunction? (if provided, toast stays until function returns) The stack allows up to NotificationConfig.MaxConcurrent (default 5) concurrent toasts. When the cap is exceeded the oldest non-executed toast is automatically closed.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio (client context).Trigger the code path that fires Signals.RequestNotification.Confirm the toast appears at the top of the screen, plays its stinger, and auto-dismisses after the expected duration.If the toast does not appear: confirm the type string is lowercase and present in NotificationConfig.Types; confirm NotificationController.client.luau has run NotificationManager.Init().
