searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Author the model in Studio.Open Studio and build or import the item as a Model. Give it a clear, unique name (e.g. WoodenCrate). This name is the canonical identifier shared between the storage folder and the PlaceableName attribute. Place the model in the placeable-items storage folder.Move (or keep) the model inside the storage location that PlacementServer scans at startup. Verify src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau for the exact FindFirstChild / WaitForChild call that resolves the folder name, and make sure your model lands there. Add a CollisionBox part.Inside the model, create a BasePart named CollisionBox. Size and position it to represent the footprint used for overlap/validity checks. Set Anchored = true, CanCollide = false, and make it invisible (Transparency = 1). PlacementSystem reads this part to decide valid placement. Set the PlaceableName attribute on the Tool.On the Tool instance that players use to enter placement mode, open Properties → Attributes and add a string attribute named PlaceableName with the value matching the model name from step 1 (e.g. WoodenCrate). PlacementServer reads this attribute at line 205 and PlacementClient at line 253. Configure ghost appearance (optional).Ghost transparency and color cues come from src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau: VisualGhostTransparency -- opacity of the main model parts during preview CollisionBoxGhostTransparency -- opacity of CollisionBox while ghosting ColorValid / ColorInvalid -- tint applied to the ghost ShowCollisionBox -- set true temporarily to debug footprint alignment Test grid mode and free mode.In a live Studio session (Rojo serving), equip the tool, open build mode, and place the item in both grid-snapped and free-rotation modes. Confirm the ghost tracks the cursor correctly and snaps as expected. Validate multiplayer ghost behavior.Run a local server with at least two clients. Confirm that observers see the ghost rendered correctly (via the replication path in PlacementClient) and that the server accepts the final placement without a distance/raycast rejection from PlacementServer. If you also need Stash / Move support, see Enable Stash & Move for the additional attribute and server wiring.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Equip the new Tool, enter build mode, and place the item. Check the Output window for any PlacementServer rejection messages. Then have a second client observe: the placed item should appear at the confirmed position with no ghost artifact remaining.

searchDocs.title: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
Steps​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Open Packets/init.luau. File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau. Browse the existing definitions to understand the declaration style before adding yours. Declare the packet. Add it in the appropriate section (or create a new labelled section). Match the style of existing entries: a local variable, a direction comment, and field-level type annotations. Simple payload (no response): -- Client → Server: description of what this carries local MyPacket = Packet( "MyPacket", Packet.String, -- fieldOne Packet.NumberF32, -- fieldTwo Packet.Boolean8 -- fieldThree ) Request/response pattern: -- Client → Server: description local ReqMyAction = Packet( "ReqMyAction", Packet.Instance -- target ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code ) Server → Client broadcast: -- Server → All Clients: description local BroadcastMyEvent = Packet( "BroadcastMyEvent", Packet.Instance :: Player, -- the relevant player Packet.Vector3F32 -- position ) Available type tokens: Packet.String, Packet.Boolean8, Packet.NumberF32, Packet.NumberF64, Packet.NumberU8, Packet.NumberU16, Packet.NumberF16, Packet.Instance, Packet.Vector3F32, Packet.CFrameF32U16, Packet.Any. For high-frequency unreliable streams (e.g., per-frame position updates) use the makeUnreliable helper already present in the file. Export the packet. Add it to the return table at the bottom of init.luau: return { -- ... existing entries ... MyPacket = MyPacket, ReqMyAction = ReqMyAction, BroadcastMyEvent = BroadcastMyEvent, } Wire the sender. On the client (fires to server): local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Packets) -- Fire and forget: Packets.MyPacket:Fire(valueOne, valueTwo, valueThree) -- Request/response: local success, reasonCode = Packets.ReqMyAction:Fire(targetInstance) On the server (fires to clients): local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Packets) -- Broadcast to all: Packets.BroadcastMyEvent:Fire(player, position) -- Fire to one client: Packets.BroadcastMyEvent:FireClient(targetPlayer, player, position) Wire the receiver. On the server (listening for client sends): Packets.MyPacket.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(sender: Player, valueOne, valueTwo, valueThree) -- validate and handle end) On the client (listening for server sends): Packets.BroadcastMyEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(player, position) -- handle end) Update the networking map. Open docs/reference/networking-map.md and add a row for your new packet in the same commit. Include: packet name, direction (C→S / S→C / S→All), payload summary, and which scripts send/receive it.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Play-test with at least one client and the server running.Trigger the send path and confirm the receiver fires.Check the Output window — Packet will warn if a type mismatch or serialization error occurs.For request/response packets, confirm the response values arrive correctly on the caller side.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open Signals/init.luau. File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau. Browse existing entries to understand the declaration style and grouping before adding yours. Add your signal. Add it under the relevant comment group (or add a new group). Follow the existing pattern exactly — type-annotate the generic parameter so Luau can check call sites: -- My System (Client Side) -- Fired by <ProducerScript> when <event>. Consumed by <ConsumerScript>. -- (<argOne>: type, <argTwo>: type) MySignal = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<string, number>, For signals with no payload (fire/connect only): MySignal = Signal(), Fire from the producer. local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) Signals.MySignal:Fire("hello", 42) Only one script should act as the authoritative producer. Document it in the signal's comment. Connect in the consumer(s). local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) Signals.MySignal:Connect(function(argOne: string, argTwo: number) -- handle the event end) When the consumer has a scoped lifecycle (e.g., a GUI controller), track the connection with a Janitor so it is disconnected on cleanup: cleaner:Add(Signals.MySignal:Connect(function(argOne, argTwo) -- handle end), "Disconnect") Update the signals map. Open docs/reference/signals-map.md and add a row for your new signal in the same commit. Include: signal name, producer script, consumer script(s), and a one-line purpose summary.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio.Trigger the code path that fires the signal.Confirm the consumer callback runs with the expected arguments.If the consumer never fires: confirm both scripts require the same Signals module instance (both via ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) and that the consumer connects before the first fire.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open SoundConfig. File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau. It exports three tables: SoundConfig.Sfx, SoundConfig.Music.Playlists, and SoundConfig.Ambience.Beds. Add your definition. One-shot / looped SFX — add an entry to SoundConfig.Sfx: MyNewSfx = { Id = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", Volume = 0.5, -- optional; default engine volume if omitted Pitch = 1.0, -- optional PitchRange = { 0.9, 1.1 }, -- optional; overrides Pitch; random per play Group = "SFX", -- "SFX" | "BGM" | "Ambience"; default "SFX" Replicate = true, -- set true only for positional sounds other clients should hear Debounce = 0.1, -- optional; min seconds between plays (anti-spam) PoolInitial = 2, -- optional; for PlaySFXAt only — pre-warms the pool at Init PoolMax = 8, -- optional; hard cap for the positional pool }, The SoundDef type (exported from SoundConfig) documents every field. Music track — add asset IDs to one of the three context playlists in SoundConfig.Music.Playlists (see BGM contexts below): Normal = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://AAA", "rbxassetid://BBB" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.5, FadeOut = 1.5, GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300, Volume = 0.6, }, Ambience bed — add to SoundConfig.Ambience.Beds and, if it should start automatically, add its name to SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart: Beds = { MyAmbience = { Id = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", Volume = 0.4 }, }, Autostart = { "MyAmbience" }, -- fade in on SoundManager.Init() Play the sound from a client script. Require SoundManager (never instantiate a Sound directly): local SoundManager = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.SoundManager) -- One-shot 2D: SoundManager.PlaySFX("MyNewSfx") -- Positional (requires PoolInitial / PoolMax in the def for pre-warm): SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("MyNewSfx", somePosition) -- Looped SFX (returns a LoopHandle — call :Stop() to end it): local handle = SoundManager.PlayLooped("MyNewSfx") -- ...later: handle:Stop() -- Music playlist (normally driven by MusicDirector via context, not called directly): SoundManager.PlayMusic("Normal") -- Ambience (replaces current beds; use AddAmbience to layer): SoundManager.SetAmbience({ "MyAmbience" }) SoundManager.AddAmbience("MyAmbience") SoundManager.RemoveAmbience("MyAmbience") SoundManager.StopAmbience() -- Volume bus (0..1): SoundManager.SetVolume("SFX", 0.8) SoundManager.Init() is called once by SoundController.client.luau — do not call it from feature code. Wire replication if needed. If other clients need to hear the sound when it plays at a world position, set Replicate = true in the SoundConfig.Sfx entry. The server relay uses SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() to build its allowlist. SoundConfig.GetPreloadIds() collects all non-empty IDs for ContentProvider:PreloadAsync.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: Background music is context-driven, not played by name from feature code. MusicDirector.client.luau owns the active context and calls SoundManager.PlayMusic for you — you only ever add tracks to a playlist and (for combat) call the server API.  SoundConfig.Music.Playlists has exactly three entries, one per context:  Context	Trigger	Gap behaviorNormal	Default; nothing else active	Gapped — random silence between tracks Combat	Server calls MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat")	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence LowFuel	Automatic, client-derived (see below)	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence  Priority when more than one condition is true: Combat > LowFuel > Normal.  Add asset IDs to Tracks on the relevant playlist — do not add new playlist names, the engine and director both assume exactly these three:  Playlists = { Normal = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://AAA", "rbxassetid://BBB" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.5, FadeOut = 1.5, GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300, Volume = 0.6 }, Combat = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://CCC" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.0, FadeOut = 1.0, GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, Volume = 0.7 }, LowFuel = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://DDD" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 2.0, FadeOut = 2.0, GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, Volume = 0.55 }, }   Field	MeaningFadeIn	Seconds to fade the new track up from 0 at start FadeOut	Seconds to fade a track down to 0 at its end (or the crossfade overlap window when continuous) GapMin / GapMax	Random silence range (seconds) between tracks. GapMax <= 0 means continuous — the next track starts FadeOut seconds before the current one ends, producing an overlapping crossfade instead of silence Volume	Target playback volume for tracks in this playlist (pre-bus-volume)  Normal uses GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300 (a real silent gap between tracks). Combat and LowFuel use GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0 so they loop continuously with no silence.  Low fuel is automatic — never set it manually. Combat is the only context gameplay code drives, via the server-authoritative MusicService:  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   SetContext fires the Packets.SetMusicContext packet to that one player; MusicDirector.client.luau receives it and resolves the active context by priority. Passing "Normal" clears the combat override — the client then falls back to LowFuel or Normal based on its own fuel state; it does not force Normal if fuel is still low.  Low fuel itself needs no code: MusicDirector watches Signals.OnTrainStateChanged and activates the LowFuel context whenever fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25).

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio (client context).Trigger the code path that calls PlaySFX / PlaySFXAt / etc.Confirm the sound plays. If silent: check the asset ID is correct, that Volume is not 0, and that the Group bus volume (SoundManager.GetVolume) is non-zero.For positional sounds with Replicate = true, check the Output window for server-relay errors.For BGM: confirm the track plays in Normal by default, that calling MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") from a server script switches it with a crossfade (no silence), and that draining fuel below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct switches to LowFuel when not in combat.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the junk config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau. Tune spawn rate. Field	Default	EffectDEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5	Seconds between spawns while the train is running STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5	Seconds between spawns while the train is braked/stalled Lower values = more frequent spawns. Both JunkService (server) and the spawn scheduler read these. Tune junk movement speed. Field	Default	EffectDEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10	Studs per second while train is running STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5	Studs per second while train is braked/stalled SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5	Seconds to smoothly transition between speed states SPEED_RAMP_DURATION also controls how smoothly junk decelerates when the train brakes. The first SetTrainState or SetJunkSpeed packet after a client joins snaps to target speed immediately; subsequent ones smoothstep over this duration. Tune despawn distance. JunkConfig.DESPAWN_DISTANCE = 700 -- studs Both the server odometer (JunkService) and client odometer (JunkController) compare accumulated currentSpeed * dt against this value. Increase it to let junk travel farther before disappearing; decrease it to clean up junk sooner. Adjust tier weights.Each tier entry has a Weight field. Selection is weighted-random across tiers. Higher weight = more frequent. Default distribution: Tier 1: 2000 (common) Tier 2: 1000 Tier 3: 10 Tier 4: 5 Tier 5: 0 (currently disabled) To enable Tier 5, set its Weight above 0. To make high-tier junk rarer, reduce Tier 3/4 weights. Adjust type weights and spawn chances within a tier.Inside each tier, Types maps type names (Metal, Wood, Energy) to a rule: Metal = { SpawnChance = 80, Yield = 3 } SpawnChance — probability (0–100) that this type is chosen once its tier is selected.Yield — how many material units are awarded when this junk is collected. To make Energy junk rarer within a tier, lower its SpawnChance relative to Metal/Wood. Tune the pity threshold. JunkConfig.ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD = 8 After this many consecutive non-Energy spawns, the next spawn is forced to be Energy. Raise the value to allow longer dry streaks; lower it to guarantee Energy more frequently. Adjust BaseModifiers for live multipliers (if used).BaseModifiers contains runtime-adjustable multipliers that scale spawn rates and per-tier/per-type frequency without rewriting the static tables: BaseModifiers = { GlobalSpawnRateMult = 1.0, TierMultipliers = { [1]=1.0, [2]=1.0, [3]=1.0, [4]=1.0, [5]=1.0 }, TypeMultipliers = { Metal=1.0, Wood=1.0, Energy=1.0 }, } These are applied by JunkService at spawn time. Modifying them at runtime (e.g. from an event/buff system) is safe; they are not cached. Validate spawn volume layout and motion path.After config changes, confirm that spawned junk appears within the intended volume and travels in the direction set by MOVE_DIRECTION (Vector3.new(1, 0, 0) by default). Open the Output window and watch for the JunkConfig: No models found warning — this fires if a JunkAssets tier folder is missing models. Verify the collection loop feels fair.Run a local session, collect junk at the new rate, and confirm the stamina/grabhook gameplay loop still has enough breathing room. If spawn rate is very high, increase MAX_SERVER_JUNKS (200) or MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS (250) to avoid the spawn cap cutting off the flow.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo playtest for 2–3 minutes with the Output window open. Confirm the observed spawn frequency roughly matches DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE, that junk despawns before leaving the visible play area, and that no JunkConfig: warnings appear.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina/sprint config.Sprint constants share the file src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau with stamina values. Both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server) read from this single config module. Update sprint speed. WalkSpeed = 16 -- base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed = 24 -- speed while sprinting Change SprintSpeed to the desired value. SprintController sets Humanoid.WalkSpeed directly and predicts locally; the server does not validate movement speed today (see Stamina & Sprint — Gotchas), so a speed change is purely a client-side/config edit. Update FOV. DefaultFOV = 70 -- camera FOV while walking SprintFOV = 85 -- camera FOV while sprinting SprintController animates the transition. Changing these values alters the start and end points of the FOV tween — no animation code changes are needed. Update keybinds. SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB } Add, remove, or replace entries. Both gamepad and keyboard inputs are accepted in the same array. SprintController reads this array to register UserInputService listeners. If state machine behavior changes, mirror both sides.If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. a new "dash" state): Edit src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau for client-side prediction and visual feedback.Edit src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau for server-side authority and packet emission.Update src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau if the validation predicates need to change (e.g. MinMoveDirection, MaxBackwardComponent, MinHorizontalSpeed) — this module is the single gate called identically by both sides.Register any new packet in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau and document it in the networking map. Verify shift-lock interaction.SmoothShiftLock (vendored in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SmoothShiftLock/) reacts to the sprint state. After changing sprint speed or keybinds, confirm that entering and exiting shift-lock while sprinting does not produce a stuck speed or FOV. Verify placement interaction.Build mode disables sprint while active. After changing sprint config, open build mode, attempt to sprint, and confirm it stays suppressed. Exit build mode and confirm sprint re-enables immediately. Test stamina drain under new speed.If SprintSpeed changed significantly, revisit StaminaDrain and StaminaRegen in the same config to ensure the economy still feels balanced. See Tune Stamina Economy for field details.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Sprint in a straight line, confirm the WalkSpeed and FOV match the new config values. Trigger shift-lock while sprinting, confirm no stuck state. Enter build mode, confirm sprint is suppressed; exit, confirm sprint resumes. Open the Output window and confirm no StaminaManager sync errors.

searchDocs.title: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
Steps​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Confirm the placement Model exists.ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> must already exist — this is required for placement itself and is the same model used by Stash/Move. Author the Tool template.Create (or confirm) a Tool in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name>. Create the PlaceableTools folder under ReplicatedStorage if it does not exist yet.Set the attribute PlaceableName = "<Name>" on the Tool root (string attribute, exact match).The Tool must have a Handle BasePart. Author its scripts and behaviour as you would any other placeable tool. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, both buttons fail silently server-side — no model is destroyed and no item is lost, but the buttons do nothing. Add the buttons to the GUI.Inside the GUI that the placeable's ProximityPrompt opens, add two ImageButton instances: one named exactly MoveButton, one named exactly StashButton. They can be placed at any depth in the GUI's descendant hierarchy. To make them invisible but still clickable, set both ImageTransparency = 1 and BackgroundTransparency = 1 on each button. If either button is missing, PlaceableActions.bind will log a warning at runtime. Bind and unbind in the controller.In the controller script that opens and closes the placeable GUI, call PlaceableActions.bind when the GUI opens and binding:Unbind() when it closes: local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) -- When the GUI opens for a specific placed Model: local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) -- When the GUI closes (or the controller cleans up): binding:Unbind() placedModel is the Model instance in workspace.PlacedObjects. guiRoot is the root GUI instance opened by the ProximityPrompt (the ancestor that contains MoveButton and StashButton). If you use a Janitor for the GUI lifecycle, track the binding with it: cleaner:Add(binding, "Unbind") (Optional) Configure sound IDs.In src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau (or the equivalent config for your placeable system), set PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash and PlacementConfig.Sounds.Move to the desired rbxassetid:// strings. Leave as "" to disable sound playback for that action. See Add a Sound if the asset ID does not yet exist in SoundConfig. (Optional) Tune cooldown and poof duration.In PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions: Cooldown — minimum seconds between successive Stash/Move requests per player (default 0.4).PoofDuration — how long the shrink-and-disappear visual plays (seconds).

searchDocs.title: Server-side guarantees​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Per-player cooldown gates spam.The target must be a direct child of workspace.PlacedObjects and carry a non-empty PlaceableName attribute (set automatically by PlacementServer at place-time).An atomic claim ensures two players cannot double-grant the same Tool simultaneously.No distance check — the ProximityPrompt enforces proximity at GUI-open time.  On success, every client receives a BroadcastPlaceablePoof packet and renders a transient shrinking clone at the model's position, parented to workspace.PlaceablePoofs and destroyed when the animation completes.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Place the item in Studio via the normal placement flow.Walk up to it so the ProximityPrompt activates and the GUI opens.Click StashButton — confirm the model disappears with the poof effect and the Tool appears in your Backpack.Place it again, open the GUI, click MoveButton — confirm the model disappears and the Tool is immediately equipped.Check the Output window for any PlaceableActions warnings about missing buttons or a missing Tool template.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Set up the premium subscription. BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID gates the entire Premium row. While it's "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs (GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync, PromptSubscriptionPurchase) are skipped entirely — safe to ship pre-launch without spamming errors. In the Creator Dashboard, go to Monetization → Subscriptions and create the subscription first (price, billing period, display copy).Paste its id (format EXP-XXXXXXXXXX) into BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID.Keep the value identical in every place of the universe — BattlePassManager runs place-agnostic (lobby and gameplay both resolve premium status live), so a mismatch would make premium appear/disappear across a teleport. Edit the tier track. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luau. The base Tiers[level] table (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL) is generated in a loop; edit an individual tier after generation, or edit the loop itself for a track-wide change: -- Bump a single regular tier's Free reward after the fact: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[7].Free = { Type = "Coins", Amount = 300 } -- Or add a one-off Item reward on a non-milestone tier: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[20].Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "SomeAccessoryId" } A Reward is { Type = "Coins", Amount: number } or { Type = "Item", ItemId: string }. An empty ItemId = "" is a placeholder milestone slot — see Gotchas. Milestone tiers (15, 30, 45, 60 in the shipped default) pay a chunkier Free coin bonus plus a Premium Item slot; regular tiers pay Coins on both rows. Add a SeasonOverrides entry for one month (optional). To swap in a different reward for one specific season only (e.g. a themed accessory for this month's milestone) without touching the evergreen base Tiers, add an entry to BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides, keyed by season index (year*12 + month-1, i.e. BattlePassState.seasonIndex), then by tier level: -- Override tier 30's Premium reward for a specific season (e.g. July 2026 = 2026*12+6 = 24318). BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[24318] = { [30] = { Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "JulyAccessory" } }, } Any row present in SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] shadows the base Tiers[level] entry for that row, for that one season only — an override that only sets Premium leaves Free on the base table for that tier. BattlePassState.tierReward resolves the override before falling back to Tiers, and both the server (grant) and client (display) call the same function, so they can never disagree. Fill milestone ItemIds. Every milestone tier ships with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = "") as a placeholder. Before launch, replace each with a real asset id: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[15].Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "AccessoryAssetId15" } See Gotchas — an unfilled slot silently grants nothing and still marks itself claimed. Tune ExpPerLevel against quest BPExp. BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel (a flat number, or a { [level]: number } table for a curve) sets the cumulative EXP cost per tier. The only EXP source is Reward.BPExp on quests (fed via Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — see Battle Pass — EXP earning), so a full clear's reachability is entirely a function of how much BPExp the quest pool pays out over a month: Flat default: ExpPerLevel = 1000, MAX_LEVEL = 60 → 60,000 total EXP for a full clear.The shipped Scope = "Season" quests alone pay 3000 BPExp each (SeasonJunk/SeasonKills/SeasonDistance = 9,000 for the month) — Daily/Weekly BPExp amounts (e.g. 200–1200 per quest, repeating every rotation) make up the rest.To make a full clear reachable in a month: estimate the average daily/weekly BPExp a reasonably active player earns per day, multiply by ~30, add the Season total, and set ExpPerLevel (or the per-level table) so the running total lands near or under that number. Raise per-quest BPExp values instead of lowering ExpPerLevel if you want the quests to feel more rewarding rather than the track to feel shorter.A { [level]: number } table lets early tiers cost less (fast early momentum) and late tiers cost more (a grind at the top) — BattlePassState.levelFromExp/progress handle either shape transparently. Add Scope = "Season" quests (optional). Season quests are the dedicated battle pass EXP feed — the whole set is active for the entire month (no rotation/shuffle, unlike Daily/Weekly). Add an entry to QuestConfig.Quests in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luau: SeasonCrafting = { Scope = "Season", Category = "Personal", Metric = QuestConfig.Metrics.JunkCollected, Target = 2000, DisplayName = "Season Scrapper", Description = "Collect 2,000 junk this season", Reward = { Coins = 0, Exp = 0, BPExp = 3000 } }, Metric must be one of QuestConfig.Metrics, same as any other quest — see Tune Quests — Add a quest for wiring a brand-new metric. The shipped Season quests pay Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and only BPExp — Season quests exist purely to move the battle pass track, not the coin/XP economy — but this isn't enforced; a Season quest can also pay coins/exp if you want it to. No Counts entry applies to Scope = "Season" — every Season quest in the pool is always active, so add exactly as many as you want visible this month.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Confirm BattlePassClient.GetProgress() returns level 0, Exp 0 on a fresh profile, and BattlePassClient.GetTiers() reflects your edited Tiers/SeasonOverrides.Complete a quest carrying BPExp and confirm BattlePassClient.Changed fires with the level/progress advancing accordingly.Call BattlePassClient.Claim(); confirm BattlePassClient.GetClaimableSummary() returns (0, 0, 0) immediately after (idempotent — a second claim finds nothing outstanding).If testing Premium: set a real SUBSCRIPTION_ID, subscribe as a test account, and confirm BattlePassClient.IsPremium() flips to true and a retroactive sweep grants every reached Premium tier for the season.If you changed SeasonOverrides, confirm the override actually landed on the current season index (BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time())) — an override keyed to the wrong season silently never applies.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable. Only do this intentionally, and change it in both places together.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward left at ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted (there's nothing to hand off to an inventory system) but the claimed flag is still set, so the player never sees that tier offered again — even after you later fill in a real ItemId. Fill every milestone slot before launch, not after.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Choose a starter perk. A perk with UnlockCost = 0 (or omitted) and UnlockLevel = 0 (or omitted) is a free "starter" — PerkManager.seedStarters auto-unlocks it for every player on load and after every respec of its pool, with no coin or level requirement. Today the two starters are PlayerHP (Vitality, Personal) and JunkRarity (Salvage Luck, Party) — one per pool, so a brand-new player always has at least one perk to invest points in per pool. PlayerHP = { Category = "Personal", BuffKey = "HPBonus", PerLevel = 0.04, MaxLevel = 10, Order = 1, DisplayName = "Vitality", Description = "+%d%% Max HP", UnlockCost = 0, UnlockLevel = 0 }, -- starter To make a different perk a starter, set its UnlockCost and UnlockLevel to 0. To stop a perk from being a starter, give it a nonzero UnlockCost and/or UnlockLevel. If you remove starter status from every perk in a pool, players in that pool have nothing to unlock for free — make sure at least one perk per pool stays a 0/0 starter. Set a perk's coin cost and level gate. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and edit the entry: PassiveRegen = { Category = "Personal", BuffKey = "RegenBonus", PerLevel = 0.10, MaxLevel = 10, Order = 2, DisplayName = "Regeneration", Description = "+%d%% HP regen rate", UnlockCost = 250, UnlockLevel = 3 }, UnlockCost — coins deducted once, via CoinManager.DeductCoins, when the player unlocks the perk (ReqUnlockPerk → PerkManager.UnlockPerk).UnlockLevel — minimum player XP level required before the unlock is allowed (PerkState.canUnlock rejects with LEVEL_REQUIRED below this). Both checks are enforced server-side by PerkState.canUnlock (order: unknown perk → already unlocked → level → coins), so there's no way to bypass them from the client. Changes take effect immediately for any not-yet-unlocked perk — there's no re-pricing concern for perks a player has already paid for, since the cost is only ever charged once. Remember costs are one-time; leveling stays point-based. UnlockCost is charged exactly once, at unlock. It has no effect on leveling a perk up afterward — that still costs 1 derived point per level from the pool's point economy (see Perks — Point economy), same as before this system existed. Raising UnlockCost makes a perk more expensive to access, not more expensive to level. Account for the respec-refund consequence. PerkManager.Respec fully resets a pool: it clears levels, re-locks every perk in that pool, and refunds each perk's UnlockCost via CoinManager.RefundCoins (exact — not scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus, unlike CoinManager.AddCoins). This means the coin cost you set is exactly what comes back on respec. A perk with UnlockCost = 800 (Heavy Ordnance) returns 800 coins when its pool is respecced; a starter (UnlockCost = 0) returns nothing and simply stays unlocked (starters are re-seeded after the clear). If you want respec to feel cheap or costly for the player, tune UnlockCost with that in mind — there is no separate respec-refund knob.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Confirm both starters (Vitality, Salvage Luck) show unlocked with no coin/level prompt, and every other perk shows locked with its UnlockCost/UnlockLevel.Earn enough coins and level to satisfy a locked perk's gate, unlock it, and confirm coins are deducted immediately and the perk becomes allocatable (buffs do not change from the unlock itself — only from subsequently spending points).Try to unlock a perk while under-leveled or under-funded and confirm the request is rejected (LEVEL_REQUIRED / NOT_ENOUGH_COINS) with no coin deduction.Allocate a few points into the unlocked perk, then respec its pool and confirm: levels clear, the perk re-locks, and its UnlockCost is refunded to the coin balance exactly (no Fortune scaling).

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME wipes all saved perk + unlock data PerkConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerPerks") is the ProfileStore key for both PerkLevels and Unlocked. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — equivalent to wiping all perk progress and all unlocks. Only do this intentionally.  Lowering PerkSchemaVersion is not a way to re-wipe perk data The one-time clean-slate migration (see Perks — Unlock gate) is guarded by profile.Data.PerkSchemaVersion < 1 and is deliberately one-shot per profile: it exists to wipe pre-unlock-gate allocations exactly once when this system shipped, not as a general-purpose "reset everyone" lever. Editing the stored version back down does not replay cleanly — PerkManager only ever bumps PerkSchemaVersion forward on load. If you need to force a full wipe later, change PerkConfig.STORE_NAME instead (see above), and expect it to also drop leveling progress, not just unlocks.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Add a quest. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luau and add an entry to QuestConfig.Quests: JunkDailyC = { Scope = "Daily", Category = "Personal", Metric = QuestConfig.Metrics.JunkCollected, Target = 60, DisplayName = "Junk Fanatic", Description = "Collect 60 junk", Reward = { Coins = 350, Exp = 160 } }, Metric must be one of QuestConfig.Metrics (EnemyKills, DistanceTravelled, JunkCollected). Reusing an already-wired metric needs no code change — QuestManager and QuestSourcesLoader pick it up automatically the next time QuestState.selectQuests includes it in the rotation.To track a new kind of progress, wire it in src/ServerScriptService/QuestSourcesLoader.server.luau first: add a new key to QuestConfig.Metrics, then call QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) (has an actor — credits Personal + fans out to Party) or QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey, amount) (ownerless world event — Party only) from wherever the underlying game event fires. See Quests — Sources for the three existing examples.Category ("Personal" or "Party") and Scope ("Daily" or "Weekly") determine which sub-pool the quest rotates into — see Quests — Buckets. Choose Target and Reward. Target is the raw progress amount required (same units the source reports — e.g. junk count, enemy kills, distance units). Compare against similar existing quests of the same Scope/Metric to keep difficulty consistent (e.g. JunkDailyA = 25 vs JunkWeeklyA = 250, a 10x jump from daily to weekly).Reward.Coins / Reward.Exp are paid once per claim via CoinManager.AddCoins(player, coins, "Quest:"..questId) (scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus, like any other earned coins — see Economy) and XPManager.AddXP(player, exp). Scale both together with Target so effort-to-reward stays proportionate; weekly quests in the shipped pool pay roughly 8x their daily counterparts.DisplayName/Description are shown by a future GUI via QuestClient's QuestView; Description should read as an activity sentence (e.g. "Collect 25 junk") since there's no separate progress-text field. Icon is optional (nil = none). Adjust Counts per period. QuestConfig.Counts controls how many quests of each category rotate in per scope: QuestConfig.Counts = { Daily = { Personal = 1, Party = 2 }, Weekly = { Personal = 1, Party = 1 }, } Raising a count (e.g. Daily.Party = 3) requires at least that many quests of that Scope+Category to exist in QuestConfig.Quests — QuestState.selectQuests clamps to math.min(count, #pool), so an under-populated pool silently rotates in fewer quests than configured rather than erroring. Add enough quest entries before raising a count. Shift reset boundaries. Resets happen at local midnight, where "local" is set by QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed offset in seconds from UTC (pre-launch default -5 * 3600 = US Eastern, the largest single Roblox player timezone). This is the one knob to change to re-timezone the whole system; set it to 0 for pure UTC. It's a fixed offset, so it does not follow daylight saving — during summer (EDT) resets land one wall-clock hour later. QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset (= -ResetTimezoneOffset, day rolls at 00:00 local) and QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset (= 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset; the 4-day base aligns week starts to Monday since the Unix epoch was a Thursday) are derived from it — change ResetTimezoneOffset, not these two directly, unless you want the daily and weekly boundaries in different timezones. Changing any of them takes effect immediately for every player on their next ensureCurrent check (the periodic rollover tick, or their next join/progress/claim) — there's no migration needed, but changing a boundary mid-period can make the live rollover fire earlier or later than players expect for whichever period is in flight. Prefer changing these during a maintenance window (see Disruption) rather than live. Keep the value identical in the lobby and gameplay places (it's the same shared file) or the two places will disagree on which period is active.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Confirm QuestClient.GetQuests() (or a print in a test script) returns the expected active ids for the current period, matching what QuestState.selectQuests would compute server-side.Trigger the relevant source (collect junk, defeat a tagged enemy, or wait through a train-running distance tick) and confirm the matching quest's Progress advances and QuestClient.Changed fires.Complete a quest and call QuestClient.Claim(questId); confirm coins and exp are granted exactly once, and a second claim attempt fails with ALREADY_CLAIMED (result code 5).If you changed Counts, confirm the newly-added quest pool member actually appears in rotation (rotation is seeded by period index, so you may need to wait for a period boundary or temporarily lower ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS to observe it sooner).

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets QuestManager's session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all prior progress, claimed flags, and the never-reset Lifetime table (the perk seam) become unreachable. Only do this intentionally, and change it in both places together.  Removing a quest id that's currently active can strand progress QuestState.selectQuests only picks from ids present in QuestConfig.Quests at call time. Deleting an id mid-period means any player with progress toward it simply loses visibility into that entry (the stored Progress[questId] value lingers harmlessly in the profile until the bucket resets, but nothing can claim it). Prefer retiring a quest by leaving it in the pool with an unreachable Target change only at a period boundary, or accept the stranded-progress edge case for a rarely-hit quest.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Change a perk's numeric values. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and adjust the entry: PlayerHP = { PerLevel = 0.04, -- ← buff per level (fraction; 0.04 = 4% per level) MaxLevel = 10, -- ← cap ... }, PerLevel is a fraction (not percent). The GUI multiplies by 100 for display. The buff folder attribute is PerLevel * level, so a change here propagates automatically — no code change needed. Add a new perk — declare it in PerkConfig.Perks. Pick a unique key, a Category ("Personal" or "Party"), a unique BuffKey attribute name, PerLevel, MaxLevel, Order (display order within the tab, no gaps required), DisplayName, and Description (with a %d placeholder for the bonus percent). Wire a consumer. The consumer reads the attribute from the buff folder: Personal: ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<player.UserId>:GetAttribute(perk.BuffKey)Party: ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs:GetAttribute(perk.BuffKey) Read it fresh each time it is needed (or subscribe to GetAttributeChangedSignal if you need live updates). Understand the point economy before tuning it. Each XP level grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point — no separate point storage.Available points = playerLevel - sum(perk levels in that pool).You cannot tune the point grant rate without changing PerkState.available and PerkManager.replicate in tandem. There is intentionally no config for it. Know what respec does. Players can respec either pool freely from the GUI. The server clears the relevant entries in PerkLevels (available points return to the wallet automatically), and also re-locks every unlocked perk in that pool and refunds its UnlockCost via CoinManager.RefundCoins (exact, not scaled by Fortune's CoinGainBonus) — see Unlock gate.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Open the perk panel (bottom-center "Perks" button).Spend a point on a perk and confirm: The level counter increments.In Explorer, ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId> shows the updated attribute.The downstream consumer reflects the change (e.g. Humanoid MaxHealth for Vitality). Respec and confirm levels reset, points return, unlocked perks in that pool re-lock, and their unlock coins are refunded.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Change a node's per-level cost or duration.Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ResearchConfig.luau and edit the Levels table on the node: Durability_T1 = { Category = "Train", DisplayName = "Scrap Plating", Description = "+%d shield capacity", Prereq = nil, MaxLevel = 3, Effect = { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 50 }, Levels = { [1] = { Cost = { Metal = 25 }, Duration = 20 }, -- ← per-level cost / time [2] = { Cost = { Metal = 60 }, Duration = 35 }, [3] = { Cost = { Metal = 120 }, Duration = 55 }, }, }, Cost is a { [materialItemType]: number } map — any ItemType that exists as a craft-material Tool template under ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials is valid (not just Wood/Metal; unlike the Workbench GUI, the Research GUI renders however many cost rows a node has). Duration is in seconds and is the wall-clock time the level takes to complete while fuel is available — see step 2 below. Both values take effect immediately for any job enqueued after the change; jobs already queued or active keep the cost/duration they were enqueued with (no live re-pricing). Changing Effect.PerLevel (for StatBuff) or Effect.DrainPerLevel (for FuelEfficiency) changes the buff granted per level — see step 5 for the effect shapes. No code change is needed; ResearchEffectsDispatcher recomputes buffs from ResearchConfig.Nodes on every level-up. Review the fuel and pause behavior before retuning it. FUEL_CAP (default 100) — the fuel reserve ceiling.FUEL_BURN_RATE (default 1.0/sec) — how fast fuel burns while a job is active. Raising this makes fuel run out faster relative to node Duration, so jobs pause more often; consider raising EnergyFuelValue in tandem if you raise this.EnergyFuelValue (default {20, 35, 55, 80, 110} for Energy tool tiers 1–5) — fuel granted per refuel. Tune this against FUEL_BURN_RATE * <typical node Duration> so a single refuel roughly covers the jobs you want it to. A job's elapsed only advances while fuel is available (ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate)), so at FUEL_BURN_RATE = 1.0 and FUEL_CAP = 100, a fully-fueled bench can sustain 100 seconds of active research before needing a refuel. Change the queue depth.QUEUE_MAX (default 8) caps how many jobs can wait behind the active one (ResearchState.validateEnqueue rejects with QUEUE_FULL beyond this). Raise it to let players stack more research ahead of time; lower it to force more frequent bench visits. Change the cancel refund fraction.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (default 0.5) is the fraction of the active job's cost refunded when it is cancelled — queued jobs always refund at 1.0 (full), since they haven't started consuming fuel/time yet. Set this to 1.0 to make cancelling an in-progress job free, or 0 to make active progress non-refundable. This does not affect the cascade behavior itself (see Research Bench — Cascade-cancel) — only the fraction applied to the active job's refund. Add a new node. Declare it in ResearchConfig.Nodes. Pick a unique key (the nodeId), a Category ("Train", "Player", "Equipment", or "Recipes" — display grouping only, drives which header the node's row appears under in the GUI), DisplayName (the only descriptive text the shipped ResearchGuiController renders per row today — Description is authored in config but not currently displayed; add it to the row-building code if you want it shown), an optional Prereq (another node's id — nil means available from the start) and PrereqLevel (defaults to 1 if omitted — the level the prereq must reach before this node accepts enqueues), MaxLevel, and Levels (one {Cost, Duration} entry per level from 1 to MaxLevel). Example — a new two-level "Reinforced Hull" node gated behind Durability_T1 reaching level 2: ReinforcedHull = { Category = "Train", DisplayName = "Reinforced Hull", Description = "+%d shield capacity", Prereq = "Durability_T1", PrereqLevel = 2, MaxLevel = 2, Effect = { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 75 }, Levels = { [1] = { Cost = { Metal = 150, Wood = 20 }, Duration = 60 }, [2] = { Cost = { Metal = 260, Wood = 40 }, Duration = 90 }, }, }, Choose an Effect shape (omit entirely — Effect = nil — for a pure recipe/gate node with no buff): { Type = "StatBuff", Key = <attributeName>, PerLevel = <number> } — the effect handler in ResearchEffectsDispatcher sums PerLevel * level across every node sharing the same Key into that attribute on ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs. Reuse an existing Key (e.g. "MaxHP") to stack with existing nodes, or introduce a new Key and wire a new consumer to read it.{ Type = "FuelEfficiency", DrainPerLevel = <number, 0 < n < 1> } — multiplies into ResearchBuffs.FuelEfficiency as DrainPerLevel ^ level (values below 1 reduce drain; e.g. 0.85 per level means 3 levels compound to 0.85^3 ≈ 0.614). TrainFuelManager already reads this attribute — no new consumer needed if you're adding another fuel-efficiency node.Any other Type string logs a warn and no-ops in ResearchEffectsDispatcher — safe to author a node ahead of its gameplay wiring, but the buff will not apply until a handler exists.nil — a recipe/gate node. Once it reaches level 1, ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> is written; wire a Workbench recipe's RequiresNode to that same id (see Workbench Crafting), or read the folder from any other gate you want to add. Test in Studio: join at the bench, confirm the new row appears under the right Category header (locked/greyed if Prereq isn't met yet), enqueue it, and confirm materials are deducted immediately. Let it complete (or refuel to speed through fuel pauses) and confirm the effect applies — check the ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs attribute in Explorer for a StatBuff/FuelEfficiency node, or ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> for a recipe node.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled, walk to the ResearchBench-tagged Model.Open the GUI (ResearchPromptPart prompt) and enqueue a cheap node's level 1.Confirm materials are deducted immediately (before the job completes) and the active panel shows the job progressing.Let fuel run to 0 (or start with an empty bench) and confirm the progress bar stops advancing and the "PAUSED" badge appears; trigger RefuelPromptPart with a held Energy tool and confirm progress resumes.Queue a second level of the same node behind the first, then cancel the first (lower) level from the active panel — confirm both the active job and the queued second level refund and clear (cascade-cancel), and that ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/ResearchBuffs do not update for a job that never completed.Let a StatBuff node complete and confirm the target attribute in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs updates, or let a recipe node complete and confirm ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> appears and the corresponding Workbench recipe ungreys.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the shredder config.All shredder constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau. Tune hold duration.The required hold scales linearly between one junk item and MAX_JUNK_COUNT items: Field	Default	EffectMIN_HOLD_DURATION	0.3 s	Hold time required for exactly 1 junk item MAX_HOLD_DURATION	3.5 s	Hold time required when carrying MAX_JUNK_COUNT or more items MAX_JUNK_COUNT	10	Junk count at which duration is fully capped at MAX_HOLD_DURATION Increase MAX_HOLD_DURATION to make large batches feel weightier. Keep MIN_HOLD_DURATION above the sum of normal round-trip latency to avoid the server rejecting fast single-item shreds. Tune arc animation. Field	Default	EffectARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5 studs	Extra Y added to the bezier midpoint — controls arc peak height ARC_DURATION	0.55 s	Travel time per material Tool from spawn to landing ITEM_EJECT_DELAY	0.125 s	Stagger between consecutive ejected materials LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5 studs	Random spread around LandingPoint for a natural pile effect MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS	60	Cap on visually animated items per shred MAX_STREAM_DURATION	6.0 s	Budget cap for the full ejection stream (compresses delay if needed) Handle anti-exploit tolerances with care.These fields directly affect server-side rejection rates. Tighten them only after validating against real network conditions: Field	Default	Risk of over-tighteningINTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5 studs	Added on top of INTERACT_DISTANCE (10 studs) server-side to cover positional desync. Reducing below 3 will cause false rejections on high-latency clients. HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE	0.5 s	Subtracted from required hold when server validates timing. Setting below 0.3 will reject legitimate completions on 150ms+ RTT connections. PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN	1.0 s	Minimum gap between consecutive successful shreds per player. Do not set below 0.5 s. Adjust material yield.Material types produced by a shred are determined by JunkConfig.MaterialRules in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau: MaterialRules = { Metal = {"Metal"}, Wood = {"Wood"}, Energy = {"Energy"}, } To add a new material output type, add an entry here and create a matching Tool template inside the CraftingMaterials folder in ReplicatedStorage (see step 6). After changing these mappings, re-test ShredderServer.buildMaterialSequence output in Studio. Verify Studio asset setup before testing.The shredder system requires the following to be in place in the live place: Each workbench Model in Workspace must be tagged Workbench (CollectionService).Each workbench Model must have its PrimaryPart set.Each workbench must contain a child Model named TrajectoryPoints (field: TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: SpawnPoint (field: SPAWN_POINT_NAME) and LandingPoint (field: LANDING_POINT_NAME). Tag this model with PlacementIgnore.ReplicatedStorage must contain a Folder named CraftingMaterials (field: MATERIALS_FOLDER) with Tool templates: Wood, Metal (and any new types). Each Tool must have a BasePart child named Handle and CanBeDropped = false.Missing templates cause ShredderServer.ejectMaterials to fail silently. Test auto-collect delay.After ejection, materials lying on the floor auto-move to the owner's Backpack after: AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY = 45 -- seconds Adjust this if the window feels too long or too short for your gameplay loop.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo session, carry a mix of junk counts (1 item, 5 items, 10 items), and hold the shredder interaction. Confirm hold durations roughly match the linear interpolation between MIN_HOLD_DURATION and MAX_HOLD_DURATION. Watch the arc animation and confirm materials land near LandingPoint. Check the Output window — a missing CraftingMaterials template will print a warning but not throw a visible error.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau. This file is shared between client and server, so one edit propagates to both sides. Adjust core stamina values. Field	Default	EffectMaxStamina	100	Pool ceiling StaminaDrain	10	Units drained per second while sprinting StaminaRegen	15	Units regenerated per second when not sprinting RegenDelay	1.4	Seconds after sprint ends before regen starts Adjust sprint feel. Field	Default	EffectWalkSpeed	16	Base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed	24	Speed while sprinting DefaultFOV	70	Camera FOV at walk SprintFOV	85	Camera FOV during sprint FOV transitions are animated by SprintController; changing the values here is enough — no animation code changes needed. See Change Sprint Behavior for keybind and state-machine edits. Adjust sprint keybinds (if needed).The SprintBinds array accepts any mix of Enum.KeyCode and Enum.UserInputType values: SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB }, Add or replace entries. Both SprintController and StaminaManager read from the same config array. Tune buff parameters.Three buff types are defined; each has a Duration (seconds) and, where applicable, a Strength multiplier: StaminaRegenBuff = { Strength = 1.75, Duration = 18 } -- multiplies StaminaRegen StaminaUsageBuff = { Strength = 0.5, Duration = 15 } -- multiplies StaminaDrain InfiniteStaminaBuff = { Duration = 10 } -- disables drain entirely Strength is a multiplier applied to the base drain or regen rate. A Strength below 1.0 on StaminaUsageBuff means less drain (easier). Update buff icons (if adding a new icon).Icon asset IDs are in BuffIcons: BuffIcons = { InfiniteStamina = "rbxassetid://136295729783969", RegenMultiplier = "rbxassetid://126110497899525", UsageMultiplier = "rbxassetid://116908939168654", } Replace the rbxassetid://... string with a new uploaded asset ID. Validate client feel and server authority.SprintController (client) predicts drain and regen locally. StaminaManager (server) is the source of truth and corrects the client via packets. After saving, test in a live Studio session: sprint until exhausted, confirm drain/regen rates match the new values, and confirm the server correction does not cause jarring snaps. Test buff interactions.Trigger each buff type (via a test script or the existing pickup pathway) while sprinting. Confirm: StaminaRegenBuff accelerates refill during and after sprint.StaminaUsageBuff visibly slows drain while active.InfiniteStaminaBuff allows indefinite sprinting with no drain.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Sprint until stamina is depleted, release sprint, and confirm the regen delay then regen rate match the new config values. Trigger a buff and confirm it overrides base rates correctly. Check the Output window for any StaminaManager sync errors.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the placement config.Visual and icon settings live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau. Replace icon asset IDs.The Icons table holds one entry per toolbar button: Icons = { GridOn = "rbxassetid://118749020984103", GridOff = "rbxassetid://132920215751528", GhostUnlocked = "rbxassetid://132512888685903", GhostLocked = "rbxassetid://128344634676430", } Replace the rbxassetid://... value for any icon you want to update. Upload the new image in Studio's Asset Manager first to get a valid asset ID. The key names (GridOn, GridOff, GhostUnlocked, GhostLocked) must remain unchanged — BuildModeGuiController looks them up by key. Adjust ghost appearance. Field	Default	EffectVisualGhostTransparency	0.45	Opacity of main model parts during ghost preview CollisionBoxGhostTransparency	0.65	Opacity of the CollisionBox part during preview OtherGhostVisualTransparency	0.60	Opacity of other parts in other players' ghosts ShowCollisionBox	false	Set true to make CollisionBox visible during preview (debug aid) ColorValid	Color3.fromRGB(100, 210, 255)	Tint when placement is valid ColorInvalid	Color3.fromRGB(255, 80, 80)	Tint when placement is blocked ColorTweenTime	0.12 s	Duration of color transition between valid/invalid states Adjust ghost movement responsiveness. Field	Default	EffectFreeModeLerpSpeed	20	How quickly the ghost follows the cursor in free mode RotationLerpSpeed	15	How quickly the ghost rotates when the player rotates the item GhostUpdateHz	20	Raycast update rate (Hz) — lower values reduce CPU cost but feel less smooth Adjust the grid overlay. Field	Default	EffectGridTextureId	"rbxassetid://6372755229"	Decal texture applied to build area surfaces during grid mode GridTransparency	0.35	Opacity of the grid overlay (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) Keep the button-to-signal mapping consistent.src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BuildModeGuiController.client.luau wires each toolbar button to a Signals event. If you add a new button (e.g. a new toggle), you must: Add the new icon key to PlacementConfig.Icons.Create a corresponding Signals entry in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau if the button drives new behavior.Wire the button in BuildModeGuiController to fire/subscribe to that signal.Update the signals map (and the networking map if the signal crosses the client/server boundary). Do not add raw RemoteEvent calls from BuildModeGuiController — all cross-boundary communication must go through Packets. Test mobile input parity.Build mode must be fully operable without a keyboard. In a Studio mobile emulation session (or on device): Confirm all toolbar buttons are reachable and tap targets are large enough.Confirm grid/free toggle and rotation controls work via touch.Confirm the ghost follows touch drag correctly. Test desktop input parity.In a standard Studio session: Confirm keyboard shortcuts for grid toggle and rotation still fire correctly after any icon or signal changes.Confirm the cursor-following ghost is smooth at the configured GhostUpdateHz.

searchDocs.title: Verify​

searchDocs.title: Runtime buff folders​
searchDocs.content: These are not config modules but runtime ReplicatedStorage folders written by dispatchers and read by gameplay systems. Listed here because their writer/reader contracts are as important to maintain as static config. Defaults to 1.0 (no effect) until Fuel_T1 reaches level 1. Stacks multiplicatively with PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus — see Research Bench. searchDocs.title: Requirements​
searchDocs.content: The caller supplies a GuiButton that already contains:  an Option child (TextLabel) — shows the current selection's label,an Arrow child (ImageLabel) — flips up/down as the list opens/closes.  The widget builds the option list beneath the button at runtime.

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: local Dropdown = require(SharedModules.Gui.Dropdown) type Option = { Value: string, Label: string } type Config = { StartValue: string?, -- initial selection (no .Changed fired) OptionTemplate: GuiButton?, -- cloned per row; needs a "Label" TextLabel. Else rows are styled from the button. MaxVisible: number?, -- cap visible rows; scroll beyond RowHeight: number?, -- pixel height per row (default 28) ArrowUp: string?, ArrowDown: string?, -- arrow image overrides } local dropdown = Dropdown.new(button, options, config?)   Instance members:  .Changed: Signal<string> — fires the selected Value when the selection changes.:Select(value) — select by Value programmatically.:GetValue(): string? — current Value.:Show(visible) — open/close the list.:Destroy() — disconnect everything and remove the built list frame.

searchDocs.title: Notes​
searchDocs.content: The host ScreenGui should use Global ZIndexBehavior so the open list (high ZIndex) draws over sibling content.All connections are owned by a Janitor and released on :Destroy().When no OptionTemplate is given, each row's Label is a clone of the button's Option label, so rows inherit its text styling (alignment,TextScaled, font, RichText, child UIPadding) and stay in sync if the button is restyled. Because TextScaled is inherited, row text scales toRowHeight; set RowHeight to the button's pixel height to match its text size exactly.

searchDocs.title: Core rule: one Janitor per lifecycle scope​
searchDocs.content: Each distinct lifecycle gets exactly one Janitor. When that lifecycle ends, call:Cleanup or :Destroy on it (see below for which to use).  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local janitor = Janitor.new() -- Track a signal connection (cleaned up by calling :Disconnect) janitor:Add(inst.Event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") -- Track an Instance (cleaned up by calling :Destroy) janitor:Add(part, "Destroy") -- Tear down and reuse (leaves the Janitor alive for the next cycle) janitor:Cleanup() -- Tear down and discard (the Janitor itself is gone afterward) janitor:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: Cleanup vs Destroy​
searchDocs.content: Method	When to use	Typical example:Cleanup()	The Janitor is module-level and reused across respawns or re-equips.	characterJanitor, backpackJanitor — cleaned on every CharacterAdded, then refilled. :Destroy()	The Janitor is created per-entry and discarded when the entry is removed.	WorkbenchEntry.Cleaner, engine/lever entry janitors.  Using :Destroy on a reused janitor silently breaks the next cycle because the object becomes unusable. Using :Cleanup on a per-entry janitor leaks the janitor table itself. Match the method to the ownership model.

searchDocs.title: Keyed-collection pattern​
searchDocs.content: When managing a dynamic set of entries (workbenches, junk pickups, registered engines, etc.), give each entry its own Janitor stored under a predictable key:  -- Type annotation (Luau) type Entry = { model: Model, cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, } local registry: { [string]: Entry } = {} local function register(id: string, model: Model) local entry: Entry = { model = model, cleaner = Janitor.new(), } entry.cleaner:Add(model, "Destroy") entry.cleaner:Add(model.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child) -- ... end), "Disconnect") registry[id] = entry end local function unregister(id: string) local entry = registry[id] if entry then entry.cleaner:Destroy() -- per-entry → Destroy registry[id] = nil end end   The pattern guarantees that removing an entry also disconnects every signal and destroys every instance that entry owns, with no possibility of leaking a handle.

searchDocs.title: Singleton exception​
searchDocs.content: Top-level controller connections that live for the full session do not need a Janitor. If the connection is created once at script root and never torn down (for example, Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded at the top of a client controller), wrapping it in a Janitor adds overhead with no benefit.  Only use a Janitor when the scope can end before the script does.

searchDocs.title: Quick TweenService equivalence​
searchDocs.content: -- TweenService (do NOT use this in client code) TweenService:Create(target, TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), goals):Play() -- MotionMaster equivalent MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Fire-and-forget shorthand. Creates a TweenObject, calls :Play(), and returns it.  MotionMaster.Play(frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Returns a TweenObject for manual lifecycle control. Does not start playback.  local tween = MotionMaster.Create(label, { TextTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.5 }) tween:Play()   TweenObject methods​  Method	Description:Play()	Start or restart from current elapsed position. :Pause()	Pause; preserves elapsed time. :Resume()	Resume a paused tween. :Cancel()	Pause and reset to the start value. :Reverse()	Flip direction mid-playback; elapsed time mirrors continuously. :Scrub(alpha)	Jump to a normalized position [0, 1] without playback. :Destroy()	Disconnect all connections and release memory. :OnStep(cb)	Register cb(alpha, dt) — fires every frame. Chainable. :OnComplete(cb)	Register cb() — fires when the tween finishes. Chainable. :OnDestroy(cb)	Register cb() — fires on :Destroy(). Chainable.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Spring(target, prop, config)​
searchDocs.content: Creates and starts a SpringDriver that follows a dynamically updated endpoint. Supports number and Vector3 properties only.  local driver = MotionMaster.Spring(frame, "Position", { Omega = 18, Zeta = 1.0 }) driver:SetTarget(newPosition) -- update the goal at any time   SpringDriver config fields: Omega (natural frequency), Zeta (damping ratio),MaxSubsteps, FixedDt.  SpringDriver methods: :SetTarget(v), :OnStep(cb), :IsSettled(eps?), :Stop(), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.fromPreset(presetName, target, prop)​
searchDocs.content: Instantiate a SpringDriver from one of the 16 named presets.  local driver = MotionMaster.fromPreset("UIPanel", frame, "Position")   Named spring presets​  Category	PresetsUI / Interface	UIPanel, UIFade, UIBounce, UISnap Camera	CameraFollow, CameraLag, CameraShake Gameplay objects	RecoilCritical, RecoilSnappy, DoorBouncy, DoorStiff, WeaponSway, JiggleBone Environment	HoverStabilizer, SpringPlatform, HeavyGate

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Sequence(config)​
searchDocs.content: Chain or parallelize TweenObjects. Returns a Sequence.  local seq = MotionMaster.Sequence() -- serial (default) seq:Add(tweenA) seq:Add(tweenB, 0.1) -- 0.1 s gap before tweenB seq:Play() local par = MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true }) -- all at once par:Add(tweenC) par:Add(tweenD) par:OnComplete(function() print("all done") end) par:Play()   Sequence methods: :Add(tweenObj, delay?), :Play(), :OnComplete(cb), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, config)​
searchDocs.content: Moves target (a BasePart) along an arc-length-reparameterized Catmull-Rom spline.controlPoints is an array of BasePart instances or Vector3 values (minimum 2).  local tween = MotionMaster.SplineMove(cart, { p0, p1, p2, p3 }, { Duration = 4, Model = "EaseInOutCubic", ConstantSpeed = true, -- default true for SplineMove }) tween:Play()   Returns a TweenObject (same lifecycle methods as above).

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.PivotMove(model, targetCFrame, config)​
searchDocs.content: Animates a Model via :PivotTo(), preserving relative part offsets. Accepts a CFrame as the goal.  local tween = MotionMaster.PivotMove(door, openCFrame, { Duration = 0.8, Model = "DoorBouncy", -- preset name accepted for Model field }) tween:Play()
