searchDocs.title: State machine​
searchDocs.content: Two orthogonal booleans select the mode (aim wins over free-look):  aimMode — set exclusively via Signals.RequestShootingCamera. No player keybind activates aim directly; only tools (GrabHook on equip), weapons (WeaponController on weapon equip/unequip), and systems (PlacementClient on build-mode entry) fire this signal.freeLookMode — toggled by LeftAlt via ContextActionService:BindAction("ToggleCameraMode", ...); inert while aimMode is true (the action sinks the input but silently no-ops).  Two more flags participate in lookActive()/applyState() without being a "mode" of their own:  guiRequestsMouse — set by Signals.RequestMouseIcon; frees and shows the cursor and suspends mouse-look, independent of freeLookMode.buildModeActive — set by Signals.OnBuildModeChanged; see Placement camera.  On every CharacterAdded a new MotionMaster.Spring (offsetSpring) is created bound to a plain { Value, Parent = true } holder (offsetHolder), not directly to humanoid.CameraOffset — the spring drives offsetHolder.Value, which the render step then feeds into CameraRig.Compose as the screen-relative offset. The spring's Omega/Zeta come from CameraConfig; it is destroyed on CharacterRemoving. The render step runs at Camera priority via RunService:BindToRenderStep("Camera", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, ...).  CameraRig.luau is pure, stateless camera math shared by nothing else today but kept separate so it's independently testable/reviewable: CameraRig.ClampPitch(pitch, minPitch, maxPitch) is a math.clamp wrapper, and CameraRig.Compose(focusPosition, offset, yaw, pitch, distance, lookOffset) rotates offset into the yaw/pitch look frame, adds it to focusPosition, then backs the camera off distance studs along the look vector, returning (cameraCFrame, adjustedFocusPosition).  lookOffset is an optional Vector2 (radians, X=pitch, Y=yaw) that rotates the look direction about the fixed camera position — the camera position and the occlusion raycast (which fires before Compose runs) are untouched. CameraConfig.ShootingLookAngle and CameraConfig.ThirdPersonLookAngle supply this in degrees; CameraController blends the active mode's angle with a second MotionMaster.Spring, mirroring offsetSpring/offsetHolder exactly (retargeted on the same applyState() calls, created/destroyed alongside it).

searchDocs.title: Modes​
searchDocs.content: Locked third-person (default) — mouse always drives yaw/pitch (lookActive() returns true); MouseBehavior = LockCenter, cursor hidden; the HRP lerps to face humanoid.MoveDirection while moving.  Aim — entered only via Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true). Shoulder offset (CameraConfig.ShootingOffset) via the offset spring, reticle visible, mouse locked+hidden, HRP lerps to face the camera's yaw (not movement direction) so aiming and strafing look correct together. Exiting fires Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled(false).  Free-look — toggled by LeftAlt when not aiming. Cursor is freed and shown (MouseBehavior = Default), but lookActive() only returns true while the right mouse button is held — a faithful port of the old default-camera free-look behavior. HRP still lerps to face movement direction, same as locked third-person.  Signals.RequestMouseIcon is orthogonal to all three modes: while guiRequestsMouse is true (and aimMode is false), the cursor is freed/shown and lookActive() returns false regardless of freeLookMode, for GUIs (e.g. the workbench) that need a clickable cursor.

searchDocs.title: Sensitivity​
searchDocs.content: sensitivity is read once at startup from SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") and kept live-updated by subscribing to Signals.OnSettingChanged (filtering on key == "CameraSensitivity"). Every frame that lookActive() is true, raw pixel delta from UserInputService:GetMouseDelta() is scaled by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity before being applied to yaw/pitch. See Settings for how CameraSensitivity is defined, synced, and persisted.

searchDocs.title: Zoom​
searchDocs.content: Scroll wheel input adjusts targetDistance by CameraConfig.ScrollZoomStep per notch, clamped to [CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance, maxDistanceForMode()]. maxDistanceForMode() returns ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance in aim mode or ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance otherwise.

searchDocs.title: Occlusion​
searchDocs.content: Each frame, a raycast runs from the offset focus point toward the desired camera position, excluding the local character. If it hits, occludedDistance is clamped to hitDistance - CameraConfig.BoomBuffer (floored at CameraMinZoomDistance); otherwise it's just targetDistance. A separate renderDistance is lerped toward occludedDistance at BoomSmoothingSpeed * dt per frame and is what actually gets passed to CameraRig.Compose — targetDistance (the zoom-wheel target) is never touched by occlusion, so releasing from behind a wall smoothly zooms back out to the player's chosen distance.

searchDocs.title: Placement camera​
searchDocs.content: While build mode is active, PlacementCameraController.client.luau — a separate script, not part of CameraController — takes exclusive ownership of the camera:  Sets Camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable and drives Camera.CFrame every frame: fixed height and pitch above the player (PlacementConfig.TopDownHeight/TopDownPitch), locked to whatever yaw the player was facing when build mode started.Eases into and out of the top-down angle via an exponential chase-lerp (alpha = 1 - exp(-CameraTransitionSpeed * dt)) rather than snapping instantly. On exit it eases toward an approximation reconstructed from the camera's offset relative to the player's HumanoidRootPart at the moment build mode was entered, then hands off to Enum.CameraType.Custom once that blend has settled (EXIT_SETTLE_TIME, ≈0.2s at the default speed).Fades any PlacementConfig.OccluderTag-tagged parts (e.g. roofs) to OccluderTransparency for the duration, restoring their original transparency on exit.Fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true) on PC (gated on UserInputService.MouseEnabled and UserInputService.KeyboardEnabled) so CameraController frees and shows the cursor instead of locking it to screen-center — needed because the placement camera doesn't rotate with mouse movement, so mouse.UnitRay (used by PlacementClient for the placement raycast) needs a cursor that can move to aim anywhere.Restores Enum.CameraType.Custom immediately (hard cut, no blend) on CharacterRemoving — a backstop in case build mode didn't cleanly exit first, e.g. character death.  CameraController and PlacementCameraController both own the Scriptable camera at different times, and coordinate via Signals.OnBuildModeChanged. CameraController subscribes to this signal and sets buildModeActive accordingly; its render step's first statement is if buildModeActive then return end, a full no-op for the duration of build mode. On resume it reasserts camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable (guarded — only writes if not already Scriptable).

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Aim mode is signal-only There is no keybind that activates aimMode directly. Only external systems fire Signals.RequestShootingCamera. If a new tool or system needs to enter aim mode it must fire this signal — do not read or write the aimMode local directly.  Accepted ~0.2s exit-stutter PlacementCameraController's own exit-blend keeps writing camera.CFrame for EXIT_SETTLE_TIME (≈0.2s at the default CameraTransitionSpeed) after build mode ends, before it hands CameraType back to Custom. Since CameraController resumes its own Scriptable writes immediately when OnBuildModeChanged(false) fires, there is a brief window where both scripts could write Camera.CFrame on the same frame-ish timescale, producing a small visual stutter. This is a known, accepted residual limitation — eliminating it would require either a new cross-module "exit fully settled" signal or coupling CameraController to PlacementCameraController's private EXIT_SETTLE_TIME constant, judged not worth it for a sub-quarter-second cosmetic blip.  Do not use TweenService to animate the camera offset. offsetSpring is a MotionMaster.Spring driver bound to offsetHolder.Value; bypassing it will produce conflicting states and the spring will override any TweenService tween on the next frame.CameraController and PlacementCameraController both write Camera.CameraType/Camera.CFrame and must never run their write paths in the same frame — that's what buildModeActive exists to prevent. Do not add a third script that writes Camera.CFrame without wiring it into this same coordination.The offset spring is re-created on every CharacterAdded and destroyed on CharacterRemoving. Holding a reference to an old spring past the character death will produce a dangling driver pointing at a destroyed Humanoid.freeLookMode frees and shows the mouse cursor, but does not re-enable humanoid.AutoRotate; CameraController always drives HRP facing itself and sets humanoid.AutoRotate = false unconditionally (skipped entirely while humanoid.Sit is true).A GUI that needs a clickable cursor fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon:Fire(true); while set (and not aiming) the camera holds MouseBehavior = Default and shows the cursor, restoring LockCenter on Fire(false).CameraSensitivity changes take effect on the very next frame via Signals.OnSettingChanged — there is no need to re-fetch SettingsClient.Get manually or restart the character.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant U as UserInputService participant C as CameraController participant Cam as Camera participant Ext as External systems U->>C: GetMouseDelta() (every RenderStep, when lookActive()) C->>C: yaw/pitch -= delta * MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity C->>C: CameraRig.ClampPitch(pitch, MinPitch, MaxPitch) U->>C: MouseWheel scroll C->>C: targetDistance = clamp(targetDistance + step, MinZoom, maxDistanceForMode()) loop RunService RenderStep "Camera" (Priority = Camera) C->>C: if buildModeActive then return end C->>C: reassert CameraType = Scriptable C->>C: occlusion raycast -> renderDistance lerped toward occludedDistance C->>Cam: CameraRig.Compose(subject, offset, yaw, pitch, renderDistance, lookOffset) C->>C: lerp HRP facing toward camera yaw (aim) or move direction end Ext->>C: Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true/false) C->>C: aimMode = value; applyState() C->>C: offsetSpring/angleSpring retarget; MouseBehavior; reticle visible C-->>Ext: Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled(aimMode) U->>C: LeftAlt (non-aim only) C->>C: freeLookMode toggles; applyState() Ext->>C: Signals.RequestMouseIcon(visible) C->>C: guiRequestsMouse = visible; applyState() Ext->>C: Signals.OnBuildModeChanged(isActive) C->>C: buildModeActive = isActive (render step becomes no-op while true)

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BattlePassController.client.luau	One-line bootstrap: calls BattlePassClient.Init() once on join Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/BattlePassClient.luau	GUI-agnostic read-model: TierView descriptors, Claim/PromptPremium commands Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/BattlePassState.luau	Pure season/level/tier math shared by server and client Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/BattlePassResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum returned by ClaimBattlePass Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/BattlePassManager.luau	Owns the PlayerBattlePass profile: EXP, premium, claim, rollover, replication Server	src/ServerScriptService/BattlePassSystemLoader.server.luau	Calls BattlePassManager.Initialize() once per server (place-agnostic) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luau	STORE_NAME, SUBSCRIPTION_ID, MAX_LEVEL, ExpPerLevel, Tiers, SeasonOverrides  Packets: ReqClaimBattlePass, ReqPromptPremium, BattlePassStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnQuestRewardGranted (consumed, from QuestManager), OnBattlePassItemGranted, OnBattlePassLevelUp (produced) — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Season math​
searchDocs.content: The season index is a calendar-month index, not a rolling 30-day window: BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) = year*12 + (month-1), computed in the timezone defined by BattlePassConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset (a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset, pre-launch default US Eastern -5*3600, mirroring QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). Being a fixed offset, month boundaries do not track daylight saving.  BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now: number): number BattlePassState.seasonExpiresAt(now: number): number -- unix ts of the 1st of next month   The underlying day math (daysFromCivil) is a pure-integer proleptic-Gregorian calculation (Howard Hinnant's algorithm), so client and server always agree without relying on os.date's host timezone handling. seasonExpiresAt is sent to the client so it can drive a countdown without any client-side date math. The server re-checks online players for a rollover — and refreshes cached premium status — every BattlePassConfig.ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS (default 60s).  The quest system's Season scope (see Quests — Season quests) uses this exact same seasonIndex as its period key, so a battle pass season and its season-long quests always start and end together.

searchDocs.title: EXP earning​
searchDocs.content: There is no gameplay source that awards battle pass EXP directly. Instead, BattlePassManager subscribes to Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — fired by QuestManager.grantReward on every quest reward grant, manual claim or rollover auto-sweep alike — and reads the optional Reward.BPExp field off the quest's reward table:  Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Connect(function(player, reward) if reward and reward.BPExp then BattlePassManager.AddExp(player, reward.BPExp, "Quest") end end)   Any quest can feed the pass just by adding a BPExp number to its Reward table — no new signal or wiring per quest. The shipped pool leans on this for its dedicated Scope = "Season" quests: three quests (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance), the whole set active for the entire month, each paying 0 coins/exp but 3000 BPExp. Regular Daily/Weekly quests also carry smaller BPExp amounts (e.g. JunkDailyA pays 200), so ordinary questing keeps the pass moving too.

searchDocs.title: Tier track and bulk claim​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[level] (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL, MAX_LEVEL = 60) is a { Free: Reward?, Premium: Reward? } pair. A Reward is either { Type = "Coins", Amount } or { Type = "Item", ItemId } (an empty ItemId = "" marks a milestone slot not filled in yet).  Tier kind	Free row	Premium rowRegular	Coins = 100 + (level-1)*10	Coins = 150 + (level-1)*15 Milestone (15/30/45/60)	Chunkier 500-coin bonus	Empty accessory Item slot (to be filled)  BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] sparsely shadows the base Tiers entry for one specific season only (e.g. swap in a different accessory for one month while keeping the rest of the track the same):  BattlePassState.tierReward(level: number, row: "Free" | "Premium", seasonIndex: number): BattlePassConfig.Reward?   tierReward resolves the override first, falling back to the base table, and is used identically by the server (grant) and client (display) so the two can never disagree.  Level is derived, never stored:  BattlePassState.levelFromExp(exp: number): number BattlePassState.progress(exp: number): (level: number, expIntoLevel: number, expForNextLevel: number)   levelFromExp walks MAX_LEVEL down to 1 and returns the highest level whose cumulative EXP threshold (BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel — a flat per-level number or a { [level]: number } table) is met; progress additionally returns the two extra values for a progress bar (both 0 once level >= MAX_LEVEL).  There is only one claim entry point:  function BattlePassManager.ClaimBattlePass(player: Player): (boolean, number, number, number, number)   Packets.ReqClaimBattlePass (no payload) invokes it, and it bulk-banks every unlocked-but-unclaimed reward across both rows in one call — there's no per-tier claim. Premium-row rewards are only granted while the player is currently premium. Claimed flags (ClaimedFree[level] / ClaimedPremium[level]) are set before the grant executes (the same idempotent-guard pattern as QuestManager.ClaimQuest), so a re-entrant call finds nothing outstanding and returns NOTHING_TO_CLAIM rather than double-paying. Returns (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted); counts/coins are 0 on any failure. Result codes (BattlePassResultCodes): OK = 0, NO_PROFILE = 1, NOTHING_TO_CLAIM = 2.

searchDocs.title: Premium (subscriptions)​
searchDocs.content: Premium is never persisted — it's live-resolved from MarketplaceService:GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync(player, SUBSCRIPTION_ID) and cached in-memory per session (premiumCache, keyed by Player). The cache is (re)populated at three points:  Trigger	WhyJoin	Before the first sweep/replicate MarketplaceService.PromptSubscriptionPurchaseFinished	The prompt closing doesn't guarantee a successful purchase, so status is always re-resolved rather than assumed Periodic rollover tick	Bounds staleness to ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS  resolvePremium yields (a web call), so it only ever runs from spawned contexts — never from the synchronous AddExp/ClaimBattlePass paths, which read the cache. On a false→true transition (a fresh subscribe), onPurchaseFinished retroactively runs a sweep granting the Premium row for every tier already reached this season, so buying mid-season immediately feels rewarding instead of only affecting future tiers. Packets.ReqPromptPremium (no payload, server-initiated) calls MarketplaceService:PromptSubscriptionPurchase — the prompt must originate server-side.  While BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID = "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs are skipped entirely — resolvePremium short-circuits to false and ReqPromptPremium returns false without calling MarketplaceService, so pre-launch never spams errors for a subscription that doesn't exist yet.

searchDocs.title: Rollover and auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: ensureCurrent (called at the top of AddExp and ClaimBattlePass, on join, and on the rollover tick) compares the profile's stored SeasonIndex against BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time()). On a mismatch it first auto-grants every reached-but-unclaimed tier from the old season (Free always; Premium only if the player is currently premium) via the same sweep helper the manual claim uses — nothing earned is lost just because a player never opened a claim UI before the month rolled. It then resets Exp = 0, ClaimedFree = {}, ClaimedPremium = {}, and advances SeasonIndex to the current value. Coins and items already granted by the sweep persist wherever they live (the coin wallet, a future inventory) — only the pass's own tier/EXP bookkeeping resets.

searchDocs.title: Item seam​
searchDocs.content: Item-type rewards fire Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted(player, itemId) — a seam with no consumer this cycle, reserved for a future inventory/accessory system. Milestone tiers ship with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = ""); granting one is a no-op (no signal fires) and logs a one-time warning (warnedEmptyItem, a module-level flag) reminding a developer to fill BattlePassConfig with a real asset before launch. The claimed flag is still set even for an empty slot, so it's marked claimed and never re-offered.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, same shape as QuestClient/PerkClient. It caches the authoritative BattlePassStateSync snapshot and derives per-tier views using the same BattlePassState.tierReward the server grants from:  export type TierView = { Level: number, FreeReward: BattlePassConfig.Reward?, PremiumReward: BattlePassConfig.Reward?, IsUnlocked: boolean, IsFreeClaimed: boolean, IsPremiumClaimed: boolean, }   Exposes GetProgress (level, expIntoLevel, expForNextLevel), GetLevel, IsPremium, GetSeasonExpiresAt, GetTiers (all 60, in order), GetClaimableSummary (a preview of what a Claim() would bank right now — counts + coin total, without actually claiming), and fire-and-forget Claim() / PromptPremium() commands. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires BattlePassClient and subscribes to Changed.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved battle pass data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward with ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no OnBattlePassItemGranted signal (nothing to grant) but still flips the claimed flag, so the player never sees it offered again even after you fill in a real ItemId later — fill milestone slots before launch.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant QM as QuestManager (server) participant BPM as BattlePassManager (server) participant Client as BattlePassClient (owning client) Note over QM: quest CLAIM or auto-sweep QM->>QM: grantReward() — CoinManager.AddCoins, XPManager.AddXP QM->>BPM: Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, quest.Reward) alt reward.BPExp present BPM->>BPM: AddExp(player, reward.BPExp) — ensureCurrent() first BPM->>BPM: profile.Data.Exp += amount alt derived level rose BPM->>BPM: Signals.OnBattlePassLevelUp:Fire(player, newLevel) end BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (season, exp, level, progress, claimed, premium, expiresAt) end Note over Client,BPM: bulk CLAIM Client->>BPM: ReqClaimBattlePass() BPM->>BPM: ensureCurrent(); sweep(1..level) — Free always, Premium if isPremium BPM->>BPM: claimed flags set BEFORE grant (idempotent guard) BPM-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted) BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: BattlePassConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luauPlaybook: Tune Battle PassQuestConfig.Quests[id].Reward.BPExp (optional) is how a quest feeds the pass; Scope = "Season" quests are the dedicated monthly source — see Tune Quests.  Field	EffectSTORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved battle pass progress. SUBSCRIPTION_ID	The Roblox subscription id whose active status unlocks Premium. Empty ("") disables premium entirely and skips the subscription APIs. ResetTimezoneOffset	Fixed seconds-from-UTC offset the calendar-month boundary is measured in (mirrors QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). No DST tracking. MAX_LEVEL	Top tier of the track (60). ExpPerLevel	BP EXP required per level — a flat number or a { [level]: number } table. ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS	How often the live server tick re-checks online players for a season rollover and refreshes cached premium status. Tiers[level].Free / .Premium	Base reward per tier per row. SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level]	Sparse per-season tier reward shadowing, keyed by BattlePassState.seasonIndex.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CannonController.client.luau	Mount prompt, movement lock, ballistic arc preview, fire input, CannonFired/ExplosionAt FX Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CannonGuiController.client.luau	Programmatic heat-bar HUD, shown only while manning a cannon Server	src/ServerScriptService/CannonServer.server.luau	Placed-cannon discovery, mount/fire validation, authoritative shell simulation, damage application, heat/overheat Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CannonConfig.luau	Ballistics, mount range, overheat params, part/sound keys, EnemyShip tag  Packets: ReqMountCannon, ReqFireCannon, CannonFired (impact reuses ExplosionAt) — see Networking MapSignals: OnCannonMounted — local-client-only bridge from mount state to CannonGuiController

searchDocs.title: Placement → mount → fire​
searchDocs.content: Place — the cannon is a placeable (PlaceableItems/Cannon + PlaceableTools/Cannon). Placement, stash, and move are inherited from Placement; the placed clone lands in workspace/PlacedObjects with a PlaceableName = "Cannon" attribute (an attribute, not a CollectionService tag — a tag would also match client build-mode ghosts).Mount — CannonController attaches a ProximityPrompt to each placed cannon's MountPromptPart. Triggering it sends ReqMountCannon(model); the server validates proximity (MountRange) and single-occupancy and records the gunner. Mounting locks the gunner's WalkSpeed/JumpPower and shows a ballistic arc preview raycast client-side every RenderStepped.Fire — input sends ReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir). The server re-derives occupancy, cooldown, and overheat, then simulates the shell from its own muzzle CFrame with a gravity Acceleration via FastCast2 (the same pattern WeaponServer uses for rockets). On impact it applies Damage * (1 + CannonDamageBonus) via CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts CannonFired (muzzle flash + barrel snap + sound) and ExplosionAt (boom + explosion sound).

searchDocs.title: Occupancy​
searchDocs.content: A live occupant (character alive) blocks takeover by another player; a dead occupant's seat can be taken over. CannonController releases the player's previous cannon when mounting a new one and dismounts on death, on the cannon being stashed/destroyed (model.AncestryChanged), or on pressing X. Signals.OnCannonMounted fires the model (or nil on dismount) so CannonGuiController can show/hide its heat bar without touching the network layer.

searchDocs.title: Overheat​
searchDocs.content: Each shot adds CannonConfig.HeatPerShot; heat decays at HeatDecayPerSec on a server Heartbeat. Reaching MaxHeat locks the cannon for OverheatLockTime. Heat (0–1) and Overheated are attributes on the placed Model (no packet) — CannonGuiController reads them directly every RenderStepped, eases the displayed percentage, and plays the overheat sound once on the transition into overheat.

searchDocs.title: Server authority & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Occupancy, cooldown, overheat-lock, and shell origin are all re-validated server-side; the server fires from its own muzzle, so a forged client-side origin or aim direction cannot help. CannonDamageBonus is read server-side from the server-written PartyPerkBuffs folder on every shot — unforgeable. Faction routing is inherited from CombatService.ApplyAOE, so EnemyNPC rigs must be in a hostile faction to take player damage. Direction is sanity-checked (rejects NaN/near-zero magnitude) before the cast fires.

searchDocs.title: EnemyShip forward seam​
searchDocs.content: CannonServer.applyCannonAOE damages Humanoids via CombatService.ApplyAOE and, in the same call, decrements a numeric Health attribute on in-radius models tagged CannonConfig.ENEMY_SHIP_TAG ("EnemyShip") with linear falloff to the blast edge, destroying the model at Health <= 0. This is inert until a future enemy-ship spec tags ships; it requires no change to the perk hook.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: OnCannonMounted is not in the shared signals map The signal is real (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau) and fires from CannonController on mount/dismount, consumed only by CannonGuiController — it is a pre-existing gap in Signals Map, not a code issue.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Cl as CannonController participant Sv as CannonServer participant Gui as CannonGuiController Cl->>Sv: ReqMountCannon(model) Sv->>Sv: validate not-occupied-by-live-player, proximity <= MountRange Sv-->>Cl: accepted: boolean Cl->>Cl: lock WalkSpeed/JumpPower, start arc-preview raycast loop Cl->>Gui: Signals.OnCannonMounted(model) loop while mounted, on fire input Cl->>Sv: ReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir) Sv->>Sv: validate occupant, cooldown, overheat; sanity-check direction Sv->>Sv: FastCast2 shell from own muzzle CFrame + Gravity Acceleration Sv->>Sv: heat += HeatPerShot; lock if heat >= MaxHeat Sv-->>Cl: (accepted, remainingCooldown) Sv->>Cl: CannonFired(gunner, muzzlePos, velocity) - all clients Note over Sv: on shell impact Sv->>Sv: applyCannonAOE - CombatService.ApplyAOE + EnemyShip Health falloff Sv->>Cl: ExplosionAt(center, radius, "Cannon") - all clients end Sv->>Sv: Heartbeat: heat -= HeatDecayPerSec*dt; release overheat lock when elapsed Cl->>Sv: ReqMountCannon(nil) - dismount (death, X key, or cannon destroyed) Cl->>Gui: Signals.OnCannonMounted(nil)

searchDocs.title: API surface​
searchDocs.content: Function	DescriptionDamageNumbers.Show(worldPosition, amount, styleName?)	Spawn a number. No-op if disabled or amount <= 0. styleName defaults to Config.DefaultStyle; unknown names fall back to it. DamageNumbers.SetEnabled(value)	Toggle spawning of new numbers (for a settings menu). In-flight numbers finish. DamageNumbers.IsEnabled()	Returns the current toggle state. DamageNumbers.Init()	Build + pre-warm the pool. Idempotent; lazy-runs on first Show otherwise. Called once by DamageNumbersController.

searchDocs.title: Spawn and animate​
searchDocs.content: Each number is a pooled BillboardGui (GenericPoolInstance). On Show it acquires an entry, applies a named style (color/font/size/stroke from DamageNumberConfig.Styles), offsets the spawn by a random jitter so rapid hits fan out, then animates with MotionMaster:  Pop — UIScale.Scale from Pop.StartScale to 1 with a back-out overshoot curve (a custom backOut alpha function, since MotionMaster's built-in easing has no overshoot).Rise — BillboardGui.StudsOffsetWorldSpace.Y drifts up by Rise.Height over Lifetime.Fade — text/stroke transparency animates to 1 during the final Fade.Duration seconds of Lifetime.  One Janitor per live number owns the pop/rise/fade tweens and a delayed fade thread. When the rise tween completes, the Janitor is destroyed and the part returns to the pool (resetEntry hides it for reuse). The billboard uses world-space (Scale) sizing, so numbers shrink with camera distance and cull past Billboard.MaxDistance.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant D as Damage source (predicted hit / server broadcast handler) participant N as DamageNumbers participant P as GenericPoolInstance D->>N: Show(worldPosition, amount, styleName?) N->>N: enabled? amount > 0? else no-op N->>P: RetrieveObject(jittered CFrame) N->>N: apply style (color/font/size/stroke) N->>N: MotionMaster.Play (Pop, Rise, Fade via delayed thread) Note over N: Rise:OnComplete N->>N: Janitor:Destroy() (cancel tweens/fade thread) N->>P: InsertObject(part) - resetEntry hides it for reuse

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/DisruptionController.client.luau	Shows the non-blocking countdown notice; no input is blocked Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/DisruptionCoordinator.luau	Trigger funnel (automatic + manual) and the full drain sequence Server	src/ServerScriptService/DisruptionSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — calls DisruptionCoordinator.Initialize(), runs in both the lobby and gameplay places Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/PersistenceRegistry.luau	Force-save registry; gameplay managers register a flush callback in their Initialize Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/DisruptionConfig.luau	Lobby place id, timing budgets, admin command, player-facing copy  Packets: DisruptionBegan — see Networking MapSignals: none — DisruptionController reuses Signals.RequestNotification for the countdown toast, but the disruption system itself defines no signals

searchDocs.title: Trigger​
searchDocs.content: Two paths funnel into the same drain sequence, guarded by an isDisrupting flag so it only ever runs once:  Automatic — game:BindToClose fires beginDisruption("shutdown") when Roblox shuts the server down.Manual — DisruptionCoordinator.BeginMaintenance(reason) (an admin chat command, DisruptionConfig.ADMIN_COMMAND, default "!maintenance") publishes to every server in the universe via MessagingService, so a fleet-wide maintenance drain doesn't require restarting each server individually. If the publish fails, it falls back to draining just the local server.

searchDocs.title: Drain sequence​
searchDocs.content: beginDisruption(reason) runs in order, all timed from a single drainStart:  Notify — broadcasts the DisruptionBegan packet (reason, NOTICE_SECONDS); each client shows a non-blocking countdown via Signals.RequestNotification.Wait — task.wait(NOTICE_SECONDS) so players can read the notice.Flush — PersistenceRegistry.FlushAll(FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) force-saves every registered profile. profile:Save() is used, not EndSession(), so players stay connected until the teleport.Teleport — TeleportService:TeleportAsync(LOBBY_PLACE_ID, …) per player, retried up to TELEPORT_RETRIES times. Skipped entirely in Studio or when LOBBY_PLACE_ID <= 0 — players then disconnect with data already saved.Drain-wait — yields until the server empties or MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS (measured from drainStart, so steps 1–4 eat into the same budget rather than adding to it) elapses; leftover players disconnect with data already saved. Skipped in Studio, where no real teleport occurs and waiting would hang every Studio "Stop" for the full budget.  A player joining mid-drain is caught by Players.PlayerAdded: they immediately receive DisruptionBegan and a teleport attempt.

searchDocs.title: Correctness​
searchDocs.content: ProfileStore session-locking is the backstop: even if a save is in flight when a player reaches the lobby server, that server's StartSessionAsync waits for the old lock to release, so no data is lost. The explicit flush in step 3 just tightens the window and gives a "saved before we move you" ordering — it is not the only thing preventing data loss.

searchDocs.title: Force-save registrants​
searchDocs.content: PersistenceRegistry.Register(flush) is called from each manager's Initialize; FlushAll invokes every registered callback with a shared timeout. Current registrants: CoinManager, ArmorManager, PerkManager, QuestManager, SettingsManager, XPManager, BattlePassManager.

searchDocs.title: Known limitation​
searchDocs.content: Direct teleport to the lobby can bounce if the lobby place is also restarting during a universe-wide Roblox update. The reliable path is the manual maintenance command, which drains the gameplay place while the lobby stays up.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS bounds the whole sequence, not just the final wait Notice + flush + drain-wait together must fit under Roblox's ~30s BindToClose budget. Tuning NOTICE_SECONDS or FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS eats into the same budget rather than adding to it.  LOBBY_PLACE_ID = 0 skips the teleport, not the flush While unset, the coordinator still runs the full notify/flush sequence — players just disconnect afterward instead of being teleported. Data is not lost, but there's no lobby to land in.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Trig as Trigger (BindToClose / admin command) participant Co as DisruptionCoordinator participant Pers as PersistenceRegistry participant Cl as DisruptionController Trig->>Co: beginDisruption(reason) Co->>Co: isDisrupting guard (idempotent) Co->>Cl: DisruptionBegan(reason, NOTICE_SECONDS) - all clients Cl->>Cl: Signals.RequestNotification countdown Co->>Co: task.wait(NOTICE_SECONDS) Co->>Pers: FlushAll(FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) Pers->>Pers: profile:Save() per registered manager alt LOBBY_PLACE_ID > 0 and not Studio Co->>Co: TeleportAsync(LOBBY_PLACE_ID, player) per player, retry TELEPORT_RETRIES else Studio or unset Co->>Co: warn - players disconnect, data already flushed end Co->>Co: wait until server empties or MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS (from drainStart)

searchDocs.content: Config module: DisruptionConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/DisruptionConfig.luau  Field	Default	EffectLOBBY_PLACE_ID	game-specific PlaceId	Teleport target. 0 skips the teleport (players disconnect after flush); also skipped automatically in Studio. NOTICE_SECONDS	4	Seconds between showing the notice and starting the drain FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS	6	Max seconds to wait for PersistenceRegistry.FlushAll() before proceeding anyway MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS	25	Hard cap on the whole sequence; must stay under Roblox's ~30s BindToClose budget TELEPORT_RETRIES	3	Retries per player on TeleportInitFailed MESSAGING_TOPIC	"EndlessJourney_Disruption"	MessagingService topic for fleet-wide manual maintenance fan-out ADMIN_USER_IDS	{}	UserIds allowed to invoke the manual maintenance chat command ADMIN_COMMAND	"!maintenance"	Chat command (case-insensitive, first word) that starts manual maintenance NOTIF_TYPE	"warn"	Notification type passed to Signals.RequestNotification DEFAULT_MESSAGE / REASON_MESSAGES	—	Player-facing copy, keyed by trigger reason (shutdown / maintenance)

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CoinController.client.luau	Bridges CoinStateSync to Signals.OnCoinsChanged Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CoinManager.luau	Sole wallet authority: profile lifecycle, earn/spend/read API, replication Server	src/ServerScriptService/CoinSystemLoader.server.luau	Calls CoinManager.Initialize() once per server (place-agnostic) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CoinConfig.luau	STORE_NAME, STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE  Packets: CoinStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnCoinsChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The PlayerCoins profile stores a single value, Coins. STORE_NAME ("PlayerCoins") and the UserId key are identical in every place of the universe, so the lobby and gameplay share one DataStore record; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. Wallet bounds (STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE) live in CoinConfig.

searchDocs.title: Wallet API (server-authoritative)​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager is the sole authority — every mutation goes through one of these four functions:  function CoinManager.GetCoins(player: Player): number function CoinManager.AddCoins(player: Player, amount: number, reason: string?) function CoinManager.DeductCoins(player: Player, amount: number): boolean function CoinManager.RefundCoins(player: Player, amount: number)   AddCoins scales the amount by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus (math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))), a 1-coin floor) and clamps to MAX_BALANCE; reason is an optional source tag logged server-side only. DeductCoins is atomic — it returns false with no mutation on amount <= 0, a missing profile, or insufficient funds. RefundCoins returns an exact amount and is not scaled by CoinGainBonus, so unlock→respec cycling can't mint coins.

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: Source	Call	NotesQuest rewards	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, quest.Reward.Coins, "Quest:"..questId)	Paid by QuestManager's shared grantReward path (manual claim or rollover auto-grant). Scaled by CoinGainBonus. Battle Pass tiers	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, reward.Amount, "BattlePassFree:"..level) / "BattlePassPremium:"..level	Paid by the bulk-claim sweep for Coins-type tier rewards. Scaled by CoinGainBonus. Premium row is gated by a Roblox subscription (BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID), not a one-time purchase — that gates the reward row, it does not grant coins directly.  Quests also pay an EXP reward via XPManager.AddXP — a separate system with its own profile. See Quests and Battle Pass.

searchDocs.title: Sinks​
searchDocs.content: Sink	Call	NotesPerk unlock	CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, perk.UnlockCost)	PerkManager.UnlockPerk pays a perk's one-time unlock cost. See Perks — Unlock gate. Respec refund	CoinManager.RefundCoins(player, perk.UnlockCost)	PerkManager.Respec reverses the unlock cost exactly (not scaled by CoinGainBonus) for every perk it re-locks.  Perk unlocking is the first implemented sink; quest/battle-pass rewards are the first implemented sources.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Every successful mutation fires CoinStateSync(balance: U32) to the owning client. CoinController re-fires it as Signals.OnCoinsChanged(balance) for a future coin HUD. There is no client→server packet — earning and spending are fully server-driven.

searchDocs.title: Not yet built​
searchDocs.content: Additional earning sources (gameplay-session completion), additional sinks (a shop + purchase packet), and the coin HUD are separate systems that would call the CoinManager API — they are not part of the wallet module.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant QM as QuestManager / BattlePassManager (server) participant PM as PerkManager (server) participant CM as CoinManager (server) participant Client as CoinController (owning client) QM->>CM: AddCoins(player, amount, reason) — scaled by CoinGainBonus PM->>CM: DeductCoins(player, cost) / RefundCoins(player, cost) — exact, unscaled CM->>CM: clamp to MAX_BALANCE; profile.Data.Coins mutated CM->>Client: CoinStateSync(balance) Client->>Client: Signals.OnCoinsChanged:Fire(balance)

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemySpawner.luau	Group registry, point selection, jitter, placement, SpawnWave/SpawnAt/ResetGroup, drip-feed scheduling, global cap Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyWave.luau	WaveHandle factory: Janitor-backed enemy tracker, OnCleared signal, Despawn/Destroy Server	src/ServerScriptService/EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau	Thin bootstrap: calls EnemySpawner.Init() once per server Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau	Stateless ground/wall/spacing validator; returns a ground-snapped position on success Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau	OnEnemySpawned signal registration Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau	Archetype registry, global tuning constants, Verification.* knobs; validates model names against ServerStorage.EnemyAssets at load  Packets: none — spawned Models replicate to clients via native Roblox replicationSignals: OnEnemySpawned — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Authoring contract​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnGroup. A spawn group is a Model in the DataModel tagged with the CollectionService tag EnemySpawnGroup. The group's identity is its GroupName string attribute; if the attribute is absent the model's .Name is used. The tag is all that is required — any Model (a pirate ship, an outpost building, a plain Part wrapped in a Model) becomes a valid group. Because spawn-point attachments are descendants of the group Model, their .WorldPosition moves automatically with the model's CFrame — placing the group on a moving ship and calling SpawnWave places enemies relative to the ship's current pose at spawn time, with no code changes.  EnemySpawnPoint. Each spawn point is an Attachment tagged EnemySpawnPoint, parented anywhere beneath the group model. Two optional per-point attributes control selection and jitter:  Attribute	Type	Default	PurposeRadius	number	archetype DefaultRadius → DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	Radial jitter disc radius in studs Weight	number	1	Base selection weight before the cumulative-inverse falloff  Points are visually editable in Studio — add, remove, or move an attachment and the spawner picks it up immediately (the cache is rebuilt on first use per group, and a CollectionService.GetInstanceRemovedSignal listener invalidates the group if the root model is untagged or removed).  EnemyAssets folder. Enemy Model assets live in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/. Each child Model must have a Humanoid (authoritative stats are applied at spawn time from the archetype config, but the Humanoid must exist for health/death tracking) and a PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart (used for pivot placement and SpawnVerification spacing tests). At module load, EnemySpawnerConfig validates every archetype's Model name against EnemyAssets children and emits a warn for any missing model. Building before art is ready is fully supported: register a placeholder dummy (any Model with a Humanoid) under the expected name.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner is a server-only module. Call EnemySpawner.Init() once from the system loader before using the rest of the API.  EnemySpawner.Init()   Called once by EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau at server start. Creates workspace.ActiveEnemies if absent and wires the group-cache invalidation listener.  EnemySpawner.SpawnWave(groupName: string, request: SpawnRequest): WaveHandle   Spawns request.count enemies across the named group's points using the selection algorithm below. composition is either a single archetype name ("PirateGrunt") or a weighted table ({ PirateGrunt = 3, PirateBrute = 1 }) — rolled per enemy. If request.interval > 0, spawns are staggered in a task.spawn loop (drip-feed); the WaveHandle is returned immediately and OnCleared waits for both all spawns to be attempted and all registered enemies to die. If request.seed is set, the internal Random is re-seeded for deterministic reproduction.  export type SpawnRequest = { count: number, composition: string | { [string]: number }, interval: number?, -- seconds between spawns; nil/0 = all at once seed: number?, -- optional deterministic RNG seed }   EnemySpawner.SpawnAt(groupName: string, pointName: string, archetypeName: string): Model?   Direct escape hatch: place exactly one archetype at the named attachment (matched by Attachment.Name), still subject to verification. Returns the placed Model or nil if verification fails after MaxRetries or the point/archetype is not found.  EnemySpawner.ResetGroup(groupName: string)   Clears the group's cumulative per-point spawn counts. Call this at the start of each new encounter so point weighting begins fresh. Deaths do not reduce a point's count; only ResetGroup does.

searchDocs.title: Per-enemy spawn algorithm​
searchDocs.content: For each enemy in a wave the spawner runs:  Select a point — weighted random over the group's EnemySpawnPoint attachments. Effective weight is point.Weight / (cumulativeCount + 1) ^ WeightFalloff, where cumulativeCount is the number of enemies spawned from that point this encounter. A point with count 0 carries its full base weight; counts are per-encounter (ResetGroup resets them, enemy deaths do not).Jitter — candidate position = point world position + a uniform random offset within a disc of the point's Radius on the XZ plane. The disc uses sqrt(NextNumber()) * radius so the distribution is uniform over the area rather than biased toward the centre.Verify — the candidate is passed to SpawnVerification with the archetype's body size, an ignore list containing the group model and the ActiveEnemies folder, and the current list of living enemies.Retry-then-skip — steps 2–3 repeat up to Verification.MaxRetries times. If no valid position is found, the enemy is skipped (a warn is emitted) and the wave continues. The wave never hard-fails; it never places a broken enemy.Place — if the global cap (GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES) is already met, the enemy is skipped with a warn. Otherwise the archetype Model is cloned from ServerStorage.EnemyAssets, archetype stats are applied (Humanoid.MaxHealth/Health/WalkSpeed), the model is tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC if archetype.Faction == "Friendly"), pivoted to the verified ground-snapped CFrame, parented to workspace.ActiveEnemies, and the point's cumulative count is incremented. The spawned model is registered with the wave handle, EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) is called (see Enemy Combat), and Signals.OnEnemySpawned fires with the placed position and archetype name.  SpawnVerification​  SpawnVerification (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau) is a stateless pure-geometry validator with no server-only dependencies. It lives in SharedModules so it is independently testable and reusable from a future client-side preview; all v1 callers are server-side.  SpawnVerification.Verify( candidate: Vector3, bodySize: Vector3, ignoreList: { Instance }, livingEnemies: { Model } ): VerifyResult -- { ok: boolean, position: Vector3?, reason: string? }   Checks run cheapest-first with short-circuit on failure:  Ground below — workspace:Raycast straight down from candidate + (0, 2, 0) up to MaxGroundDrop studs, excluding ignoreList. No hit returns { ok = false, reason = "void" }. On hit, the Y position snaps to the floor: snapped.Y = hit.Position.Y + bodySize.Y / 2.Clear of walls / headroom — workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox of HeadroomSize centred on the snapped position, excluding ignoreList. Any solid collidable part returns { ok = false, reason = "blocked" } — this catches both embedded-in-wall and under-floor cases.Spacing — if any model in livingEnemies has its pivot within MinEnemySpacing studs of the snapped position, returns { ok = false, reason = "crowded" }.  A successful check returns { ok = true, position = snapped }.

searchDocs.title: WaveHandle lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: SpawnWave returns a WaveHandle backed by a Janitor. The handle tracks every spawned enemy's death and removal.  export type WaveHandle = { OnCleared: Signal<()>, -- fires once: all enemies dead AND wave complete GetAlive: (self) -> number, -- count of enemies still alive GetEnemies: (self) -> { Model }, -- list of enemies still alive Despawn: (self) -> (), -- destroy remaining enemies + remove from tracking Destroy: (self) -> (), -- Despawn + Janitor teardown }   Each spawned enemy's Humanoid.Died and AncestryChanged (for despawn-without-death) are connected via the handle's Janitor. OnCleared fires once when the alive count reaches zero and the wave has been marked complete (all drip-feed spawns attempted) — killing enemies before the last drip-feed slot fires will not trigger OnCleared prematurely.  local wave = EnemySpawner.SpawnWave("PirateShip", { count = 6, composition = { PirateGrunt = 3, PirateBrute = 1 }, interval = 0.5, }) wave.OnCleared:Connect(function() resumeEncounter() end)   Despawn lets an orchestrator abort a wave early (encounter cancelled, train resumes) and cleanly destroy remaining enemies; calling it when all enemies are already dead is a safe no-op. Destroy implies Despawn and additionally tears down the Janitor.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnGroup model: select any Model in the workspace (pirate ship, outpost, or a plain wrapped Part), tag it EnemySpawnGroup via the Studio Tag Editor, and optionally set a GroupName string attribute (defaults to model.Name).  EnemySpawnPoint attachments: under the group model, insert one or more Attachment instances, tag each EnemySpawnPoint, and optionally add Radius/Weight number attributes. The attachment's Studio position is the spawn point's world-space origin at runtime; move attachments freely, the spawner reads .WorldPosition live at spawn time.  EnemyAssets folder: create a folder named EnemyAssets inside ServerStorage; each child Model needs a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart/HumanoidRootPart, and its name must match the Model field in the corresponding EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes entry. Minimum viable setup for testing before art is ready: insert a default Roblox Dummy into ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/ and rename it to match an archetype (e.g. PirateGrunt) — the archetype validation warning clears and SpawnWave clones the dummy.  Collision and combat wiring​  No additional Studio wiring is required for collision passthrough or combat. Spawned enemies are tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC), and both services detect the tag automatically via CollectionService.GetInstanceAddedSignal:  NpcCollisionService places their parts in the Character collision group (registered and matrixed by CollisionGroups) so players and thrown charges (WeaponProjectile) pass through them — the non-player sibling of CharacterCollisionService, which does the same for player characters.CombatService.ApplyToModel resolves them via Factions so weapon hits deal damage.  placeAt also calls EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) immediately after placement, arming any archetype that has a matching EnemyCombatConfig profile so it paths toward and fires at players. Archetypes with no profile entry are unaffected — Register no-ops and they remain passive. See Enemy Combat for the full director, weapon, and config breakdown.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: WaveHandle OnCleared requires both conditions OnCleared fires only when the alive count is zero AND all drip-feed spawns have been attempted (MarkComplete called internally). In an instant wave (interval = 0) this means OnCleared can fire during SpawnWave itself, before it returns, if every enemy was skipped. Always set up OnCleared connections before calling SpawnWave; do not assume it is deferred.  Cumulative counts survive across waves; ResetGroup does not run automatically. If SpawnWave is called a second time without resetting, previously-used points start at a cumulative disadvantage. For repeating encounter patterns (waves 1, 2, 3…), decide explicitly whether to reset between waves or let cumulative weighting carry across the full encounter.  GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES counts workspace.ActiveEnemies children. If enemies are not parented there (e.g. manually cloned models outside the spawner), they do not count toward the cap, which may allow over-cap situations. Always spawn enemies through EnemySpawner.  SpawnVerification is in SharedModules but is server-only in v1. It has no server-only dependencies so it can be reused from a future client-side preview (e.g. displaying valid spawn zones in a director tool), but in v1 all calls happen server-side via EnemySpawner. Do not call it on the client in production without auditing the ignoreList/livingEnemies arguments for client-visible data.  Archetype validation warns but does not error. If a model is missing from EnemyAssets at load time, EnemySpawnerConfig emits a warn but does not error; the spawner also warns (and skips the enemy) at spawn time if the model is still absent. Register placeholder models early to keep the Output clean during development.

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: Off-screen spawn preference — an additional weighting term in the point-selection step that demotes EnemySpawnPoints currently inside any player's camera frustum, so enemies appear from behind cover or the edge of vision.Reachability pre-check — PathfindingService:CreatePath from the verified candidate to the nearest player, rejecting candidates in sealed-off areas. This is the deferred line-of-sight check in SpawnVerification, done properly.Encounter director — a layer above the spawner that scales count/composition/interval by wave number, player count, or Tech Tree progress. The spawner stays a dumb placement service; the director owns escalation and pacing.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant O as Orchestrator participant ES as EnemySpawner participant SV as SpawnVerification participant EB as EnemyBrain participant W as WaveHandle O->>ES: SpawnWave(groupName, { count, composition, interval, seed? }) ES->>W: create WaveHandle (Janitor-backed) ES-->>O: return WaveHandle (immediately) loop per enemy (drip-fed if interval > 0) ES->>ES: select point (cumulative-inverse weight) ES->>ES: jitter position within point Radius ES->>SV: Verify(candidate, bodySize, ignoreList, livingEnemies) SV-->>ES: { ok, position, reason } alt verification failed after MaxRetries ES->>ES: skip enemy (warn) else global cap reached ES->>ES: skip enemy (warn) else success ES->>ES: clone from EnemyAssets, apply stats, tag EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPC ES->>W: register spawned Model (tracks Died/AncestryChanged) ES->>EB: EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) ES->>ES: Signals.OnEnemySpawned:Fire(position, archetypeName) end end ES->>W: MarkComplete (all drip-feed spawns attempted) Note over W: OnCleared fires once alive count = 0 AND MarkComplete W-->>O: OnCleared

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: EnemySpawnerConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau  All tuning lives in this module. It is accessible from both client and server; the archetype validation block is guarded by RunService:IsServer() since ServerStorage is inaccessible on the client.  Field	Default	EffectGLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES	40	Hard cap on total active enemies across all groups. Exceeding the cap skips spawns with a warn. Lower temporarily to verify the cap in Studio. DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	6	Fallback jitter disc radius (studs) when neither the point Radius attribute nor the archetype DefaultRadius is set. WeightFalloff	1.0	Exponent k in effectiveWeight = baseWeight / (count + 1) ^ k. At 1.0 weight halves each time a point is used. Raise to flatten selection (less adaptive); lower toward 0 to disable cumulative penalisation. Verification.MaxGroundDrop	25	Maximum downward raycast distance (studs) to find a floor below the candidate. Verification.HeadroomSize	Vector3.new(3, 6, 3)	Box dimensions used for the wall/headroom overlap check. Should match or slightly exceed the tallest enemy body. Verification.MinEnemySpacing	4	Minimum distance (studs) between a new candidate and any already-living enemy pivot. Verification.MaxRetries	8	Number of jitter re-rolls before an enemy is skipped with a warn. Archetypes	(see below)	Per-archetype table: Model (child name in EnemyAssets), Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction ("Enemy" / "Friendly"; defaults to "Enemy").  EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes = { PirateGrunt = { Model = "PirateGrunt", Health = 100, WalkSpeed = 14, DefaultRadius = 6 }, PirateBrute = { Model = "PirateBrute", Health = 300, WalkSpeed = 10, DefaultRadius = 4 }, }   Adding a new archetype: add an entry here, create the corresponding Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/, and the spawner picks it up at next load — no code changes elsewhere are needed. Note that an archetype also needs a matching entry in EnemyCombatConfig.Profiles to be armed; see Enemy Combat → Studio setup.
