searchDocs.title: Point economy​
searchDocs.content: Each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point.Available points = playerLevel - sum(spent in that pool), computed by PerkState.available — points are never stored directly.Points cannot go negative; the pool is floored at 0.Respec costs nothing and returns all points in the chosen pool — it also re-locks each unlocked perk in that pool and refunds its UnlockCost in coins (see Unlock gate).Points carry across places because PerkManager uses the same DataStore key (PlayerPerks) everywhere in the universe.  PerkConfig.Perks is the single tuning surface: 12 perk declarations with Category, BuffKey, PerLevel, MaxLevel, DisplayName, Description, display Order, an optional ValueKind, and per-perk UnlockCost/UnlockLevel.  ValueKind controls GUI effect-string formatting in PerkClient.effectFor: nil/"percent" (the default, every perk except Net Cast) renders Description's %d as the whole-percent bonus (floor(PerLevel * level * 100 + 0.5)); "count" (Net Cast only) renders %d as a raw total, baseline 1 plus the bonus (1 + floor(PerLevel * level + 0.5)) — so "Grab up to %d junk at once" reads "Grab up to 3 junk at once" at level 2 (1 baseline + 2 bonus), not a percent.

searchDocs.title: Unlock gate​
searchDocs.content: Every perk declares a one-time UnlockCost (coins) and UnlockLevel (player level) gate in PerkConfig. A perk with both 0 is a free starter, auto-unlocked: PlayerHP (Vitality) and JunkRarity (Salvage Luck).  Unlock is permanent: it persists on the PlayerPerks profile as an Unlocked map ({ [perkId]: boolean }), alongside PerkLevels and a PerkSchemaVersion guard.  function PerkManager.UnlockPerk(player: Player, perkId: string): (boolean, number)   UnlockPerk validates with PerkState.canUnlock (order: UNKNOWN_PERK → ALREADY_UNLOCKED → LEVEL_REQUIRED → NOT_ENOUGH_COINS), deducts UnlockCost via CoinManager.DeductCoins, and replicates. Allocating a point on a locked perk returns PERK_LOCKED (PerkState.canAllocate checks unlocked[perkId] before the level/point checks). The frozen enum (PerkResultCodes) shared by server and client:  Code	Value	MeaningOK	0	Success NO_PROFILE	1	Profile not loaded UNKNOWN_PERK	2	Perk id not in PerkConfig AT_MAX_LEVEL	3	Already at MaxLevel NO_POINTS	4	No available points in that pool PERK_LOCKED	5	Perk not yet unlocked ALREADY_UNLOCKED	6	Unlock requested twice LEVEL_REQUIRED	7	Below UnlockLevel NOT_ENOUGH_COINS	8	Below UnlockCost  Unlocking a perk changes no buffs (its level is still 0), so PerkManager.UnlockPerk does not fire Signals.OnPerkStateChanged; PerkEffectsDispatcher is untouched by an unlock.  Migration: the first load after this shipped wipes all existing PerkLevels/Unlocked once (clean slate — derived points return automatically), guarded by PerkSchemaVersion < 1 (then set to 1) so it fires exactly once per profile. migrateAndSeed re-seeds starters immediately after so play never begins with zero unlocked perks.  Respec (PerkManager.Respec) fully resets the chosen pool: it clears PerkLevels and Unlocked for every perk in that pool, refunds each unlocked perk's UnlockCost via CoinManager.RefundCoins — an exact, un-inflated refund, not scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus (unlike CoinManager.AddCoins) — then re-seeds free starters so the pool isn't left fully locked.  The client-facing PerkView descriptor (PerkClient.luau) carries IsUnlocked, UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and MeetsUnlockLevel fields. PerkClient.Unlock(perkId) is the fire-and-forget command that sends ReqUnlockPerk; reconciliation arrives via the next PerkStateSync.

searchDocs.title: Party-max resolution​
searchDocs.content: Party perks (Salvage Luck, Fuel Efficiency, Thrift, Shield Capacity, Heavy Ordnance) apply to the entire server, but only the highest level held by any single player is active. If Player A has Salvage Luck 6 and Player B has Salvage Luck 3, the server resolves at 6. PerkEffectsDispatcher recomputes the max on every allocate, respec, player join, and player leave.

searchDocs.title: Buff contract​
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher is the sole writer of the buff folders — every other system reads, never writes. It listens to Signals.OnPerkStateChanged, PlayerAdded, and PlayerRemoving, then calls publishPersonal (per-player attributes) and publishParty (server-max across all players). It also bridges Junk Rarity to Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier, which JunkService already consumes. PerkManager.GetPerkLevels(player) returns the live reference PerkEffectsDispatcher reads from.  Folder	Scope	Updated whenReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>	Personal, per-player	On allocate/respec, player join, player leave ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs	Party, server-max	Same as above  Attribute keys match PerkConfig.BuffKey:  Perk	BuffKey	Value formula	ConsumerVitality	HPBonus	0.04 * level	HealthManager Regeneration	RegenBonus	0.10 * level	HealthManager Quick Reel	ReelSpeedBonus	0.05 * level	GrabHook Power	DamageBonus	0.03 * level	WeaponServer (chokepoint: scaledDamage, applied after headshot multiplier, all 5 player-attack sites) Fortune	CoinGainBonus	0.05 * level	CoinManager.AddCoins (math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) — 1-coin minimum) Armor	ArmorEfficiency	0.025 * level	HealthManager (chokepoint: applyDamageInternal) — see Armor damage mitigation Net Cast	NetCapacityBonus	1 * level (max level 4)	GrabHook / JunkService — hook capacity = 1 + NetCapacityBonus (server-clamped to GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetMaxTargets = 5). See GrabHook. Salvage Luck	JunkTierRarityBonus	0.08 * level	JunkService (via ApplyTierMultiplier) Efficiency	FuelEfficiencyBonus	0.04 * level	TrainFuelManager drain multiplier — stacks multiplicatively with ResearchBuffs.FuelEfficiency (see Research Bench) Thrift	WeaponCostReduction	0.03 * level	(deferred — no weapon cost mechanic exists; declared in config, intentionally unwired) Shield Capacity	TrainShieldBonus	0.05 * level	TrainShieldManager.recomputeMax — multiplicative on top of BASE_SHIELD + ResearchBuffs.MaxHP; see Train Shield Heavy Ordnance	CannonDamageBonus	0.06 * level	CannonServer (applyCannonAOE, applied as Damage × (1 + CannonDamageBonus) per shot). Consumed by the Cannon system at the server shell-damage line.  Perks marked (deferred) have no planned consumer yet.

searchDocs.title: Armor damage mitigation​
searchDocs.content: Crafted armor (see ArmorConfig / ArmorManager) publishes a per-player ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction — the base fraction of incoming damage removed by the player's current armor tier. The Armor perk does not reduce damage on its own; it's an efficiency multiplier on that base. HealthManager.applyDamageInternal reads both per hit and computes:  reduction = clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75)   amount is then scaled by (1 - reduction) as the final step before subtracting from health. With no armor (tier 0 → base 0) the perk contributes nothing. Because the attacker's DamageBonus is already applied upstream in WeaponServer, attacker bonus and defender mitigation multiply independently: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - reduction). Coverage is every path routed through CombatService/HealthManager (Melee/Bullet/AOE and NPC hits); damage written directly to Humanoid.Health bypasses the sink and is not mitigated (see Health).

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: PerkClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (owns no GUI). It caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot (perkLevels, unlocked, personalAvailable, partyAvailable, playerLevel) and watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder. Queries return PerkView descriptors via GetPerks/GetActivePerks/GetAvailablePoints/GetPerk. Commands: optimistic-prediction Allocate/Respec/CanRespec, plus Unlock(perkId) (no optimistic coin prediction — the server owns the balance; the next PerkStateSync reflects success or failure), and a Changed signal fired on every snapshot update.  "Active" is category-aware: a Personal perk is active at the player's Level > 0; a Party perk is active at its server-wide ActivePartyLevel > 0. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires PerkClient and subscribes to Changed, exactly like QuestClient/BattlePassClient. PerkController.client.luau is the one-line bootstrap that calls PerkClient.Init() once on join so the data layer is warm before any GUI opens.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Points are derived, not stored Available points are never stored directly — only PerkLevels, Unlocked, and PerkSchemaVersion persist. Available points = level - spent. Never add a separate stored point counter — it will desync.  Party perk levels shown in the GUI are per-player, not the resolved active level The + button and level display in the Party tab show how many points this player has invested. The (active N) sub-label shows the server-resolved max. Both are expected: a player at level 3 in a party where someone else is at level 7 sees Lv 3/10 (active 7).  PerkEffectsDispatcher must run before PerkManager on join PerkEffectsDispatcher seeds its folder at boot. PerkManager fires OnPerkStateChanged after profile load, which triggers a republish. The ordering is correct because both are ServerScriptService scripts and PerkManager.Initialize() is called from PerkSystemLoader, which yields on ProfileStore:StartSessionAsync before firing the signal.  HPBonus subscription attaches once at join HealthManager subscribes to the HPBonus attribute change in PlayerAdded, not CharacterAdded. If PerkBuffs/<UserId> does not exist at join time (the dispatcher hasn't seeded yet), the subscription is skipped for that session. In practice the dispatcher seeds synchronously at boot, so the folder exists before any player's PlayerAdded fires normally.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Client as PerkController (client) participant Manager as PerkManager (server) participant Dispatcher as PerkEffectsDispatcher (server) Note over Manager: JOIN Manager->>Manager: profile loaded (migrateAndSeed: one-time wipe + seedStarters) Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, personalAvail, partyAvail, playerLevel) Client->>Client: perkLevels / unlocked / available updated; repaint() Manager->>Dispatcher: publish personal buffs (0s); publishParty() Note over Client,Manager: UNLOCK Client->>Manager: ReqUnlockPerk(perkId) Manager->>Manager: UnlockPerk — canUnlock (level+coins) then DeductCoins then Unlocked[perkId]=true Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync (no OnPerkStateChanged fired — buffs unchanged) Manager-->>Client: (success, reasonCode) Note over Client,Manager: ALLOCATE Client->>Client: optimistic level++, avail--; repaint() Client->>Manager: ReqAllocatePerk(perkId) Manager->>Manager: AllocatePoint — canAllocate then mutate Manager->>Dispatcher: Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, ...) Client->>Client: reconcile to authoritative state; repaint() Dispatcher->>Dispatcher: publishPersonal(player); publishParty() Manager-->>Client: (success, reasonCode) Note over Manager: LEVEL UP Manager->>Manager: XPManager level increases; Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp:Fire(player, newLevel) Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, personal+1, party+1, newLevel) Client->>Client: repaint() — new points visible

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleShared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau	Client bind/unbind helper + poof visual renderer; auto-connects poof broadcast on the client side Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau	Server validation, atomic claim, Tool grant, BroadcastPlaceablePoof dispatch Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau	PlaceableActions sub-table with all tuning knobs  Packets: ReqStashPlaceable, ReqMovePlaceable, BroadcastPlaceablePoof — see Networking MapSignals: OnPlaceableStashed, OnPlaceableMoved — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Binding the GUI​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActions.bind(model, gui) wires MoveButton and StashButton into the packet system and returns a Binding with a single Unbind() method. On success the module fires Signals.OnPlaceableMoved or Signals.OnPlaceableStashed so other systems can react without polling. Call binding:Unbind() when the GUI closes — failing to unbind leaves the Janitor alive and button listeners connected to a GUI that may already be gone.

searchDocs.title: Poof visual​
searchDocs.content: The poof handler is client-only and lives in PlaceableActions.luau. On receiving BroadcastPlaceablePoof it clones the matching model from ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems, strips scripts/collisions/shadows from the clone, parents it to workspace.PlaceablePoofs, then runs a parallel MotionMaster.Sequence that shrinks every BasePart to near-zero while fading it out. The clone self-destructs when the sequence completes.

searchDocs.title: Server validation and atomic claim​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActionsServer owns the OnServerInvoke handlers for ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. It runs, in order: a per-player cooldown check (os.clock), an ancestry check (model.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects), an attribute check (PlaceableName attribute on the model), a tool template check (ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools/<Name>), and a proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance). The atomic claim pattern (model.Parent = nil followed by a re-read) prevents two simultaneous requests from granting the same item twice. The handler returns boolean — false on any failed check, true on full success.

searchDocs.title: Move and the revert store​
searchDocs.content: On a successful Move, the handler also calls PlaceableRevertStore.Set(player, { cframe = cframe, placeableName = placeableName, tool = newTool }), recording the item's original CFrame under the granted tool instance. This lets the build-mode cancel (RequestPlacementRevert) revert the item to its original spot if the player presses X without re-placing. The entry is cleared when the player re-places via PlaceItem, when the revert fires and consumes it, or when the player leaves the server.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Three requirements must all be present A placeable supports Stash/Move only when all three of the following exist simultaneously: A Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> (already required for placement).A Tool template in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with a PlaceableName attribute set to the same name string.ImageButton instances named exactly MoveButton and StashButton somewhere inside the GUI that PlaceableActions.bind is called with. Either the Tool or a button may be omitted, but the missing one will log a warning and that action will be silently unavailable to the player. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, the server returns false and nothing is destroyed — no item is lost — but the player gets no feedback.  The server proximity check (MaxActionDistance) is a second guard independent of the ProximityPrompt range. Keep them in sync when tuning the in-world prompt.Stash/Move discards all per-instance state on the placed model. The granted Tool is always a fresh clone from the template. If per-instance state matters, snapshot attributes before the action reaches the server.Any nearby player can stash any placement — ownership is not tracked. Add per-instance owner attributes and an ownership check in handleAction if griefing becomes a concern.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as PlaceableActions (client) participant S as PlaceableActionsServer participant O as All clients P->>C: Press MoveButton / StashButton C->>S: ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable S->>S: Cooldown check (per-player, os.clock) S->>S: Ancestry check (model.Parent == PlacedObjects) S->>S: Attribute check (PlaceableName) S->>S: Tool template check (PlaceableTools/<Name>) S->>S: Proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance) S->>S: Atomic claim (model.Parent = nil, race guard) S->>S: Clone Tool -> player.Backpack alt Move S->>S: humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) end S->>O: BroadcastPlaceablePoof(cframe, placeableName, isMove) S->>S: model:Destroy() + record cooldown timestamp O->>O: PlaceableActions plays shrink tween + SFX

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PlacementClient.client.luau	Build-mode controller: tool equip detection, ghost Heartbeat loop, input wiring, observer ghost rendering Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PlacementCameraController.client.luau	Owns the camera during build mode (top-down view + occluder fade) Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau	Server authority: ghost relay, anti-exploit validation, item finalization Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlacementSystem.luau	Ghost model lifecycle, placement calculation, and validity checking; used by both client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau	All tuning constants for the placement system  Packets: ClientToggleGhost, ServerToggleGhost, ClientUpdateGhost, ServerUpdateGhost, PlaceItem, RequestPlacementRevert — see Networking MapSignals: OnBuildModeChanged, OnBuildValidityChanged, OnPlacementModeChanged, OnGhostLockChanged, RequestRotate, RequestPlacementConfirm, RequestPlacementCancel, RequestGridModeToggle, RequestGhostLockToggle, RequestShootingCamera — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Entering build mode​
searchDocs.content: On tool equip, PlacementClient creates one PlacementSystem instance (grid size 2, tag BuildArea), calls SetBuildMode(true) and SetGhostModel(template), and fires ClientToggleGhost. It also fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) to disable the aim camera. PlacementCameraController then takes over: it switches to CameraType.Scriptable (near-top-down, follows the player, yaw locked at entry), eases in and out of the angle rather than snapping, and fades any PlacementOccluder-tagged geometry. See Camera.

searchDocs.title: Tracking the ghost​
searchDocs.content: A Heartbeat loop rate-limited to GhostUpdateHz (default 20 Hz) raycasts, calls UpdateGhostPosition, and fires ClientUpdateGhost with the resulting CFrame. Signals.OnBuildValidityChanged fires whenever validity changes so UI and audio can react. Grid/free toggle, rotation, confirm, cancel, and ghost-lock are all driven by signals wired to BuildModeGuiController. The client listens for ServerToggleGhost / ServerUpdateGhost and calls SetOtherGhost to render other players' ghost previews.

searchDocs.title: Server relay and validation​
searchDocs.content: PlacementServer relays ClientToggleGhost to other players after confirming the item name exists in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems, and relays ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame type-checked) to other players. On PlaceItem it enforces a per-player cooldown (PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 s), character/tool guards, ray-origin distance (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50 studs), final-position distance (MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60 studs), and collision validity — all using an isolated PlacementSystem instance with a ServerStorage-parented ghost that is never replicated.

searchDocs.title: Finalizing a placement​
searchDocs.content: On success, the server clones the template, calls finalizeModel (makes CollisionBox invisible + non-collidable, visual parts opaque, and tags the CollisionBox with PlacementObstruction so future placements collide with it), parents it to workspace/PlacedObjects, destroys the player's tool, and broadcasts ghost-clear to all clients. If the placer's own character ends up overlapping the placed item, they are teleported horizontally clear of it, clamped to stay within the same BuildArea part.

searchDocs.title: Shared PlacementSystem​
searchDocs.content: PlacementSystem handles ghost model lifecycle, grid-snap vs free-placement position calculation, collision-box derivation, obstruction validity check, and other-player ghost rendering. IS_CLIENT guards prevent Texture and TweenPlus calls from running on the server; SetBuildMode is client-only (it creates grid Texture instances on build area parts), while the server sets IsBuildMode = true directly. Each PlaceItem request creates an isolated PlacementSystem instance — this is intentional, so concurrent requests from different players cannot corrupt shared state. Never cache a server-side PlacementSystem across requests.

searchDocs.title: Cancelling build mode​
searchDocs.content: Pressing X (configurable via PlacementConfig.CancelKey) or the on-screen Cancel button (mobile) fires Signals.RequestPlacementCancel. Both paths reach the same cancelPlacement function in PlacementClient, which snaps build-mode visuals off and sends a RequestPlacementRevert RemoteFunction call to the server. Escape is intentionally not used — Roblox reserves it for the in-game menu.  The server checks PlaceableRevertStore to determine the outcome:  Session type	OutcomeFresh placement (item was never placed before)	Server returns false → client calls humanoid:UnequipTools() and the tool returns to the Backpack Move session, original spot is free	Server re-places the item at its original CFrame, destroys the tool, returns true → item reverts, no unequip needed Move session, original spot is occupied	Server returns false → client falls back to unequip  See Placeable Actions for how a Move session records the revert entry.

searchDocs.title: Own-character exclusion and push-out​
searchDocs.content: PlacementSystem.new(buildAreaTag, gridSize, excludePlayer)'s third argument controls which player's Character is skipped by BuildObstructionFilter. The client always passes its own Players.LocalPlayer; the server passes the requesting player for both PlaceItem and RequestPlacementRevert. Other players' characters are never excluded — they still block placement as before. Because every other player's character remains an obstruction, no other player can ever end up overlapping a freshly finalized item, so pushCharacterClearOfBox in PlacementServer only needs to act on the requesting/reverting player.  The platform it clamps into comes from PlacementSystem.LastBuildAreaPart, populated only by CalculatePlacement's raycast (the PlaceItem path). The revert path re-places at a stored CFrame and never calls CalculatePlacement, so LastBuildAreaPart is nil there; PlacementServer falls back to findBuildAreaBelow, a dedicated helper that raycasts straight down from the revert position (filtered to the BuildArea tag, the same idiom CalculatePlacement uses) to resolve the platform part.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit — do not relax the server thresholds MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60, and PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 in PlacementServer are the primary defences against remote placement exploits. Raising these values substantially would allow clients to place items anywhere in the world or spam unlimited items.  Model structure is required. Every entry in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems must have a CollisionBox (BasePart) child. Without it, PlacementSystem warns and falls back to bounding-box collision, which can cause floating or incorrect validity checks.Obstruction is tag-driven, not folder-driven. Build placement only avoids a volume if it is tagged PlacementObstruction. Placed items are tagged automatically on their CollisionBox by finalizeModel. Any static world model that placement must respect (e.g. TrainShieldGeneratorPlaceholder, ResearchBenchPlaceholder) must have a CollisionBox BasePart tagged PlacementObstruction by hand. Tag the CollisionBox part only, never the whole model — sibling sub-models like TrajectoryPoints would otherwise become map-wide placement blockers.CollisionBox must not be named RootPart or tagged PlacementIgnore. Those names cause the part to be treated as invisible/non-collidable in the ghost.SetBuildMode must only be called on the client. Calling it on the server would create Texture instances in workspace and replicate them to all clients.Ghost relay is observer-only. The GhostModels folder and its contents exist only on the client; the server's validity check correctly skips that folder for this reason.Cutscene and combat gates (isInCutscene, isInCombat) in PlacementClient are not yet wired to any external system — they are TODO integration points.  Server-side security thresholds live in PlacementServer.server.luau as local constants (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE, PLACE_COOLDOWN) — treat them as sensitive anti-exploit values.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as PlacementClient participant S as PlacementServer participant O as Other clients P->>C: Equip tool C->>C: SetBuildMode(true), SetGhostModel(template) C->>S: ClientToggleGhost S->>S: Validate itemName exists S->>O: ServerToggleGhost (relay) loop Heartbeat @ GhostUpdateHz C->>C: CalculatePlacement (raycast) + CheckValidity C->>S: ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame) S->>S: Type-check CFrame S->>O: ServerUpdateGhost (relay) end P->>C: Click / confirm signal C->>S: PlaceItem (origin, dir, rotation, mode) S->>S: Cooldown + distance checks S->>S: Isolated PlacementSystem: CalculatePlacement + CheckValidity S->>S: Clone + finalizeModel -> workspace/PlacedObjects S->>C: Destroy tool S->>O: ServerToggleGhost(false)

searchDocs.title: Data model and curve​
searchDocs.content: The profile stores a single value, TotalXP (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are never stored — they're derived from it every time via XPCurve:  XPCurve.xpToNext(level: number): number -- round(CURVE_COEFF * level ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET, 0 at/above MAX_LEVEL XPCurve.levelFromTotal(totalXP: number): number XPCurve.progress(totalXP: number): (level: number, xpIntoLevel: number, xpForNextLevel: number)   Defaults: CURVE_COEFF = 5, CURVE_EXP = 1.5, CURVE_OFFSET = 45, MAX_LEVEL = 100. Total XP to reach level 100 is roughly 204,000. All constants live in XPConfig.

searchDocs.title: Earning (party-shared)​
searchDocs.content: XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every player in the server receives the full award via XPManager.AddPartyXP.  Source	Amount	TriggerDistance	DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK (1) every DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS (5s)	Train is in its "go" state (running, not braked/stalled) — driven off Signals.SetTrainState Kills	KILL_XP (10)	Any EnemyNPC-tagged model's Humanoid.Died (attribution-agnostic)  The train starts braked, so no distance XP accrues before the first un-brake.  function XPManager.AddXP(player: Player, amount: number) function XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number)   Both are no-ops if amount <= 0 or the profile isn't loaded. AddXP fires XPLevelUp and Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp when the level increases, then replicates XPStateSync.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place sharing (lobby ↔ gameplay)​
searchDocs.content: DataStores are universe-wide: both places use the same STORE_NAME and key (tostring(UserId)), so XP/Level are shared automatically, and ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. The lobby place must run XPManager.Initialize() and XPController (for display + clean handoff) but not XPSystemLoader — there are no earners in the lobby. The lobby mirror is a separate deployment, not part of this repo.

searchDocs.title: Not yet built​
searchDocs.content: An XP bar HUD (would consume OnXPChanged), level rewards (hook: XPLevelUp), per-killer attribution, and additional XP sources are all unbuilt.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau	PickupItemReady hover/spin, PickupItemClaimed float-to-hand animation and SFX Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau	RegisterItem, Claim, zone creation, shared-loot zone.Touched handler, _TryMerge, player-disconnect cleanup Server	src/ServerScriptService/DroppedToolService.server.luau	DroppableSurface tag wiring, DescendantAdded drop detection, DropLandingHelper integration Shared	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CollisionGroups.luau	Centralized registrar for every collision group + its collidability matrix Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ProximityPickupConfig.luau	Radius, float duration, hover/spin parameters, merge settings, landing poll constants  Packets: PickupItemClaimed, PickupItemReady, RequestDrop — see Networking MapSignals: none — this system communicates only via Packets and Roblox-native events (AncestryChanged, CollectionService, zone.Touched)

searchDocs.title: Drop path​
searchDocs.content: Pressing Backspace drops the equipped Tool as a direct child of workspace. A workspace.DescendantAdded listener in DroppedToolService catches craft-material Tools parented directly to workspace (the Roblox default Backspace drop path). The handle's CollisionGroup is set to "DroppedMaterial", CanCollide = true, Anchored = false. DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding(handle) then polls every DROP_POLL_INTERVAL (0.1 s) for DroppableSurface contact and a velocity below SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD (0.5 studs/s). On landing, the handle is re-anchored with rotation reset to identity, and ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(tool, metadata, callback, keepModel=true) is called.  DroppedToolService also bootstraps two PhysicsService collision groups: DroppedMaterial (Tools that leave the player's hand) and DroppableSurface (tagged geometry). DroppedMaterial is non-collidable with Default and collidable with DroppableSurface, so dropped items fall through characters and walls but land on tagged floors.

searchDocs.title: Shredder path​
searchDocs.content: ShredderServer.ejectMaterials() anchors each handle at its landing position once its arc completes, then calls ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(handle, metadata, pickupCallback, false) and tags the handle "CraftMaterial" via CollectionService.

searchDocs.title: Registration and claim​
searchDocs.content: ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(part, metadata, callback, keepModel?) is the sole public registration entry. It generates a GUID itemId, sets PickupItemId on the part as an attribute, tags the part "PickupItem", spawns an invisible anchored sphere zone (DEFAULT_RADIUS = 6 studs) in workspace.PickupZones, and fires PickupItemReady to all clients. zone.Touched is the primary claim trigger — any player, shared-loot semantics. Claim(part, player) is the programmatic path used by the shredder's auto-collect loop. Both paths call the same executeClaimAsync, which transitions the record to "Claimed", destroys the zone, broadcasts PickupItemClaimed, then after FLOAT_DURATION (0.25 s) calls the callback and cleans up.  _TryMerge runs MERGE_DELAY (1 s) after registration and absorbs a newly registered handle into a nearby same-type unclaimed survivor within MERGE_RADIUS (2 studs), accumulating Quantity on the survivor. It skips keepModel items — merging would destroy one of the actual inventory objects, so only non-keepModel handles (shredder clones) are eligible.

searchDocs.title: Client hover and claim animation​
searchDocs.content: ProximityPickupController listens to two packets only; it creates no UI and does no proximity math. PickupItemReady applies a HoverEffect (bob + Y-spin) to the handle via a Janitor-managed cleanup handle, and wires AncestryChanged so the effect stops cleanly when the part is destroyed. PickupItemClaimed stops the hover effect, then for the local claimer plays a pickup SFX (via SoundManager.PlaySFXAt using CharacterAnchor to resolve the player's position) and tweens the handle toward the camera using MotionMaster.Play; for all other clients it destroys the handle immediately.

searchDocs.title: Auto-collect​
searchDocs.content: A 0.5 s poll loop in ShredderServer checks each dropped material's age. Once now - SpawnTime >= AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY (45 s), it calls ProximityPickupServer.Claim(mat, owner); if the item is not registered, the callback runs directly and the material is destroyed.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Shared loot — not owner-only Any player who steps into the pickup sphere claims the item, regardless of who dropped it or who the shredder owner was. The auto-collect timer (AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY in ShredderConfig, 45 s) returns unclaimed floor materials to the owner via ProximityPickupServer.Claim. If owner-only pickup is ever needed, the RegisterItem signature must be extended with an owner: Player? parameter and the zone.Touched handler must gate on it (see audit comment PP6 in ProximityPickupServer).  DroppableSurface tagging — no code change needed. Any BasePart tagged "DroppableSurface" in CollectionService is automatically assigned the DroppableSurface collision group at runtime via GetInstanceAddedSignal. To make a new floor or shelf surface catchable, tag it in Studio only.Collision groups are registered in one place. CollisionGroups.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules) is the sole registrar and owns the full collidability matrix. Besides DroppedMaterial/DroppableSurface, it defines Character (every character BasePart, assigned by CharacterCollisionService) and WeaponProjectile (thrown charges, assigned by ServerProjectile). Because characters now live in their own group rather than Default, dropped materials and projectiles both pass through players while still colliding with world geometry. Any system that needs a new group or a new pair rule should edit CollisionGroups.luau, not call PhysicsService directly.keepModel semantics. When keepModel = true (the DroppedToolService path), the registered part is the actual Tool that will go into the player's Backpack — RegisterItem will not destroy it, and the callback sets tool.Parent = player.Backpack. When keepModel = false (the shredder path), the server clones the template, registers the clone, and the callback grants a fresh clone again; the floor handle is destroyed after claim.Zone placement. Pickup zones are parented to workspace.PickupZones (not to the item part). This prevents "trying to set locked parent!" physics warnings when the zone is destroyed at claim time while the item is still mid-float.Late-joining players. ProximityPickupServer has a Players.PlayerAdded listener that replays all currently "Unclaimed" PickupItemReady events to the new client, so items already on the floor will show their hover effect for late joiners.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant DTS as DroppedToolService participant SS as ShredderServer participant PPS as ProximityPickupServer participant C as ProximityPickupController (client) alt Drop path P->>DTS: Press Backspace (Tool -> workspace) DTS->>DTS: DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding (poll 0.1s) DTS->>PPS: RegisterItem(tool, metadata, callback, keepModel=true) else Shredder path SS->>SS: ejectMaterials() arc completes, handle anchored SS->>PPS: RegisterItem(handle, metadata, callback, false) end PPS->>PPS: generate itemId, tag PickupItem, spawn sphere zone PPS->>C: PickupItemReady(part, itemId) C->>C: HoverEffect.Apply (bob + spin) par Zone touch P->>PPS: zone.Touched -> executeClaimAsync and Auto-collect (45s poll) SS->>PPS: Claim(mat, owner) end PPS->>PPS: record.State = Claimed, destroy Zone PPS->>C: PickupItemClaimed(itemId, claimer) C->>C: cleanup hover; if claimer == LocalPlayer, play SFX + float to hand; else destroy PPS->>PPS: after FLOAT_DURATION, callback(player, metadata) -> Backpack

searchDocs.title: Buckets​
searchDocs.content: Each period (Daily or Weekly) rotates a fixed count of quests per category, set by QuestConfig.Counts:  Scope	Personal	PartyDaily	1	2 Weekly	1	1  Personal quests credit only the player who performed the action (e.g. collecting junk). Party quests credit every player in the server for ownerless world events (enemy kills, train distance) — a shared team objective, but the reward is still claimed and paid out per player.

searchDocs.title: Global rotation​
searchDocs.content: The active quest ids for a scope are never stored — they're recomputed deterministically from the period index alone:  QuestState.selectQuests(scope: "Daily" | "Weekly" | "Season", periodIndex: number): { string }   A seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle (distinct large-prime seeds per category so Personal and Party picks don't correlate) runs over the sorted id pool for that scope+category, sliced to Counts, then re-sorted for stable display order. Given the same periodIndex, every machine — client or server, any server in the universe — produces the identical set. Only progress, claimed flags, period indices, and lifetime stats persist on the PlayerQuests profile; the set itself is derived, not saved.

searchDocs.title: Period math​
searchDocs.content: Period indices come from os.time() (UTC), never client input:  Function	FormulaQuestState.dayIndex(now)	floor((now - DailyResetOffset) / 86400) QuestState.weekIndex(now)	floor((now - WeeklyResetOffset) / 604800) QuestState.dailyExpiresAt(now)	Unix timestamp the current daily period ends QuestState.weeklyExpiresAt(now)	Unix timestamp the current weekly period ends  Daily rolls at 00:00 local (QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset); Weekly rolls Monday 00:00 local (QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset, a 4-day base offset — the Unix epoch was a Thursday, so shifting 4 days aligns week starts to Mondays). Both offsets are derived from QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset defining the timezone "midnight" is measured in (pre-launch default US Eastern, -5 * 3600). It's fixed, so it does not track daylight saving; set it to 0 for pure UTC resets (DailyResetOffset = -ResetTimezoneOffset; WeeklyResetOffset = 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset). The expiry functions are sent to the client so it can drive a live countdown with no client-side period math.

searchDocs.title: Season quests​
searchDocs.content: A fifth Scope = "Season" exists alongside Daily/Weekly, dedicated to feeding the Battle Pass. It doesn't rotate — selectQuests("Season", periodIndex) returns the entire curated set (Personal ids then Party ids, each sorted), not a Counts-limited shuffle-and-slice, so every Season quest is active for the whole month. Its period index is BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) (a calendar-month index, not a quest-owned index), so a season's quests reset in lockstep with the battle pass itself — the profile's SeasonPeriod/SeasonProgress/SeasonClaimed fields follow the exact same rollover/auto-grant pattern as Daily/Weekly.  The shipped pool (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance) pays Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and a large BPExp (3000 each) — Season quests exist purely to move the battle pass track, not the coin/XP economy. Any quest, of any scope, can additionally carry an optional Reward.BPExp: number?; the shipped Daily/Weekly pool also pays smaller BPExp amounts alongside normal coins/exp, so ordinary questing keeps the pass moving too.

searchDocs.title: Attribution​
searchDocs.content: Two entry points on QuestManager mirror XPManager.AddXP/AddPartyXP:  function QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor: Player, metricKey: string, amount: number) function QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey: string, amount: number)   Function	Has an actor	AdvancesReportProgress	Yes (e.g. junk collection)	Bumps the actor's own Lifetime metric, advances the actor's Personal quests, and fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric ReportPartyProgress	No (e.g. enemy died, train distance)	Advances every online player's Party quests and bumps each player's Lifetime metric total  Either path calls ensureCurrent first (rolls any elapsed period before applying progress) and only replicates (QuestStateSync) to players whose progress actually changed.

searchDocs.title: Claim and auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: function QuestManager.ClaimQuest(player: Player, questId: string): (boolean, number, number, number)   Manual claim is wired to Packets.ReqClaimQuest and invokes ClaimQuest, which validates in order — profile loaded, quest exists, quest is in the currently active set for its scope, progress ≥ target, not already claimed — and returns (ok, reasonCode, coinsGranted, expGranted). The claimed flag is set before the reward is granted, so a re-entrant or duplicate call cannot double-pay: the second call fails fast with ALREADY_CLAIMED.  The auto-grant sweep runs inside ensureCurrent (called on join, before every progress report/claim, and on the periodic rollover tick). When a scope's stored period index differs from the current index, it walks the old set (selectQuests(scope, oldPeriodIndex)) and grants any quest that was completed but never claimed, before resetting that scope's Progress/Claimed maps. A player who finishes a quest right before rotation and never opens the claim UI is still paid.  Both paths share one grantReward function, which pays coins/exp then fires Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted(player, quest.Reward). BattlePassManager connects to this signal and reads reward.BPExp off the payload regardless of whether the grant came from a manual claim or an auto-grant sweep — see Battle Pass — EXP earning.

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: QuestSourcesLoader (gameplay-only — safe to run in the lobby place, where these events simply never fire) wires the three QuestConfig.Metrics to their gameplay triggers:  Metric	Category	TriggerEnemyKills	Party	Humanoid.Died on any CollectionService-tagged ENEMY_TAG ("EnemyNPC") model — one Janitor per tracked enemy DistanceTravelled	Party	A recurring task.wait(DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS) loop credits DISTANCE_PER_TICK while Signals.SetTrainState reports the train running JunkCollected	Personal	Signals.OnJunkCollected — fired by JunkService once per successful finalized junk grab (collector, junkId)  Adding a quest that reuses one of these Metric keys needs no source code change — only a new entry in QuestConfig.Quests. Wiring a brand-new metric needs one new source hookup in QuestSourcesLoader (see Tune Quests).

searchDocs.title: Perk seam​
searchDocs.content: profile.Data.Lifetime is a { [key]: number } table that is never reset by rollover — distinct from the per-period Progress maps. advancePlayer bumps Lifetime["QuestsCompleted"] by 1 on every below-target → at-target transition, and both report functions bump Lifetime["metric:"..metricKey] by the raw reported amount.  function QuestManager.GetLifetimeStat(player: Player, key: string): number   This is a deliberate seam for a future PerkConfig unlock criterion (e.g. "unlock this perk after QuestsCompleted >= 25") — not wired to any perk this cycle.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: QuestClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, the same shape as PerkClient. It caches the authoritative QuestStateSync snapshot, recomputes the active set client-side with the same QuestState.selectQuests the server uses (so client and server never disagree), and exposes a QuestView descriptor:  export type QuestView = { Id: string, Scope: "Daily" | "Weekly" | "Season", Category: "Personal" | "Party", DisplayName: string, Description: string, Icon: string?, Metric: string, Target: number, Progress: number, IsComplete: boolean, IsClaimed: boolean, IsClaimable: boolean, RewardCoins: number, RewardExp: number, ExpiresAt: number, }   Queries: GetQuests/GetActiveQuests/GetCompletedQuests/GetQuest, plus GetLifetimeStat and a fire-and-forget Claim(questId) command. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires QuestClient and subscribes to Changed, exactly like PerkClient.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") is the ProfileStore key for progress, claimed flags, and the never-reset Lifetime table. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — all prior quest progress and lifetime stats are orphaned (not deleted, just unreachable). It must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places for the cross-place session handoff to share the same record.  Personal progress from ReportProgress also advances Party quests ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) is not Personal-only — it fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric, then additionally advances the actor's Personal quests. A quest author reusing a Personal-sourced metric (JunkCollected) for a new Party quest gets it "for free" — no new source wiring needed.  The active set query needs the correct period index QuestState.selectQuests takes a periodIndex, not a timestamp. Always derive it via QuestState.dayIndex/weekIndex(os.time()) (server) or read it from the cached QuestStateSync snapshot (client, via QuestClient) — never hardcode or guess an index.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Source as QuestSourcesLoader participant Manager as QuestManager (server) participant Client as QuestClient (owning client) Note over Source,Manager: REPORT Source->>Manager: ReportProgress(actor, metric, amt) / ReportPartyProgress(metric, amt) Manager->>Manager: ensureCurrent() — roll elapsed periods first Manager->>Manager: advancePlayer() bumps Progress[questId] (clamped to Target) alt progress changed Manager->>Client: QuestStateSync(periods, expiry, progress, claimed, lifetime) end Note over Manager: COMPLETE (progress[questId] >= Target) Manager->>Manager: bumpLifetime("QuestsCompleted", 1) on the below→at-target transition Client->>Client: QuestView.IsClaimable becomes true (IsComplete and not IsClaimed) Note over Client,Manager: CLAIM Client->>Manager: ReqClaimQuest(questId) Manager->>Manager: validate (active set, progress >= Target, not claimed) Manager->>Manager: claimed[questId] = true (BEFORE grant — idempotent guard) Manager->>Manager: CoinManager.AddCoins(.., "Quest:"..questId); XPManager.AddXP(..); Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, reward) Manager-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, coinsGranted, expGranted) Manager->>Client: QuestStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.title: Threat model​
searchDocs.content: A reserved server (created by the lobby via TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync) already blocks the normal server-list join and rejects follow-a-friend joins. Two vectors remain: launching the gameplay placeId directly and landing in a non-reserved public server (game.PrivateServerId == ""), or a non-roster user reaching a reserved server with a stale access code or expired session.  JoinGuard closes both by validating every joiner against an authoritative roster keyed off the engine-set game.PrivateServerId, which cannot be spoofed from the client — so authorization can never be forged.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place contract​
searchDocs.content: Coordination between the lobby and gameplay places goes through two MemoryStore hash maps (fast, TTL-native, built for ephemeral cross-server state — unlike DataStore, which is slower, rate-limited, and has no native expiry). SessionStore is the only module that touches them.  Roster — keyed by privateServerId:  { partyId, authorizedUserIds: {number}, leaderUserId, createdAt }   The lobby writes this immediately before TeleportAsync, so it exists by the time the gameplay server boots. SessionStore.GetRoster reads it on boot with a short retry loop (GET_RETRIES × GET_RETRY_WAIT) to cover the boot/write race. SessionCoordinator mutates it via RemoveFromRoster when a grace window expires, and clears it entirely via ClearRoster on run end.  Session pointer — keyed by userId:  { placeId, accessCode, privateServerId, jobId, status, heartbeatAt }   This lets the lobby route a rejoiner back to the exact live server. The lobby seeds placeId/accessCode/privateServerId at teleport time, obtaining accessCode + privateServerId from the server-only TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(gameplayPlaceId). Gameplay fills jobId and heartbeats the entry via SessionStore.RefreshPointer(userId, jobId), which uses UpdateAsync to stamp only jobId/status/heartbeatAt onto the already-seeded entry — it returns without creating a pointer if the lobby never seeded one, since gameplay never learns the raw accessCode and must not fabricate it.  jobId is informational/liveness only — it is not used to route the rejoin. On the lobby side, rejoin must set opts.ReservedServerAccessCode = accessCode alone; the engine API forbids combining ReservedServerAccessCode with ServerInstanceId or ShouldReserveServer on the same TeleportOptions. The access code alone resolves to the one reserved server it was issued for. TeleportData may additionally carry { partyId, rosterVersion } for diagnostics/logging — never trusted for authorization.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: JoinGuard — IsReservedServer() is true only for a non-empty PrivateServerId with PrivateServerOwnerId == 0 (rejects both a directly-launched public server and a VIP server). IsAuthorized(roster, userId) checks roster.authorizedUserIds. BounceToLobby(player) retry-teleports to DisruptionConfig.LOBBY_PLACE_ID, reusing that config and its TELEPORT_RETRIES count from the Disruption system.SessionState — RegisterProvider(name, capture, restore) lets other managers plug into the grace/restore flow (see below). Capture(player) must run synchronously from PlayerRemoving, before any deferred teardown clears state. HoldForGrace/HasGrace/TakeBundle/Discard manage the grace window via a Janitor per held entry.SessionSystemLoader — registers AmmoManager.Snapshot/RestorePool and HealthManager.GetHealth/SetHealth as SessionState providers (under the keys "ammo" and "health"), then calls SessionCoordinator.Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Grace and restore flow​
searchDocs.content: On an unexpected PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby), SessionCoordinator.handleLeave synchronously calls SessionState.Capture(player) — which clones every Tool from the player's Backpack and Character into a per-user folder under ServerStorage.SessionToolCache, then runs every registered provider's capture (ammo pool snapshot, current health) — and holds the bundle via SessionState.HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, SessionConfig.GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire). The player stays on the roster while held.  Scenario	What happensRejoin within the grace window	JoinGuard re-admits the player (still authorized). SessionCoordinator.handleJoin sees SessionState.HasGrace(userId) and calls scheduleRestore, which waits for CharacterAdded (or applies immediately if a character already exists) and, deferred one frame so HealthManager's full-health CharacterAdded reset runs first, calls SessionState.Restore(player, bundle) — reattaching cached Tools to the fresh Backpack and running every provider's restore. The player respawns at the normal train/party spawn; character position is never captured or restored. Grace window expires without a rejoin	The task.delay in HoldForGrace fires onExpire, which clears the session pointer and removes the user from the roster so they can no longer rejoin; the bundle's Janitor destroys the cached Tools folder. Clean leave (ReqLeaveToLobby)	SessionCoordinator marks the userId in cleanLeaving before bouncing, so the ensuing PlayerRemoving calls SessionState.Discard (no grace hold) and clears the pointer + roster entry immediately. Run end	When PlayerRemoving leaves the server empty (#Players:GetPlayers() <= 1, checked before removal completes) or on game:BindToClose, runEnded clears the roster and every remaining pointer for this privateServerId. No live-server rejoin is possible once the run has ended — a later rejoin attempt lands in the normal lobby flow.  SessionState's tools-folder cleanup uses an explicit Janitor index (Janitor:Add(toolsFolder, "Destroy", TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX)), not the implicit form, specifically so TakeBundle can detach the folder without destroying it: it calls Janitor:RemoveNoClean(TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX) (clears the index with no side effect) rather than Janitor:Remove (which would run the cleanup method immediately and destroy the very folder the caller is about to restore Tools from).  A SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS loop in SessionCoordinator periodically refreshes the roster TTL (SessionStore.RefreshRosterTTL) and every present, authorized player's pointer TTL (SessionStore.RefreshPointer), so a live run never expires while a dead run (crashed process, no clean shutdown) self-expires after ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: Live-server rejoin only — rejoin works only while the reserved server stays alive (≥ 1 member keeps it running). If the server empties, the run ends and rejoiners return to the lobby fresh; there is no shared-world snapshot or run resurrection.No character-position restore — a rejoining player always respawns at the normal train/party spawn.No DataStore for ephemeral state — health/ammo/Tools grace-window state lives only in server memory (SessionState) and is lost if the server itself dies during the grace window; this is a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight.The lobby implementation (reserve, roster write, rejoin UI) is a separate project; only the cross-place contract above is specified here.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO still exercises grace/restore In Studio, SessionConfig.BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO (default true) makes SessionCoordinator authorize everyone unconditionally, since no reserved server or lobby exists locally. It does not disable the grace/restore code paths — a Studio playtest still exercises Capture/HoldForGrace/Restore normally.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Player participant Coordinator as SessionCoordinator participant State as SessionState participant Guard as JoinGuard participant Store as SessionStore (MemoryStore) Note over Player,Coordinator: UNEXPECTED DROP Player--xCoordinator: PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby) Coordinator->>State: Capture(player) — Tools + ammo + health Coordinator->>State: HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire) alt Rejoin within GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS Player->>Coordinator: PlayerAdded (still on roster) Coordinator->>Guard: IsAuthorized(roster, userId) Guard-->>Coordinator: true Coordinator->>State: HasGrace(userId) == true Coordinator->>State: scheduleRestore -> TakeBundle + Restore (on CharacterAdded) State-->>Player: Tools reattached; ammo + health restored at train spawn else Grace window expires State->>State: onExpire fires Coordinator->>Store: ClearPointer(userId); RemoveFromRoster(privateServerId, userId) Note over Player: A later join is now unauthorized -> Guard.BounceToLobby ejects them end

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ResearchGuiController.client.luau	Builds the entire ResearchGui in code; node rows, active job panel, queue, fuel gauge Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ResearchService.luau	ModuleScript; authoritative owner of ResearchState.State, wires packet handlers + tick loop Server	src/ServerScriptService/ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau	One-line boot script: require(ResearchService) then ResearchService.Initialize() Server	src/ServerScriptService/ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau	Connects Signals.OnResearchLevelUp, republishes ResearchBuffs / ResearchUnlocked Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ResearchState.luau	Pure, stateless rules module: enqueue, cancel, advance, refuel, serialize Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ResearchResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum shared by client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ResearchConfig.luau	Bench tag/interaction distances, queue/fuel/refund constants, the Nodes table  Packets: ReqResearchSnapshot, ReqResearchEnqueue, ReqResearchCancel, ReqResearchRefuel, ResearchStateUpdate — see Networking MapSignals: OnResearchLevelUp, OnResearchStateChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Core loop​
searchDocs.content: Enqueue — player spends materials immediately (pay-on-enqueue, not pay-on-complete) to queue the next level of an eligible node. If nothing is active, the job just enqueued starts immediately.Advance — a server tick burns bench fuel and advances the active job's elapsed time. Progress pauses whenever fuel hits 0; it resumes the instant fuel is added back.Complete — when elapsed >= duration, the node's level is recorded, Signals.OnResearchLevelUp fires, and the next queued job (if any) becomes active.Refuel — a player feeds a held Energy tool into the bench via a second ProximityPrompt; the tool's tier maps to a fuel amount (ResearchConfig.EnergyFuelValue).Cancel — a player cancels a specific level of a node (queued or active); see Cascade-cancel — this is the trickiest part of the system.  Because there is one shared queue and one shared fuel pool for the whole server, this is explicitly a co-op system: any player at the bench can enqueue, cancel, or refuel, and progress benefits everyone.

searchDocs.title: Leveled nodes vs. recipe nodes​
searchDocs.content: Every entry in ResearchConfig.Nodes is a Node with MaxLevel and a Levels table ({ [1] = {Cost, Duration}, [2] = ..., ... }, one entry per level). Two shapes exist:  Leveled upgrade nodes have an Effect ({Type = "StatBuff", Key, PerLevel} or {Type = "FuelEfficiency", DrainPerLevel}). Each completed level contributes to a running total recomputed by ResearchEffectsDispatcher (see Buff/unlock folders).Recipe nodes have Effect = nil. Completing level 1 (recipe nodes are always MaxLevel = 1) writes only a ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> BoolValue; there is no buff to compute. The shipped example is RepeaterRifle, which demonstrates the shape of a pure recipe node but has no Workbench recipe wired to it yet in the shipped WorkbenchConfig. The one recipe gate actually in use — CraftSMG's RequiresNode = "Durability_T1" — instead points at a leveled StatBuff node, showing that any node id can gate a recipe, not just Effect = nil ones. See Workbench Crafting for the consumer side.  A node may declare Prereq (another node's id) and PrereqLevel (default 1) — the prereq node must have reached at least that level before this node accepts enqueues (ResearchState.isEligible).

searchDocs.title: Cascade-cancel​
searchDocs.content: Cancelling is keyed by (nodeId, fromLevel) — the target level of the specific job the player clicked Cancel on (the active job's targetLevel, or a specific queued row's targetLevel). ResearchState.cancel does not cancel just that one job:  Every queued job of the same node with targetLevel >= fromLevel is removed and its full cost refunded (fraction 1.0 — no penalty).If the active job belongs to the same node and active.targetLevel >= fromLevel, it is cancelled too, and its cost is refunded at ResearchConfig.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (0.5 — the "partial progress lost" penalty). If the active job was cancelled, the next queued job (of any node) immediately becomes active with elapsed = 0.  The reasoning: levels are sequential and dependent — you cannot legally hold "Durability_T1 level 3" without level 2 and level 1 having already resolved (pendingLevel stacks consecutively). Cancelling a lower level therefore must also cancel every already-queued higher level of that node, or the queue would contain an orphaned level 3 with no level 2 underneath it.  Concretely, with Durability_T1 active at level 1 and level 2 queued behind it:  Cancelling from level 1 (the active job's row) cancels both: the active level-1 job gets 50% of its cost back, the queued level-2 job gets 100% back, and the queue's next job (if any, possibly for a different node) starts immediately.Cancelling from level 2 (the queued row) cancels only the queued level-2 job (100% refund) — level 1 keeps advancing untouched, because active.targetLevel (1) >= fromLevel (2) is false.  If neither the queue nor the active job matches, ReqResearchCancel returns NOTHING_QUEUED and nothing is refunded. Refunds are ejected at the bench via MaterialEjector along the same TrajectoryPoints → SpawnPoint → scattered LandingPoint arc used by the old Tech Tree (ported verbatim into ResearchConfig).

searchDocs.title: Fuel and pause behavior​
searchDocs.content: Fuel is a single server-wide reserve, capped at ResearchConfig.FUEL_CAP (100).While a job is active, fuel burns at ResearchConfig.FUEL_BURN_RATE (1.0/sec) — burn only happens while a job is active; an idle bench (no active job) never burns fuel.ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate) so a job's elapsed only ever grows in step with fuel actually spent — the moment fuel reaches 0, elapsed stops advancing (the job pauses, it does not fail or lose progress). Refueling resumes it on the next tick.Refueling is Energy-tool based: ResearchService.Initialize's ReqResearchRefuel handler reuses the existing ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnergyToolHelper.luau (GatherEnergyTools/GetEnergyTier/ConsumeTool) — the same helper the Train Fuel and Train Shield recharge flows use — rather than hand-rolling Tool-attribute detection. It takes the first Energy tool found (backpack, then equipped), maps its Tier (1–5) through ResearchConfig.EnergyFuelValue (20/35/55/80/110), consumes the tool, and adds the value to fuel (clamped to FUEL_CAP).  Fuel and queue are shared, not per-player There is exactly one fuel value and one queue for the entire server. Any player at the bench can enqueue against the shared queue, refuel the shared reserve, or cancel any job — including jobs another player paid for. This is intentional (co-op resource pooling, same spirit as the old Tech Tree's shared pools) but means griefing-by-cancel is possible; there is no per-player ownership check.

searchDocs.title: Buff/unlock folders​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of two ReplicatedStorage folders, both recomputed from scratch (not delta-accumulated) on every Signals.OnResearchLevelUp:  Folder	Shape	Written by	Read byReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs	Attributes on the folder itself: one numeric attribute per StatBuff.Key (summed PerLevel * level across all nodes with that key), plus FuelEfficiency (product of DrainPerLevel ^ level across all FuelEfficiency nodes; 1 = no effect)	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	TrainShieldManager (MaxHP), TrainFuelManager (FuelEfficiency) ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked	One BoolValue (named by nodeId, Value = true) per node at level ≥ 1 — recipe nodes included	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	WorkbenchService (server gate), WorkbenchGuiController (client greying)  Recompute-from-levels means totals are always correct with no drift risk, at the cost of iterating every node in ResearchConfig.Nodes on every level-up (cheap — the node count is small). ResearchEffectsDispatcher also seeds both folders once at server boot (before any player joins) so WaitForChild consumers never race an empty folder.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared responsibilities​
searchDocs.content: Shared — ResearchState.luau is a pure, stateless module with no Roblox service calls: newState, levelOf, pendingLevel, isEligible, validateEnqueue, enqueue, cancel (cascade logic), advance (tick), refuel, serialize. Both the server (authority) and the client GUI (asState() cast over the cached snapshot, for greying/afford checks) call the same pure helpers, so the rules can never drift between sides. validateEnqueue deliberately does not check whether the player holds the materials — that check is server-only and layered on top by ResearchService.  Server — ResearchService.luau is the authoritative owner of ResearchState.State. It is a ModuleScript, not a .server.luau Script — see ModuleScript + loader split below. Initialize() (idempotent, guarded by a boot flag) wires all four packet handlers plus the RunService.Heartbeat tick loop. GetLevels() exposes the live levels table for ResearchEffectsDispatcher to read.  Server — ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is a one-line boot script: require(...ResearchService) then ResearchService.Initialize(). Mirrors PerkManager.luau / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau.  Server — ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau connects Signals.OnResearchLevelUp and republishes both buff/unlock folders from scratch. See Buff/unlock folders.  Client — ResearchGuiController.client.luau builds the entire ResearchGui ScreenGui in code (no Studio template) and opens it via the bench ResearchPromptPart ProximityPrompt. Node rows are grouped by Category (fixed order Train/Player/Equipment/Recipes) and sorted by prereq depth then DisplayName. A side panel shows the active job (MotionMaster-spring-driven progress bar, Cancel button) and the queue (each entry independently cancellable), plus a fuel gauge (also spring-driven) with a "PAUSED" badge shown whenever fuel is at 0 while a job is active, and a Refuel button. Between ResearchStateUpdate broadcasts, interpolated() fast-forwards the active job's elapsed time and the fuel gauge locally using the known burn rate and the synced server clock, so the bars move smoothly every frame rather than stepping only on broadcast. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle (springs + the per-frame RenderStepped connection are recreated on open and destroyed on close).

searchDocs.title: ModuleScript + loader split (caution)​
searchDocs.content: ResearchService is a ModuleScript, booted by a separate loader ResearchService.luau lives under ServerStorage/SharedModules/ as a ModuleScript, not ServerScriptService/ResearchService.server.luau. This is deliberate: Roblox's require() only accepts ModuleScript instances — a *.server.luau file compiles to a plain Script, which can never be required by another script. Because ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau needs to call ResearchService.GetLevels(), ResearchService has to be a ModuleScript. The split mirrors the existing PerkManager.luau (ModuleScript, state + Initialize()) / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau (thin boot Script) pattern: ResearchService.luau defines state + an idempotent Initialize() that wires packets and the tick loop, but does nothing until Initialize() is called.ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is the only script that calls ResearchService.Initialize(), exactly once per server. If you ever see require() fail on a *.server.luau/*.client.luau path in this codebase, this is the fix: split the requirable state into a ModuleScript and add a thin loader Script that calls its Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Manual, one-time Studio work — none of this is created automatically by code:  Bench Model. One Model tagged ResearchBench (CollectionService) with its PrimaryPart set.Refund-arc trajectory. A child Model named TrajectoryPoints (tagged PlacementIgnore, per the Placement "tag the CollisionBox only" rule) holding two BasePart children: SpawnPoint (arc start, the bench's output mouth) and LandingPoint (arc end, the floor drop zone). If missing, MaterialEjector degrades gracefully and drops refunded pieces at the bench pivot instead of erroring.Research prompt. A child BasePart named ResearchPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — opens the GUI. MaxActivationDistance is set to ResearchConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE by the client controller at runtime.Refuel prompt. A separate child BasePart named RefuelPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — feeds a held Energy tool into the bench.Material templates. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials must hold Wood and Metal Tool templates with IsCraftMaterial = true and ItemType attributes set — shared with the Shredder and Workbench, no duplication needed.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every request The client's ProximityPrompt distance is never trusted. ReqResearchEnqueue, ReqResearchCancel, and ReqResearchRefuel all re-run isNearBench on the server using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE. A player invoking from range receives TOO_FAR.  Validate-then-consume ordering on enqueue ReqResearchEnqueue calls countMaterial for every cost entry before calling consumeMaterial for any of them. If the player is short on any single material, nothing is consumed — there is no partial-payment state.  Cost is paid on enqueue, not on completion Unlike the old Tech Tree's pooled-contribution model, materials are deducted the instant a level is successfully enqueued — the queue holds already-paid-for jobs. Cancelling is therefore the only way to get materials back, and only at the refund fractions described in Cascade-cancel.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as ResearchGuiController participant S as ResearchService participant D as ResearchEffectsDispatcher P->>C: Walk within INTERACT_DISTANCE C->>C: ProximityPrompt fires (ResearchPromptPart) C->>S: ReqResearchSnapshot() S->>C: { levels, active, queue, fuel } C->>C: cache populated; rows/queue/fuel repainted P->>C: Click Enqueue on a node row C->>S: ReqResearchEnqueue(nodeId) S->>S: re-check bench + proximity S->>S: ResearchState.validateEnqueue (unknown/prereq/max level/queue full) S->>S: countMaterial then consumeMaterial for each cost entry S->>S: ResearchState.enqueue(...) - starts immediately if idle S->>C: (success, reasonCode) S->>C: ResearchStateUpdate(state, serverTime) loop every TICK_INTERVAL S->>S: ResearchState.advance(state, dt, FUEL_BURN_RATE) Note over S: effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel/burnRate) - progress pauses at fuel==0 alt elapsed >= duration S->>D: Signals.OnResearchLevelUp(nodeId, level) S->>S: startNext() - pop next queued job end S->>C: broadcast() on completion, or at most every HEARTBEAT_BROADCAST_INTERVAL end C->>C: interpolate elapsed/fuel locally between broadcasts (synced server clock) D->>D: republish(): recompute ResearchBuffs from GetLevels() D->>D: publish ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> if level >= 1 P->>C: Click Cancel (active job or a queued row) C->>S: ReqResearchCancel(nodeId, fromLevel) S->>S: ResearchState.cancel -> (activeRefund?, queuedRefund) S->>S: eject queuedRefund @ 1.0, activeRefund @ ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION S->>C: (success, reasonCode) + broadcast() P->>C: Click Refuel (or trigger RefuelPromptPart) C->>S: ReqResearchRefuel() S->>S: EnergyToolHelper.GatherEnergyTools/GetEnergyTier/ConsumeTool S->>S: ResearchState.refuel(state, value, FUEL_CAP) S->>C: (success, reasonCode) + broadcast()

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SettingsClient.luau	Get/Set/GetAll/GetDefinition/GetByCategory, value cache, debounced save, join-sync apply Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SettingsAppliers.luau	Client-only key -> applier registry (volumes → Groups.SetVolume) Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/SettingsManager.luau	ProfileStore session lifecycle, legacy Volumes migration, SyncSettings on join, SaveSetting listener Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SettingsSchema.luau	Validate(key, value), Sanitize(map) — the one validator both sides call Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SettingsConfig.luau	Definitions registry, VolumeBusByKey, GetDefaults(), STORE_NAME  Packets: SyncSettings, SaveSetting — see Networking MapSignals: OnSettingChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Config & schema​
searchDocs.content: SettingsConfig is pure data with no client dependencies, so the server can require it directly. SettingsConfig.Definitions is the single registry — one entry per setting key, typed as:  export type Definition = { type: "number" | "boolean" | "enum", default: any, category: string, label: string, order: number, min: number?, max: number?, step: number?, options: { string }?, }   SettingsConfig.GetDefaults() returns a fresh { [string]: any } map of every key to its default — this seeds both a brand-new ProfileStore profile and profile:Reconcile() for existing ones. SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey maps the four volume setting keys to their SoundConfig/Groups bus name (Master, BGM, SFX, Ambience) — the one place that mapping is declared, reused by both the migration step and SettingsAppliers. SettingsConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerSettings") is the ProfileStore name and must not change without a migration plan, since it is also where the legacy Volumes table is read from.  SettingsSchema is the single validator, called identically by server and client so the two sides can never disagree on what's valid. SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value): (boolean, any) looks key up in Definitions (unknown key is rejected, acting as an allowlist); for "number" it rejects non-numbers/NaN then clamps to [min, max]; for "boolean" it requires an exact boolean; for "enum" it requires membership in options. SettingsSchema.Sanitize(map) builds a complete settings map from GetDefaults() overlaid with every entry in map that passes Validate — anything invalid or no longer in the registry is silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: Server authority​
searchDocs.content: SettingsManager owns one ProfileStore session per player (PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), ...)), following the same lifecycle pattern as CoinManager/XPManager: it kicks the player if the session fails to start, ends the session and re-kicks on OnSessionEnd, and ends the session on PlayerRemoving.  On join, before profile:Reconcile() runs, migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) does a one-time, idempotent copy: for every key in VolumeBusByKey, if Settings[key] is unset and the legacy profile.Data.Volumes[bus] is a valid number, it's validated and copied into Settings[key]. Once a key exists in Settings it is never overwritten from Volumes again, so this is safe to leave running indefinitely. The legacy Volumes table itself is left in place (not cleared) after migration.  SettingsManager.Initialize() — called once per server by SettingsSystemLoader.server.luau — wires Packets.SaveSetting.OnServerEvent: it looks up the player's profile (drops the message if none), checks key is a string, re-validates (key, value) through SettingsSchema.Validate, and on success writes profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced. There is no explicit save call — ProfileStore autosaves the profile. Any invalid or unknown-key message is silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: Client API​
searchDocs.content: SettingsClient — initialized once via SettingsController.client.luau calling SettingsClient.Init() at startup — is the only module the settings GUI talks to. It holds a local cache of every setting's current value and exposes Get(key), Set(key, value): boolean, GetAll(), GetDefinition(key), and GetByCategory() (every definition grouped by category and sorted by order; today: "Audio" with 4 entries, "Controls" with 1, CameraSensitivity).  Internally, applyAndNotify(key, value) is the shared path for both the join-sync handler and Set: it writes the cache, calls SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value), then fires Signals.OnSettingChanged:Fire(key, value). The join-sync path calls only applyAndNotify (never scheduleSave), which is what prevents applying the server's own synced values from looping back into another save. scheduleSave(key, value) debounces persistence per key: the latest value is stashed in a pending table, and a single task.delay(0.25, ...) per key sends the trailing value via Packets.SaveSetting:Fire(key, value) — rapid changes (e.g. dragging a volume slider) collapse into one network send 0.25s after the drag settles.

searchDocs.title: Client appliers​
searchDocs.content: SettingsAppliers is a client-only key -> (value) -> () registry, kept deliberately separate from SettingsConfig so the shared config module stays free of client-only dependencies (Groups, UserSettings()) that the server must never require. The four volume keys are wired generically by iterating VolumeBusByKey and calling Groups.SetVolume(bus, value) — see Sound for the underlying SoundManager.SetVolume/GetVolume primitives; persistence lives here, not in SoundManager. Apply(key, value) looks up and calls the applier for key, or no-ops silently if the key has no client-side effect — CameraSensitivity is a deliberate example of the no-entry-needed case: it has no applier because CameraController reads it directly via SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") at startup and stays live via Signals.OnSettingChanged (see Camera).

searchDocs.title: Adding a new setting​
searchDocs.content: Two steps, at most:  Add one entry to SettingsConfig.Definitions — a unique key, a type ("number" | "boolean" | "enum"), a default, a category + label for the GUI, an order within that category, and the relevant bounds (min/max/step for "number", options for "enum"). That's enough for the setting to round-trip end to end: it seeds into new profiles, syncs on join, validates, and persists.If the setting has a direct client-side effect, add a matching entry to SettingsAppliers's appliers table — a one-argument function that applies value. Skip this step for settings with no client effect.  No packet, schema, or ProfileStore change is needed for a new setting — SettingsSchema.Validate and SettingsManager are fully generic over the Definitions table.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never call SettingsAppliers or SettingsManager's internals directly GUI code should only ever call SettingsClient.Get/Set/GetAll/GetDefinition/GetByCategory and listen to Signals.OnSettingChanged. Calling SettingsAppliers.Apply directly skips validation, caching, and persistence — the value will apply visually but never save and will be wiped out by the next join-sync. SettingsManager is server-only and cannot be called from client code; firing Packets.SaveSetting directly skips client-side validation and the cache, desyncing SettingsClient.Get from what the server actually has.  The join-sync path never re-saves. SettingsClient.Init()'s SyncSettings handler calls applyAndNotify directly, not Set — applying the server's own synced values must never re-fire a save back to the server in a feedback loop.SettingsManager.Initialize() re-validates every SaveSetting message. A modified or out-of-date client can fire any (key, value) pair; the server drops anything that fails SettingsSchema.Validate rather than trusting the client's own clamping.Legacy Volumes data is migrated, not deleted. migrateLegacyVolumes copies old per-bus volumes into the generic Settings map once, but the old Volumes table is left on the profile afterward. Don't write new code that reads profile.Data.Volumes.Removing a Definitions entry doesn't delete saved data, but does stop syncing it. SettingsSchema.Sanitize drops any key no longer present in Definitions, so a removed setting simply disappears from SyncSettings/GetAll going forward — it does not actively scrub the old key from the ProfileStore document.CameraSensitivity scales GetMouseDelta(), not an engine property. UserGameSettings.MouseSensitivity is gated behind the RobloxScript capability (CoreScript-only) and throws if a game LocalScript writes it. UserInputService.MouseDeltaSensitivity is settable but only scales GetMouseDelta() consumers — it would have had no effect on the old default Roblox camera, which didn't consume GetMouseDelta() for look/rotation at all. That constraint is why CameraController is a fully script-owned Scriptable camera that reads raw GetMouseDelta() and scales it by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity itself. See Camera.
