searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Player participant SM as SettingsManager participant SC as SettingsClient participant Appliers as SettingsAppliers Note over SM: Join Player->>SM: onPlayerAdded SM->>SM: PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync ("PlayerSettings") SM->>SM: migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) - idempotent Volumes -> Settings copy SM->>SM: profile:Reconcile() - fill missing keys from GetDefaults() SM->>SM: SettingsSchema.Sanitize(profile.Data.Settings) SM->>SC: Packets.SyncSettings(settings) SC->>SC: for each key: SettingsSchema.Validate -> applyAndNotify SC->>Appliers: SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value) SC-->>SC: Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, value) - no re-save Note over SC: Manual change (GUI calls SettingsClient.Set) Player->>SC: SettingsClient.Set(key, value) SC->>SC: SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value) SC->>Appliers: SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, coerced) - immediate local effect SC-->>SC: Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, coerced) SC->>SC: scheduleSave(key, coerced) - debounced 0.25s SC->>SM: Packets.SaveSetting(key, coerced) SM->>SM: SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value) - server re-validates, never trusts client SM->>SM: profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced - ProfileStore autosaves

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ShredderClient.client.luau	Prompt registration, nonce-guarded two-step handshake, junk-count-reactive HoldDuration updates Server	src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau	Session management, anti-exploit validation, junk consumption, material ejection arc, auto-collect loop Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderMath.luau	Shared ComputeHoldDuration helper (linear interpolation) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum (9 codes) shared between client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau	All tunable constants for interaction, hold duration, anti-exploit, arc animation, auto-collect, and asset names  Packets: ReqShredderStart, ReqShredderComplete — see Networking MapSignals: none — the shredder is a self-contained two-step RemoteFunction handshake

searchDocs.title: Client: prompt and handshake​
searchDocs.content: ShredderClient watches CollectionService for Workbench-tagged models. On each workbench it finds a ProximityPrompts/ShredPromptPart/ProximityPrompt, sets ActionText, HoldDuration, and MaxActivationDistance from config, and wires three connections: PromptButtonHoldBegan (fires ReqShredderStart), PromptButtonHoldEnded (bumps the nonce to cancel), and Triggered (fires ReqShredderComplete only when the nonce matches the armed value). A Backpack and Character Janitor pair keeps HoldDuration in sync whenever junk is added or removed. If the player holds the prompt with zero non-Energy junk, an "info" notification fires and the prompt is briefly disabled.

searchDocs.title: Server: two-step session​
searchDocs.content: ReqShredderStart validates the workbench tag, proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE), workbench lock state, per-player cooldown, and junk availability. It stores a session record (workbench, start time, computed duration, junk snapshot). ReqShredderComplete re-checks all constraints plus timing (elapsed >= duration - HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE), re-validates junk still belongs to the player from the snapshot, builds a shuffled material sequence, destroys all junk Tools, locks the workbench, then spawns ejectMaterials.

searchDocs.title: Ejection​
searchDocs.content: ejectMaterials animates each handle along a Catmull-Rom spline (MotionMaster.SplineMove) with uniform-disk scatter around LandingPoint, then calls ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem. Overflow beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS is granted directly in scheduler batches. A 0.5 s auto-collect loop sweeps droppedMaterials; after AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY the item is force-claimed to the owner. See Proximity Pickup for the registration/claim contract.

searchDocs.title: Shared math and result codes​
searchDocs.content: ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration linearly interpolates hold time between MIN_HOLD_DURATION (1 item) and MAX_HOLD_DURATION (MAX_JUNK_COUNT items). Both client and server call it so the prompt ring and the server timing check always agree. ShredderResultCodes is a frozen enum used by both sides for unambiguous rejection reasons.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, and PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN are the primary barriers against timing exploits and teleport-shredding. Increasing tolerances too far removes protection; tightening them too far breaks legit high-latency players.  Studio asset requirements — all three must be present or the server will warn and abort ejection:  Each workbench Model must be tagged "Workbench" with a PrimaryPart set.Each workbench must contain a child Model named "TrajectoryPoints" (tag it PlacementIgnore) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: "SpawnPoint" (at the shredder output mouth) and "LandingPoint" (floor landing target).In ReplicatedStorage, a Folder named "CraftingMaterials" must contain Tool templates named "Wood" and "Metal", each with a BasePart child named "Handle". Set CanBeDropped = false on each template.  Nonce guard. The client uses a per-workbench nonce pair (holdNonce, armedNonce) to drop stale ReqShredderComplete calls when the player releases early or changes workbenches mid-hold. Modifying the hold flow must preserve this guard or the server's NO_SESSION rejection will fire spuriously.  Junk snapshot. The server snapshots junk at ReqShredderStart time. ReqShredderComplete re-filters that snapshot to tools still in the player's possession — it does not re-scan the Backpack. This prevents inflation from picking up new junk during the hold.  Energy junk exclusion. Only Metal and Wood junk types are consumed and yield output. Energy junk is excluded from both the client count and the server's junk collection helpers.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant C as ShredderClient participant S as ShredderServer C->>C: PromptButtonHoldBegan - countNonEnergyJunks() > 0 C->>S: ReqShredderStart(bench) S->>S: validate tag, proximity, not locked, cooldown, junk count S->>S: ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration() S->>S: record session + StartTime S->>C: (isValid, duration, code) C->>C: prompt.HoldDuration = duration C->>C: PromptButtonHoldEnded -> nonce bump (cancels armed session) C->>C: Prompt.Triggered (hold complete), armedNonce check passes C->>S: ReqShredderComplete(bench) S->>S: re-validate session, workbench match, elapsed >= duration - TOLERANCE S->>S: re-verify junk still owned, buildMaterialSequence(junks) S->>S: destroy junk Tools, lock workbench S->>C: (success, woodCount, metalCount, code) S->>S: task.spawn(ejectMaterials) Note over S: SplineMove handle P0->arcPeak->landing<br/>ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem()<br/>tag CraftMaterial, auto-collect loop (0.5s poll)<br/>unlock workbench after ARC_DURATION

searchDocs.content: Config module: ShredderConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luauPlaybook: Tune Shredder Economy  Field	Default	EffectINTERACT_DISTANCE	10	Max studs client prompt activates INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5	Extra server-side slack for desync MIN_HOLD_DURATION	0.3	Hold time (s) for exactly 1 junk item MAX_HOLD_DURATION	3.5	Hold time (s) at MAX_JUNK_COUNT items MAX_JUNK_COUNT	10	Junk count that saturates hold duration HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE	0.5	Seconds subtracted from required hold on server (covers network latency) PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN	1.0	Seconds between successful shreds per player ARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5	Y-axis overshoot of arc midpoint (studs) LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5	Radius of uniform-disk scatter around LandingPoint ARC_DURATION	0.55	Seconds per item arc ITEM_EJECT_DELAY	0.125	Seconds between streamed item ejections MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS	60	Cap on visually animated ejects; overflow granted directly MAX_STREAM_DURATION	6.0	Budget (s) for the stream; compresses delay as needed DIRECT_GRANT_BATCH_SIZE	25	Overflow materials granted per scheduler yield AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY	45	Seconds before unclaimed floor material is moved to owner Backpack WORKBENCH_TAG	"Workbench"	CollectionService tag on workbench Models TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME	"TrajectoryPoints"	Child Model name inside each workbench SPAWN_POINT_NAME / LANDING_POINT_NAME	"SpawnPoint" / "LandingPoint"	Part names inside TrajectoryPoints MATERIALS_FOLDER	"CraftingMaterials"	ReplicatedStorage folder with material Tool templates DROPPED_FOLDER_NAME	"DroppedMaterials"	Workspace folder for in-flight material handles

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/init.luau	Public facade (PlaySFX/PlaySFXAt/PlayLooped/PlayMusic/SetAmbience/SetVolume); the only module other scripts should require Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Groups.luau	Creates/manages the Master → SFX / BGM / Ambience SoundGroup hierarchy under SoundService Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Pool.luau	Per-asset pool of BasePart + Sound pairs used by PlaySFXAt Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/SFX.luau	Play (2D), PlayAt (positional pooled), PlayLooped, and the replication receiver Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Music.luau	Context playlist manager: shuffle, fade, gapped or continuous crossfade Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Ambience.luau	Global 2D ambience bed management with MotionMaster fade Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SoundController.client.luau	Thin bootstrap; calls SoundManager.Init() once Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/MusicDirector.client.luau	Resolves the active BGM context (Combat > LowFuel > Normal) and drives SoundManager.PlayMusic Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MusicService.luau	Stateless API (SetContext) for gameplay code to switch a player's combat music context Server	src/ServerScriptService/ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau	Validated relay for positional sound replication: rate limit + allowlist Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau	Asset IDs, volumes, pitch, pool sizes, bus volumes, playlists, ambience beds  Packets: ReplicateSoundAtLocation, SetMusicContext — see Networking MapSignals: OnTrainStateChanged (consumed, from TrainClient — toggles LowFuel locally) — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Facade and playback​
searchDocs.content: SoundController.client.luau calls SoundManager.Init() once at startup. Init creates the SoundGroup bus hierarchy (Groups.Ensure), warms the positional sound pool (Pool.Ensure plus per-asset pre-warm), connects the replication receiver (SFX.ConnectReplication), preloads every configured asset ID via ContentProvider:PreloadAsync, and autostarts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart.  After Init, any client script or tool may require(SharedModules.SoundManager) and call the facade (PlaySFX, PlaySFXAt, PlayLooped, PlayMusic, SetAmbience, SetVolume). The submodules (Groups, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience) are internal and should not be required directly. The bus hierarchy is fixed:  SoundService └─ Master SoundGroup ├─ SFX SoundGroup ├─ BGM SoundGroup └─ Ambience SoundGroup

searchDocs.title: Positional replication​
searchDocs.content: The server does not play audio itself — ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau acts only as a validated relay for Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:  Per-player rate limit (MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05s) rejects bursts.Payload shape is validated (data.SoundConfig.Id must be a string).The sound ID must be in ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS, built at startup from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() — any SFX entry with Replicate = true is included automatically.The original payload is passed to every other connected player via FireClient.  The receiving client's SFX.ConnectReplication handler acquires a pooled part at the given position and plays it, the same path PlaySFXAt uses locally.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: SoundConfig.Music.Playlists defines exactly three named playlists — one per BGM context. There is no generic/default playlist; Music.Play falls back to "Normal" only when called with no argument.  Context	Trigger	Gap behaviorNormal	Default; nothing else active	Gapped — random silence between tracks Combat	Server calls MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat")	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence LowFuel	Automatic, client-derived from fuel level	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence  Priority when more than one condition is true: Combat > LowFuel > Normal. MusicDirector.client.luau holds two local inputs — combatContext (set by the server) and lowFuelActive (derived locally from Signals.OnTrainStateChanged) — and recomputes the resolved context on every change to either, calling SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) only when the resolved context actually changes. A low-fuel state during combat is suppressed without losing track position when combat ends.  Driving combat from server gameplay code (an event or outpost zone):  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   MusicService.SetContext is stateless — it only fires Packets.SetMusicContext to the targeted player. Passing "Normal" clears the combat override; the client then falls back to LowFuel or Normal based on its own fuel state. Low fuel itself needs no gameplay code: MusicDirector watches Signals.OnTrainStateChanged and activates LowFuel whenever fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25).

searchDocs.title: Volume persistence​
searchDocs.content: The four buses (Master, SFX, BGM, Ambience) persist across sessions as part of the generic Settings system, not inside SoundManager itself. SoundManager.SetVolume(group, volume) / GetVolume(group) remain the immediate-apply primitives — they read/write the Groups bus hierarchy directly and do nothing else.  UI code that needs the change saved calls SettingsClient.Set("MasterVolume" | "MusicVolume" | "SFXVolume" | "AmbienceVolume", value) instead. SettingsClient.Set validates via SettingsSchema, applies it (SettingsAppliers maps the key to a bus via SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey and calls Groups.SetVolume), fires Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, value), and schedules a debounced save (Packets.SaveSetting) that coalesces rapid changes (e.g. a slider drag) into one trailing send. On join, SettingsManager delivers the saved settings map via Packets.SyncSettings; SettingsClient applies each entry the same way but never re-saves a synced value, so no feedback loop results. See Settings for the full validate/apply/persist flow.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never create ad-hoc Sound instances All Sound creation must go through SoundManager. Creating Sound instances by hand bypasses the bus groups (volume controls have no effect), skips the positional pool (memory churn), and may leak sounds that persist across character reloads.  SoundManager.Init() must be called before any Play* call. It is called once by SoundController.client.luau; do not call it again elsewhere.PlaySFXAt parents a pooled BasePart at the given Vector3 in the workspace; the pool releases it after sound.TimeLength + 0.05 seconds. Do not hold references to the part or sound after the call.PlayLooped returns a LoopHandle. The caller must call handle:Stop() or handle:Destroy() when done — an abandoned handle leaks a live Sound under SoundService.A sound entry with Replicate = true and an empty Id ("") is excluded from the allowlist automatically by GetReplicatedIds(); the pool warm step also skips empty IDs.The BGM and Ambience buses default below 1.0. An SFX entry authored at Volume = 0.5 will be audibly louder than music at the same numeric volume because the bus multipliers differ.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant ClientA as Playing client participant Relay as ReplicatedSoundService (server) participant ClientB as Other clients participant MusicSvc as MusicService (server) participant Director as MusicDirector (owning client) Note over ClientA,ClientB: POSITIONAL SFX REPLICATION ClientA->>ClientA: SoundManager.PlaySFXAt(name, position) — local pooled playback ClientA->>Relay: ReplicateSoundAtLocation(location, soundConfig) Relay->>Relay: rate-limit (MIN_INTERVAL) + payload + ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS check Relay->>ClientB: FireClient to all other players ClientB->>ClientB: SFX.ConnectReplication — Pool.Acquire(position) positional playback Note over MusicSvc,Director: BGM CONTEXT SWITCH MusicSvc->>Director: SetMusicContext(context) (e.g. "Combat") Director->>Director: resolve priority Combat > LowFuel > Normal alt resolved context changed Director->>Director: SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) — crossfade or gap per playlist end Note over Director: Signals.OnTrainStateChanged (fuel) toggles LowFuel locally — no server round-trip

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: SoundConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luauPlaybook: Add a Sound  Bus volumes (SoundConfig.GroupVolumes):  Bus	DefaultMaster	1.0 SFX	1.0 BGM	0.6 Ambience	0.5  Per-SFX definition fields (SoundConfig.Sfx):  Field	DescriptionId	Roblox asset ID string; empty string disables the entry Volume	Default playback volume (0–1) Pitch	Fixed pitch multiplier PitchRange	Two-element array {min, max}; randomizes pitch per play Group	Bus name ("SFX", "BGM", "Ambience"); defaults to "SFX" Replicate	true to include the entry in the server relay allowlist Debounce	Minimum seconds between plays of this entry (anti-spam) PoolInitial	Pre-allocated pool slots warmed at Init (positional only) PoolMax	Hard cap on the per-asset pool size (positional only)  Adding a new replicable SFX needs only Replicate = true on the SoundConfig.Sfx entry — GetReplicatedIds() and ReplicatedSoundService pick it up automatically on next server start.  Music playlist fields (SoundConfig.Music.Playlists):  Field	DescriptionTracks	Array of asset IDs; played in Shuffle order if set, else array order Shuffle	Randomize track order each time the playlist (re)starts FadeIn	Seconds to fade a new track up from 0 at start FadeOut	Seconds to fade a track down to 0 at its end; also the crossfade overlap window when continuous GapMin / GapMax	Random silence range (seconds) between tracks; GapMax <= 0 means continuous (overlapping crossfade, no silence) Volume	Target playback volume for tracks in this playlist  SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25) is the fuel-fraction threshold below which MusicDirector activates the LowFuel context.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau	Input binding, WalkSpeed/FOV prediction, intent signalling, sync consumption Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau	Drain/regen simulation, buff application, sync dispatch Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau	Shared sprint gate conditions (humanoid state checks) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau	Speed, FOV, drain/regen, validation thresholds, buff presets  Packets: StaminaSprintIntent, StaminaStateSync, StaminaBuffSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnStaminaValueChanged, OnStaminaBuffsChanged, OnSprintToggled, MobileSprintToggled, OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Client prediction​
searchDocs.content: SprintController binds sprint to LeftShift and ButtonB (gamepad) via ContextActionService; a separate MobileSprintToggled signal handles the mobile toggle button. On each RenderStepped tick it calls canSprintNow() (wraps SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint) and calls setSprinting accordingly, which sets humanoid.WalkSpeed, tweens FieldOfView via TweenPlus, and fires Signals.OnSprintToggled. Sprint intent resets on CharacterRemoving and on WindowFocusReleased.  On StaminaStateSync the client clamps the received stamina, forces sprint off if the server says so, and fires Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged for the HUD. On StaminaBuffSync it forwards buff state to Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged for UI and icon updates.

searchDocs.title: Server authority​
searchDocs.content: StaminaManager maintains a StaminaRecord per player (Stamina, IsSprinting, SprintIntent, LastSprintTime, LastSyncTime). On the StaminaSprintIntent packet it immediately updates sprint state and calls syncPlayer. Its Heartbeat loop clamps dt to MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s to prevent large delta spikes, drains stamina at StaminaDrain * dt * UsageMultiplier while sprinting, and regenerates at StaminaRegen * dt * RegenMultiplier after RegenDelay seconds of not sprinting.  It syncs to the client when sprint state changes, stamina hits 0 (forced stop), stamina refills to max, or the periodic sync interval (STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s) elapses while stamina is changing. It consults StaminaBuffManager each tick for buff multipliers and resyncs immediately on Signals.OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged. StaminaManager.RestoreStamina(player, amount) is available for pickup items but has no caller yet. StaminaManager.Initialize() must be called exactly once — it is called by StaminaSystemLoader.server.luau.

searchDocs.title: Shared validation gate​
searchDocs.content: SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint(humanoid, rules) returns false if health is 0, MoveDirection magnitude is below MinMoveDirection, the character is moving backward beyond MaxBackwardComponent, or horizontal speed is below MinHorizontalSpeed. It is called identically on the client (canSprintNow) and the server (canPlayerSprint) so the gate condition can never desync between the two sides.

searchDocs.title: Buffs​
searchDocs.content: Buff presets (StaminaRegenBuff, StaminaUsageBuff, InfiniteStaminaBuff) define strength and duration for collectible buffs; BuffIcons holds asset ids for the HUD. Buff state is authoritative on the server — StaminaBuffSync pushes the current multipliers to the client for display only, and the client never applies buffs directly to the drain/regen calculation.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Sprint logic must be mirrored on both sides SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint is the shared gate. If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. stun), add it to SprintValidation and verify it is called by both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server). A condition added only to one side will cause desyncs.  WalkSpeed is client-only. The server does not validate movement speed (see audit note S3 in SprintController's source); a cheating client can move at any speed. If movement integrity becomes necessary, add a server-side speed sanity check.STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s (10 Hz). The server only sends a sync when stamina is actively changing — if stamina is full and the player is standing still, no sync is sent, which is intentional.MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s clamp. The server caps the Heartbeat delta so a lag spike cannot drain or regen an unrealistic amount of stamina in one tick. Do not remove this clamp.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as SprintController participant S as StaminaManager P->>C: Hold Shift / mobile toggle C->>S: Packets.StaminaSprintIntent(true) S->>S: record.SprintIntent = true loop Heartbeat (dt clamped to 0.1s) S->>S: drain or regen stamina by UsageMultiplier / RegenMultiplier end S->>C: Packets.StaminaStateSync(stamina, isSprinting) C->>C: currentStamina = stamina; force stop if !isSprinting C-->>C: Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged(stamina) -> HUD bar Note over C: RenderStepped, every frame C->>C: setSprinting(intent AND canSprintNow()) C->>C: humanoid.WalkSpeed, FOV tween C-->>C: Signals.OnSprintToggled(isSprinting) -> HUD S-->>C: Packets.StaminaBuffSync(infinite, regenMult, usageMult) C-->>C: Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged(...) -> HUD / buff icons

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainClient.client.luau	Engine/lever prompt registration, ReqRefuelTrain/ReqToggleBrake calls, error toasts, bridges TrainStateSync to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainFuelGuiController.client.luau	Predicts fuel forward from the last snapshot, exponential smoothing, HUD bar + color Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau	Authoritative fuel state, algebraic drain model, ReqRefuelTrain/ReqToggleBrake handlers, ApplyFuelDamage combat sink Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainGameOver.luau	Idempotent game-over gate, shared with Train Shield Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/TrainGameOverReason.luau	Frozen numeric enum identifying how a round ended Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/TrainConfig.luau	Fuel rates, tiers, proximity tolerance, tags/prompt names (shield knobs live alongside)  Packets: TrainStateSync, ReqRefuelTrain, ReqToggleBrake — see Networking MapSignals: SetTrainState, SetTrainStarted, OnTrainStateChanged, OnTrainGameOver — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Algebraic fuel model​
searchDocs.content: getFuel() is computed as fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed rather than ticked every frame. commitEvent snapshots fuel under the old rate before switching to the new one, so every transition (brake, refuel, stall) is seamless. A scheduleNonce guards task.delay callbacks: any subsequent commitEvent increments the nonce, and a stale callback no-ops if its captured nonce no longer matches. Do not call reschedule directly — always go through commitEvent.  While hasStarted = false (before the first brake release), the drain rate is forced to 0 and no task.delay stall timer is scheduled — fuel is frozen pre-game.

searchDocs.title: Brake toggle​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a TrainBrakeLever-tagged prompt sends ReqToggleBrake(lever). The server flips isBraked; on the first-ever un-brake it also sets hasStarted = true and fires Signals.SetTrainStarted(true). Either way it calls commitEvent(), which reschedules the stall task.delay under the new rate and broadcasts TrainStateSync. The client updates the lever's ActionText ("Stop Train" / "Resume Train") from the returned isBraked.

searchDocs.title: Refuel​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a TrainEngine-tagged prompt sends ReqRefuelTrain(engine). The server validates the tag, proximity, and that the tank isn't already full, gathers the player's Energy tools via EnergyToolHelper.GatherEnergyTools, consumes them smallest-tier-first up to MAX_FUEL, clears a stall if fuel becomes > 0, then calls commitEvent(newFuel). A boolean isRefueling mutex serializes concurrent requests — it is not a queue, so a second request while one is in flight returns NO_ENERGY even if the player holds tools; the player can retry immediately after.

searchDocs.title: Game-over reasons​
searchDocs.content: There are exactly two ways a round ends, both funneled through TrainGameOver.Trigger(reason) so the game-over sequence fires exactly once regardless of which path gets there first:  Reason	Code	Trigger path	Grace?FUEL_DEPLETED	1	Natural fuel-out. Fuel algebraically reaches 0 → onStall() marks the train stalled and broadcasts the 0 → after GAME_OVER_DELAY (180s) elapses with no refuel, onGameOver() fires.	Yes — GAME_OVER_DELAY seconds to refuel before it's final. FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK	2	Combat fuel-kill. TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage routes hits to ApplyFuelDamage once the shield is at 0; if that hit drives fuel to exactly 0, the trigger fires immediately.	No — immediate, no GAME_OVER_DELAY.  TrainGameOver.Trigger(reason: number?) stores the reason (GetReason() returns it) and fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver(reasonCode) exactly once per round; Reset() clears the flag for a future round restart (not yet wired). Both paths currently only log and fire the signal — the real game-over mechanic (round reset / respawn / UI) is a placeholder.  TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount: number, source: any?) is the combat fuel-damage sink. amount is fuel units already converted by TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR — the only caller today is TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage, once the shield is at 0. Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op): hasStarted must be true, TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be false, amount must be > 0 and not NaN. If the hit leaves fuel above 0 it just commits the lower level (the natural stall timer shortens). If it drives fuel to exactly 0, isStalled and gameOverFired are set before commitEvent(0) so no grace timer arms, then TrainGameOver.Trigger(FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK) fires with no wait.

searchDocs.title: Client HUD prediction​
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelGuiController reads the authored StarterGui.TrainFuelGui (never creates UI). On every RenderStepped it computes predictedFuel = snap.fuel - snap.rate * (now - snap.serverTime) and smooths displayedFuel toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing (k = 8). It sets FuelBar.Size/FuelText.Text and colors the bar green (running) / amber (braked) / red (stalled) from snap.isBraked/snap.isStalled.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Each TrainEngine-tagged and TrainBrakeLever-tagged root (a Model or BasePart) must contain a BasePart named TrainConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME ("ProxPromptPart") with a child ProximityPrompt. Both client and server resolve the prompt part recursively via PromptResolver, so it may be nested at any depth. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance and the engine's ActionText are authored in Studio; only the lever's ActionText is set by script.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Game-over is a placeholder Both onGameOver() (natural) and the immediate combat-kill path in ApplyFuelDamage funnel through TrainGameOver.Trigger, which only logs and fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver. No round reset, respawn, or UI is triggered. Do not ship without replacing the placeholder with a real mechanic.  Combat fuel-kill skips the grace delay Unlike natural stall-out, a fuel-zeroing hit via ApplyFuelDamage ends the round immediately — GAME_OVER_DELAY is not consulted on that path. See Game-over reasons.  Algebraic drift note: commitEvent captures now() once and uses it for both lastEventTime and the serverTime field broadcast in TrainStateSync. Any task.wait or async work inserted between the snapshot and the broadcast would drift the client's extrapolation baseline — keep commitEvent synchronous.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Sv as TrainFuelManager participant Cl as TrainClient participant Gui as TrainFuelGuiController Sv->>Sv: Initialize() - fuelAtLastEvent=80, isBraked=true, currentRate=0 (frozen) Sv->>Cl: TrainStateSync(fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime) Cl->>Gui: Signals.OnTrainStateChanged(snap) Note over Cl,Sv: BRAKE TOGGLE Cl->>Sv: ReqToggleBrake(lever) Sv->>Sv: validate lever tag + proximity, flip isBraked (first un-brake: hasStarted=true) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent() - snapshot fuel, switch rate, scheduleNonce++, reschedule() Sv-->>Cl: (success, isBraked, code) Sv->>Cl: TrainStateSync(...) Note over Cl,Sv: REFUEL Cl->>Sv: ReqRefuelTrain(engine) Sv->>Sv: validate proximity + not full, consume Energy tools smallest-tier-first Sv->>Sv: commitEvent(newFuel) Sv-->>Cl: (success, fuelAdded, code) Note over Sv: NATURAL STALL -> GAME OVER Sv->>Sv: task.delay(timeToEmpty) fires -> onStall(): isStalled=true, commitEvent(0) Sv->>Sv: task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) fires -> onGameOver() Sv->>Sv: TrainGameOver.Trigger(FUEL_DEPLETED) - OnTrainGameOver(1), once per round Note over Sv: COMBAT FUEL-KILL (immediate, no grace) Sv->>Sv: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage while shield==0 -> ApplyFuelDamage(amount*FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR) Sv->>Sv: newFuel<=0: isStalled=true, gameOverFired=true, commitEvent(0) Sv->>Sv: TrainGameOver.Trigger(FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK) - immediate, skips GAME_OVER_DELAY Note over Gui: CLIENT HUD LOOP (RenderStepped) Gui->>Gui: predicted = snap.fuel - snap.rate*(now-snap.serverTime); smooth k=8 Gui->>Gui: FuelBar.Size + color (green/amber/red)

searchDocs.title: Recharge​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a ShieldConsole-tagged prompt sends ReqRechargeShield(console). The server validates the tag and proximity, gathers the player's Energy tools via EnergyToolHelper.GatherEnergyTools, and consumes them smallest-ShieldRecharge-value-first until currentShield == maxShield (never over-filled). An isRecharging boolean mutex serializes concurrent requests — like the fuel system's isRefueling, it is not a queue: a second request in flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY rather than a queued success. On success the client plays SoundManager.PlaySFX("ShieldRecharge").

searchDocs.title: Damage / fuel bleed-through​
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, source?) is the single damage entry point for the train — all incoming attack/hazard damage, whether it lands on the shield or bleeds through to fuel, routes through this call. No system calls it yet; it is designed for a future combat/hazard system. Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op): hasStarted must be true, TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be false, amount must be > 0 and not NaN.  Shield > 0 (absorbs): currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount); broadcast() -- a hit that drives it exactly to 0 discards its excess; this does NOT end the round Shield == 0 (bleeds): TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) -- see Train Fuel: Combat fuel-kill for what happens if this zeroes fuel   This replaced the old behavior where the shield reaching 0 called TrainGameOver.Trigger directly — shield depletion by itself no longer ends the round, it just removes the train's damage buffer. TrainConfig.CORE_TAG ("TrainCore") is reserved for the train's structural model for a future combat system to tag; ApplyDamage does not read it directly.

searchDocs.title: Max formula (buffs)​
searchDocs.content: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + ResearchBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus)   Research Bench additive: each completed level of Durability_T1 accumulates onto ResearchBuffs.MaxHP (+50/level, up to MaxLevel = 3 for +150 total), added before the perk multiplier.Party perk multiplicative: TrainShieldBonus = 0.05 * maxLevel across all players (server-max resolution), applied on top of the base + Research sum.Ratio-preserving recompute: when either buff changes, recomputeMax preserves the current fill ratio (currentShield / oldMax) and rounds to the nearest integer — a player at 60% shield stays at ~60% after an upgrade.  subscribeBuffs attaches GetAttributeChangedSignal listeners to both buff folders via WaitForChild, then calls recomputeMax once after attach to catch any missed signals during the wait. See Research Bench and Perks for the upstream buff systems.

searchDocs.title: Shield monitor (SurfaceGui)​
searchDocs.content: The shield HUD is diegetic, not on-screen: TrainShieldGuiController clones the ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui SurfaceGui template onto every BasePart tagged TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG ("TrainShieldMonitor"), discovered via CollectionService:GetTagged plus live add/remove signals. The clone is created client-side, so each player drives their own independent copy on the same shared surface — no server/replication involvement in the GUI itself. Each registered monitor owns a Janitor that destroys the clone and disconnects its RenderStepped loop when the tag is removed.  The monitor drives two readouts, both eased every frame via exponential smoothing:  Shield — from Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged (current / max). Reads "Online" (cyan) above 25%, flips to "Critical" (red) at or below 25%, with hysteresis — it doesn't return to Online until the displayed percentage rises back above 28%. Entering/exiting Critical also swaps the Shield ImageLabel asset.Fuel reserve — extrapolated from Signals.OnTrainStateChanged exactly like the separate on-screen TrainFuelGui HUD. Cyan normally, red at or below 25% fuel. This is purely a second readout on the same monitor face — it does not replace TrainFuelGui, which continues to run unchanged.  No server, packet, or signal changes were needed for the monitor — it consumes the same signals the old HUD already used.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Each ShieldConsole-tagged root (Model or BasePart) must contain a child BasePart named TrainConfig.SHIELD_PROMPT_PART_NAME ("ProxPromptPart") with a child ProximityPrompt, resolved recursively via PromptResolver. Multiple consoles are supported, each registered independently. Tag every BasePart that should display a monitor with TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG; the template is authored at ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui and its element names are load-bearing — TrainShieldGuiController resolves them with WaitForChild and errors on startup if any are missing or renamed. Tag the train's structural model with TrainConfig.CORE_TAG ("TrainCore") — currently unused by TrainShieldManager but reserved for future combat systems.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Recharge mutex is not a queue isRecharging is a boolean, not a queue. A second recharge request while one is in-flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY — not a queued success. The player can try again immediately after.  Pre-game freeze hasStarted is false until Signals.SetTrainStarted fires (the first brake release on the fuel side). ApplyDamage is a no-op until then.  Passive regen is off by default SHIELD_REGEN_ENABLED = false and SHIELD_REGEN_PER_SEC = 0. No regen loop exists yet. To add passive regen, implement a RunService.Heartbeat-based loop in TrainShieldManager gated on SHIELD_REGEN_ENABLED, and update this page and the config map.  Shield depletion is no longer a game over The shield can sit at 0 indefinitely; only fuel reaching 0 (natural stall-out or combat bleed-through) ends the round. See Train Fuel — game-over reasons.  typeof guard on OnServerInvoke ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke receives (player, console) where console is client-supplied. A typeof(console) == "Instance" guard runs before acquiring the isRecharging lock, so a malformed invocation (nil or non-Instance) is rejected cleanly without erroring.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Sv as TrainShieldManager participant Cl as TrainShieldController participant Gui as TrainShieldGuiController Sv->>Sv: Initialize() - maxShield=computeMax(), currentShield=maxShield Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldSync(currentShield, maxShield) Cl->>Gui: Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged(current, max) Note over Cl,Sv: RECHARGE Cl->>Sv: ReqRechargeShield(console) Sv->>Sv: isRecharging mutex, validate tag + proximity Sv->>Sv: GatherEnergyTools smallest-first, consume until full Sv-->>Cl: (success, shieldAdded, code) Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldSync(...) Note over Sv: DAMAGE (future combat/hazard caller) Sv->>Sv: ApplyDamage(amount, source) - guard hasStarted, not HasFired, amount>0 alt currentShield > 0 Sv->>Sv: currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount); broadcast() else currentShield == 0 Sv->>Sv: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) end Note over Sv: BUFF CHANGE Sv->>Sv: ResearchBuffs.MaxHP or PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus changes Sv->>Sv: recomputeMax() - ratio-preserving rescale, broadcast() Note over Gui: MONITOR UPDATE (RenderStepped, per tagged part) Gui->>Gui: displayedShieldPct eased toward shieldSnap; Online/Critical + image swap Gui->>Gui: fuel reserve readout extrapolated from OnTrainStateChanged

searchDocs.title: Opening the bench​
searchDocs.content: Hovering the MoveButton / StashButton swaps each button's Icon image and eases its ButtonIconContainer.BackgroundColor3 to the dark accent Color3.fromRGB(19, 15, 24) via MotionMaster, restoring the originally-authored icon and color on mouse leave. This is purely cosmetic and is wired in WorkbenchGuiController.client.luau, not PlaceableActions.  On the first open of a session, the detail pane auto-selects the first recipe in the grid's sort order (Category, then DisplayName — the same order shown under the "All" filter) so it never shows the unselected Studio placeholder. This is a one-time default: once any recipe is selected (by this default or by a player click), the selection persists across closes/reopens like any manual pick.

searchDocs.title: Client — recipe grid and gating​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchGuiController opens via the bench CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt. It builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes and greys any recipe whose RequiresNode is not present in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked. Fires ReqCraft on the Craft button and fires Signals.OnItemCrafted on a confirmed success. The CloseButton closes the GUI. The DropdownButton is driven by the reusable Dropdown widget, which fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory on selection to re-filter the grid. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle.

searchDocs.title: Server — authoritative craft handler​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchService is the sole owner of the authoritative ReqCraft handler. On ReqCraft(bench, recipeId) it validates, in order:  Look up the recipe in WorkbenchConfig (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE).Verify the bench is a tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET).Re-check proximity, INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE (else TOO_FAR).CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate, per-player timestamp (else COOLDOWN).Check the RequiresNode gate in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED).CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(recipe.Output) — verify the output slot is usable before consuming any materials (else OUTPUT_FAILED).Confirm the player holds enough cost materials (else INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS).  On pass: consume materials from the player's Backpack, then call CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(player, recipe.Output) and record the cooldown timestamp. The handler returns (success: Boolean8, code: NumberU8).

searchDocs.title: Output dispatch​
searchDocs.content: CraftOutputDispatcher handles the three output kinds:  Kind == "Weapon" — clones the named Tool from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Armor" — calls ArmorManager.SetTier(player, output.Tier), updating ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction in ReplicatedStorage.Kind == "Placeable" — grants the named Tool from ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> into the player's Backpack.  isFeasible(output) verifies the target output slot is usable (e.g. the template exists, the tier is valid) before materials are consumed. A misconfigured recipe never costs the player materials.

searchDocs.title: Recipe schema​
searchDocs.content: Recipes are declared in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes as a { [string]: Recipe } table keyed by a string recipe ID:  export type Output = { Kind: "Weapon", ToolName: string } | { Kind: "Armor", Tier: number } | { Kind: "Placeable", PlaceableName: string } export type Recipe = { Category: string, -- one of RecipeCategories ("weapons"|"ammo"|"armor"|"workstation") DisplayName: string, Description: string, Tier: number, -- 1..5 flavor/quality badge only; NOT a prerequisite ladder Icon: string, -- rbxassetid:// string for the grid tile and detail panel Cost: { Wood: number?, Metal: number? }, RequiresNode: string?, -- Research Bench nodeId gate or nil = always available Output: Output, }   Tier is a purely cosmetic quality badge displayed as a star rating in the GUI. It has no prerequisite chain and imposes no unlock order — any recipe with RequiresNode = nil is available to craft at any time regardless of Tier. The only unlock gate is RequiresNode. The Cost table is limited to Wood and Metal because the GUI renders exactly two material rows; adding a third material requires a GUI layout change and a matching config key.  The Recipes table is the live catalog. The shipped placeholder entries:  Recipe ID	Category	Cost	RequiresNode	OutputCraftPistol	weapons	Metal 10	nil	Weapon "Pistol" CraftArmorT1	armor	Metal 15	nil	Armor tier 1 CraftWorkbench	workstation	Wood 5	nil	Placeable "Workbench" CraftSMG	weapons	Metal 25	"Durability_T1"	Weapon "SMG"  The workstation category currently contains only CraftWorkbench — it exists as its own dropdown filter rather than folding the Workbench into weapons or armor because future placeable stations (e.g. a second crafting structure) are expected to land in the same category.

searchDocs.title: Research gate seam​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher publishes leveled-up node IDs into a ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked folder (a BoolValue per node at level ≥ 1, named by nodeId) in parallel to the ResearchBuffs folder. This folder is written by the server whenever a node reaches level 1 and is read by:  WorkbenchService (server): authoritative gate check. A craft request whose recipe has a non-nil RequiresNode is rejected with LOCKED if the corresponding BoolValue is absent or false. Because the folder is written by the server, clients cannot forge an unlock.WorkbenchGuiController (client): greying. Recipes with a locked RequiresNode are rendered as unavailable in the grid so players know they need to research the gating node first. The client reads this folder but never writes it.  Unlike the old Tech Tree (where a node auto-unlocked the instant its pooled material cost was met), a gating Research Bench node now also costs time: the player pays materials on enqueue, then the node's level advances in real time (gated by bench fuel) before ResearchUnlocked is written. Recipes behind a RequiresNode are therefore no longer available the moment materials are gathered — see Research Bench for the full enqueue/advance/complete flow and the ResearchBuffs/ResearchUnlocked folder contract.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Tag the Workbench Model. In ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench, tag the root Model with the CollectionService tag Workbench (the same tag the Shredder scans for — one Model serves as both crafting station and shredder). Give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model — PromptResolver finds it recursively) containing a ProximityPrompt. Set the Model's PrimaryPart. The shredder half uses a sibling ShredPromptPart.Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates. Add a folder named WeaponTemplates inside ServerStorage. Place craftable weapon Tools here (e.g. clones of Pistol and SMG from StarterPack). These are separate from the StarterPack copies — the Workbench clones from here into the player's Backpack, so stat changes or visual differences can live here independently.Ensure craftable placeables exist. Each recipe with Output.Kind == "Placeable" needs a Tool at ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<PlaceableName>. The Workbench itself already follows this convention as a grid-placeable item.Material templates are shared. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials already holds Wood and Metal Tool templates (shared with the Shredder and Research Bench systems). No duplication is needed.Wire ResearchUnlocked. ResearchEffectsDispatcher creates and writes this folder automatically at runtime. No manual Studio setup is required for the gate to function. If testing in isolation (without a running ResearchService/ResearchEffectsDispatcher), create a Folder named ResearchUnlocked in ReplicatedStorage and add BoolValue children named after whichever node IDs you want to treat as unlocked.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every craft The client proximity prompt is never trusted. WorkbenchService re-runs the distance check using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE on every ReqCraft call. A player exploiting from range receives TOO_FAR.  Feasibility is checked before materials are consumed CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(recipe.Output) runs (and must succeed) before any material Tool is removed from the player's Backpack. A recipe that references a missing weapon template or an invalid armor tier therefore fails without costing the player anything. Misconfigured recipes are safe to ship; they only result in a visible craft failure.  Research gate is read from server-written state The ResearchUnlocked folder is written exclusively by ResearchEffectsDispatcher on the server. A client cannot create or modify entries in that folder. The server re-reads the folder on every ReqCraft call, so a client that somehow fakes the UI greying cannot bypass the gate.  Cost is limited to Wood and Metal The GUI renders exactly two material rows. Cost may only specify Wood and/or Metal. Adding a third material type (e.g. Energy) requires a GUI layout change alongside the config key — otherwise the cost is silently unchecked on the client (though the server will still validate it).  Tier is a flavor badge, not a prerequisite ladder Tier (1–5) drives the star-rating display only. There is no inter-recipe prerequisite chain derived from Tier values. The sole unlock gate is RequiresNode. Do not attempt to use Tier as a crafting order enforcer — it will not work without code changes.  Known edge case: respawn mid-craft (v1) If a player's Backpack disappears between the feasibility check passing and CraftOutputDispatcher.grant executing (e.g. the player respawns during that narrow window), materials may be consumed but the grant returns OUTPUT_FAILED. The client receives a failure response and the player loses the materials. This is an accepted v1 limitation — the window is sub-frame in practice. A future refund path or a pre-grant Backpack re-check is the recommended fix.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as WorkbenchGuiController participant S as WorkbenchService P->>C: Walk within INTERACT_DISTANCE C->>C: ProximityPrompt fires (CraftPromptPart) C->>C: GUI opens; grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes C->>C: Grey recipes whose RequiresNode is not in ResearchUnlocked P->>C: Click a recipe tile C->>C: Show DisplayName, Description, Tier badge, Cost rows, RequiresNode note P->>C: Click Craft button C->>S: ReqCraft(bench, recipeId) S->>S: look up recipe (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE) S->>S: verify tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET) S->>S: re-check proximity (else TOO_FAR) S->>S: CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate (else COOLDOWN) S->>S: check RequiresNode in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED) S->>S: CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(Output) (else OUTPUT_FAILED) S->>S: verify materials held (else INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) S->>S: consume materials, CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(...) searchDocs.title: Client: controller and handlers​
searchDocs.content: WeaponController.client.luau is the bootstrap that watches the local character for Tool equip/unequip events. It looks up WeaponConfig[tool.Name].Category and dispatches to the matching category handler (MeleeHandler, GunHandler, or ThrowableHandler). It creates one Janitor per equipped Tool (and one per character) so all connections clean up correctly on unequip, death, or weapon switch. It fires Signals.WeaponEquipped/Signals.WeaponUnequipped for the HUD, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip to toggle the aim camera mode. It binds R to OnReload and G to OnDetonate for handlers that declare those callbacks.  MeleeHandler — combo stepping: on each left-click it calls WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing (tolerance 0) to determine the next step. If the click arrives during recovery it buffers one keyed retry via Janitor rather than dropping the input. It executes the predicted step (swing sound via SoundManager, optional AnimationTrack, local hitbox query via WeaponValidation.queryMeleeTargets for an instant hitmarker fired as Signals.WeaponLocalHit, debug box draw, Signals.WeaponComboChanged), then fires payload-less ReqMeleeSwing. Client combo state is cleared on unequip.  GunHandler — hitscan + rocket cosmetic + ammo prediction. On activate, it gates on a client-local fire-rate check and predicted magazine count (via AmmoApi), then fires ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir). It draws the shooter's own tracer (hitscan only; rocket has no local projectile) and supports semi and automatic fire. OnReload fires ReqReloadWeapon and predicts the ammo transition after the server-confirmed reload window. Authoritative ammo is reconciled via WeaponMagSync → Signals.WeaponMagChanged and AmmoPoolSync → Signals.AmmoPoolChanged.  ThrowableHandler — grenade and C4. On activate, it gates on the throw cooldown, plays throw sound, and fires ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir). There is no local projectile cosmetic — the server-spawned instance replicates to all clients. For C4 (Detonation == "Manual"), OnDetonate fires ReqDetonate. Grenade ignores G.  TrajectoryPreview — a client-local green-neon ballistic arc shown while any throwable is equipped, using a fixed pool of reused BasePart segments updated every RenderStepped. Origin offset (SPAWN_OFFSET = 2.5) and upward aim bias match ServerProjectile/ThrowableHandler exactly so the preview arc matches the real projectile path. Purely cosmetic — no packets sent.  WeaponEffectsController — consumes replicated combat FX packets. WeaponFired is ignored for the local shooter (who already drew its own tracer) and renders tracer + impact spark for other players' shots. WeaponImpact renders an impact spark + sound for all melee/gun hits. ExplosionAt renders an expanding neon sphere + sound for rocket, grenade, and C4 detonations, for everyone including the shooter.

searchDocs.title: Shared validation (WeaponValidation)​
searchDocs.content: Pure math run on both client (prediction) and server (authority):  canFire(lastFireTime, cooldown, now) — fire-rate gate.meleeHitbox(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize) — single source of truth for the oriented swing box CFrame and size.queryMeleeTargets(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize, ignore) — box overlap returning unique Humanoid-bearing Models.resolveComboSwing(state, combo, now, tolerance) — pure combo step resolution; shared so client and server stay in sync.resolveStep(config, step) — merges step overrides with weapon-level defaults into a ResolvedStep.applySpread(direction, spreadDegrees) — applies a random spread cone to an aim direction (cosmetic on client; server does its own authoritative ray).isWithinRange(origin, hitPos, maxDistance) — range cap check.ammoAfterShot(mag) / ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magazineSize) — pure ammo transitions. ammoReloadFromPool returns (newMag, taken) where taken is the pool amount consumed.aoeFalloff(center, hitPos, radius, maxDamage) — linear AOE falloff.queryAOEModels(center, radius, ignore) — sphere overlap returning { model, humanoid, distance } for AOE application.

searchDocs.title: Server: packet handling​
searchDocs.content: WeaponServer.server.luau receives all weapon packets and runs per-category validation (fire-rate, ammo, origin tolerance, direction validity) before any damage or projectile spawn. It manages gun ammo initialisation on equip via WeaponState.EnsureAmmo + WeaponMagSync. On reload, it waits ReloadTime, calls ammoReloadFromPool, consumes the drawn ammo from AmmoManager, then fires WeaponMagSync + AmmoPoolSync (the latter emitted by AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo). On a successful throwable throw, the server destroys the player's matching Tool (onThrowProjectile — 1 Tool = 1 throw). It drives the FastCast2 rocket caster (rocketServerCaster) — its LengthChanged callback steps the cosmetic part, its Hit callback calls CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts ExplosionAt. It also handles throwable throw (onThrowProjectile) and detonate (onDetonate).

searchDocs.title: Server: damage routing (CombatService)​
searchDocs.content: CombatService is the single damage router with two primary entry points:  ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — applies damage to a resolved Model. Players route through HealthManager.ApplyDamage (keeping the HUD-tracked record correct — see Health); faction-tagged NPCs ("EnemyNPC"/"FriendlyNPC") take direct humanoid:TakeDamage. Anything without a recognized faction is ignored. Friendly-fire is enforced via Factions.canDamage: only Player↔Enemy damage lands; players never hurt players or friendly NPCs. A nil attacker is treated as environmental and bypasses the faction gate. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt.ApplyAOE(center, radius, maxDamage, attackType, attacker, ignore) — calls queryAOEModels, applies aoeFalloff to each target, and routes through ApplyToModel with aoeVariant = "Explosion".  Also available: ApplyToPart(part, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model then calls ApplyToModel. EnemyWeapon calls the same entry points for enemy fire — see Enemy Combat.

searchDocs.title: Server: per-player state (WeaponState)​
searchDocs.content: Per-player authoritative state. Fields per player record:  lastFire: { [weaponName]: number } — os.clock() of last shot/swing per weapon; gates fire-rate.combo: { [weaponName]: { index, lastHitTime } } — authoritative combo progress.ammo: { [weaponName]: { mag, reloadEndsAt } } — magazine count and reload window (reloadEndsAt is the os.clock() timestamp when a reload finishes; 0 means not reloading). Reserve is no longer stored here — pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager.active: { ActiveCharge } — active manual throwables (C4) awaiting detonation.  Key functions: EnsureAmmo (seeds magazine from config), GetMag/SetMag, GetLastFire/SetLastFire, GetCombo/SetCombo, IsReloading, SetReloadEnd, GetActiveCount, AddActive, TakeAllActive. Clear destroys all active charges and removes the player's record on PlayerRemoving.

searchDocs.title: Server: projectiles (ServerProjectile)​
searchDocs.content: Spawns and owns server-authoritative, replicated projectile instances cloned from ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets into workspace/ServerProjectiles. Two spawn paths:  spawnRocket(templateName, cframe) — anchored, non-collidable cosmetic part; the caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the FastCast2 cast.spawnThrowable(templateName, origin, direction, speed, rest, ignore) — server-owned physics rigid body. prepareAssembly un-anchors all parts, sets the WeaponProjectile collision group (passes through characters), and applies per-mode elasticity: "Stick" (C4) elasticity = 0 (lands dead); "Bounce" (Grenade) elasticity = 0.15 (one small hop). installSettle polls until the charge has contacted a world surface and come to rest, then anchors it flat. Network ownership is kept server-side via root:SetNetworkOwner(nil).

searchDocs.title: HUD integration contract​
searchDocs.content: This system ships no UI. A HUD widget that wants to display ammo or combat feedback must consume:  Packets (server → owning client, handled by AmmoApi): WeaponMagSync(weaponName, mag) — authoritative magazine count sent on equip, after each shot, and after reload completion.AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) — authoritative pool count for a given ammo type sent whenever the pool changes (shot, reload, craft). AmmoApi read surface (preferred over raw packets): AmmoApi.GetMag(weaponName) → (mag, magSize) — current magazine and max size.AmmoApi.GetPool(ammoType) → (amount, capacity) — current pool and capacity cap.AmmoApi.GetEquippedAmmo() → (mag, magSize, pool, cap)? — combined ammo for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns.AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount(toolName) → count — counts matching Tools in the Backpack + equipped slot. Signals (client-side): WeaponEquipped(toolName, category) — fired on equip.WeaponUnequipped(toolName) — fired on unequip.WeaponMagChanged(weaponName, mag) — fired by AmmoApi on predicted mag update and on WeaponMagSync reconciliation.AmmoPoolChanged(ammoType, amount) — fired by AmmoApi on AmmoPoolSync or local prediction.ThrowableCountChanged(toolName, count) — fired by AmmoApi when the backpack throwable count changes.WeaponReloadStarted(weaponName, reloadTime) — fired when a reload request is sent.WeaponReloadComplete(weaponName) — fired when the reload window elapses or reload is rejected.WeaponLocalHit(model) — fired on a predicted melee/hitscan hit for hitmarker display.WeaponComboChanged(toolName, stepIndex, totalSteps) — fired on each combo step advance.  Ammo HUD. AmmoHudController (client) drives the authored AmmoGui (bottom-right ScreenGui). It shows the equipped weapon's DisplayName and, for guns, the loaded magazine over the reserve pool (mag / pool); for throwables, the carried count. It is hidden for melee and when nothing is equipped. All data comes from AmmoApi + the weapon/ammo Signals; the HUD never talks to the server.

searchDocs.title: Ammo economy​
searchDocs.content: Pool and magazine model​  Ammo is split into two distinct layers:  Magazine (WeaponState, server) — per-gun in-memory count representing what is currently loaded. The magazine is seeded to MagazineSize rounds on the gun's first equip (EnsureAmmo) and then persists across deaths within the session (it is not refilled on every equip or on respawn). On each shot the magazine decrements by one. On reload, the magazine refills from the pool. The magazine is the only ammo state WeaponState owns; there is no longer a reserve field per gun.Pool (AmmoManager, server) — per-player, per-type in-memory count of unloaded ammo. Entirely session-only — nothing is persisted to a DataStore. The pool is seeded to each type's Starting value on the player's first spawn only; it then persists across deaths for the rest of the session (dying never refills reserve ammo). Every type's Starting is 0: players are never given free reserve ammo — all reserve ammo is crafted (see Crafting ammo). AmmoManager.EnsureStarting re-syncs the current pool to the owning client on each respawn so the HUD shows the correct value after the character and Backpack rebuild. The pool is shared across all guns of the same ammo type.  A freshly crafted weapon still spawns with one full magazine (the magazine is seeded to MagazineSize on first equip), so it can fire immediately. But once that magazine is emptied the gun cannot be reloaded until the player crafts ammo into the reserve pool.  Ammo types (AmmoConfig)​  Ammo type	Display name	Capacity	Starting (first spawn)Light	Light Rounds	300	0 Heavy	Heavy Rounds	60	0 Rocket	Rockets	12	0  Gun → ammo type mapping:  Gun	Ammo typePistol, SMG, AR	Light SR	Heavy RocketLauncher	Rocket  Reload flow​  Client fires ReqReloadWeapon.Server checks mag < magSize and pool > 0; rejects otherwise (returns 0 reload time).Server waits ReloadTime, then calls ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magSize) (in WeaponValidation), which returns (newMag, taken).AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo(player, ammoType, taken) is called atomically; it clamps, deducts, and fires AmmoPoolSync to the owning client.Server sets the new magazine via WeaponState.SetMag and fires WeaponMagSync to the owning client.  Throwables​  Throwables are physical Roblox Tools in the player's Backpack. Each throw consumes exactly one Tool: WeaponServer.onThrowProjectile destroys the equipped throwable Tool server-side on a successful throw. There is no numeric reserve or CarryCount in WeaponState — count is inferred by AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount by scanning the Backpack and equipped slot.  C4 detonation is intentionally decoupled from holding the Tool: ThrowableDetonateController.client.luau listens for the global G keybind and fires ReqDetonate regardless of what is currently equipped. The server no-ops if the player has no active charges. This design handles the edge case where the last C4 was thrown (destroying its Tool) but live charges are still stuck to surfaces awaiting detonation.  Crafting ammo​  See Workbench Crafting for the full crafting flow; the recipe values below are illustrative — WorkbenchConfig.Recipes is canonical.  Ammo can be replenished at a Workbench. Crafting recipes in the "ammo" category call AmmoManager.AddAmmo (which clamps to Capacity). Available ammo recipes:  Recipe	OutputCraftLightAmmo	+60 Light Rounds CraftHeavyAmmo	+12 Heavy Rounds CraftRocketAmmo	+2 Rockets CraftGrenade	3 Grenade Tools CraftC4	1 C4 Tool  Weapon Tool recipes clone the template from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates directly into the player's Backpack.  Client read surface (AmmoApi)​  AmmoApi is the single client-side cache and read surface for all ammo data. HUD widgets and handlers should call AmmoApi rather than listening to raw packets.  Method	Returns	NotesGetMag(weaponName)	(mag, magSize)	Current magazine count and magazine capacity. GetPool(ammoType)	(amount, capacity)	Current pool count and pool capacity cap. GetEquippedAmmo()	(mag, magSize, pool, cap)?	Combined view for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns or unarmed. GetThrowableCount(toolName)	count	Counts matching Tool instances in Backpack + equipped slot.  AmmoApi listens to WeaponMagSync and AmmoPoolSync packets, updates its cache, and fires the corresponding Signals. It also watches the player's Backpack for tool additions/removals (rebinding per-character via Janitor) to keep GetThrowableCount accurate. Bootstrapped once by AmmoController.client.luau.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Fire-rate enforcement Guns enforce 60/RPM intervals via WeaponState.GetLastFire; melee enforces Recovery, ChainWindow, and ResetCooldown per combo step via WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing (server tolerance = 0.05 s). Requests that arrive too early are silently dropped.  Server-authoritative ammo and reload Magazine counts and reload timing are owned by WeaponState on the server; pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager. Firing at an empty magazine is rejected. Firing while a reload window is active (reloadEndsAt > now) is rejected. Reloading with an empty pool is rejected. Neither the magazine count, pool count, nor the reload timer is read from the client.  Origin, spread, and distance validation The claimed muzzle origin for guns and throw origin for throwables must be within 14 studs of the server-side HumanoidRootPart position and must be a finite (non-NaN) vector. Claimed directions with zero or non-finite magnitude are rejected before normalization. The server caps hitscan range at MaxDistance on its authoritative ray; applySpread is applied client-side for feel only — the server recasts from the validated origin and does not verify the spread angle.  Friendly-fire prevention Enforced in CombatService.ApplyToModel via Factions.canDamage. Only Player↔Enemy damage lands. Players never damage other players or friendly NPCs; enemies never damage other enemies or friendly NPCs. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt — the self-check bypasses the faction gate so a player's own rocket can still hurt them if they walk into the blast.  NPC pass-through via CollectionService tag: the "EnemyNPC"/"FriendlyNPC" CollectionService tag is the dual-purpose NPC marker. It gates damage routing in CombatService (only tagged NPCs with a Humanoid take weapon damage) and, via NpcCollisionService, places NPC parts in the Character collision group so thrown charges physically pass through them (see Enemy Spawner → Collision and combat wiring). A Model without a recognized faction tag receives no damage and does not block thrown projectiles — tag it or it is invisible to the weapon system.  HealthManager routing via CombatService: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage (via CombatService) will leave the HUD showing a stale record value. Never write to humanoid.Health directly for player damage. See Health.  Hitbox debugging (WeaponDebug): flip the single ENABLED flag at the top of WeaponDebug.luau and save (Rojo syncs it in — no command bar, no attributes) to draw a bright Neon box for every melee/gun query volume, green on hit and red on whiff, auto-removed after LIFETIME seconds. Every weapon handler requires this module; it's the fastest way to confirm a hitbox query ran even when the part is off-screen.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant C as Client (handler) participant S as Server (WeaponServer) Note over C,S: MELEE C->>C: resolveComboSwing (prediction, tol=0); local hitbox -> WeaponLocalHit C->>S: ReqMeleeSwing() S->>S: fire-rate gate, resolveComboSwing (tol=0.05), queryMeleeTargets (server CFrame) S->>S: CombatService.ApplyToModel (Melee) S->>C: WeaponImpact(pos, name) C->>C: render impact FX + sound (WeaponEffectsController) Note over C,S: HITSCAN GUN C->>C: canFire gate + local ammo predict; muzzle flash + local tracer C->>S: ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir) S->>S: canFire, IsReloading, mag>0, origin tolerance (<=14 studs) S->>S: workspace:Raycast (capped MaxDistance); headshot x Multiplier on "Head" S->>S: CombatService.ApplyToModel (Bullet) S->>C: WeaponFired(shooter, name, origin, endpoint, isHit) S->>C: WeaponMagSync(name, mag) / AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) -> owner C->>C: WeaponEffectsController tracer for non-shooters; WeaponMagChanged for HUD Note over C,S: ROCKET (Gun / Projectile) C->>S: ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir) S->>S: same gates as hitscan; ServerProjectile.spawnRocket (anchored cosmetic, FastCast2-stepped) S->>S: FastCast2 Hit -> CombatService.ApplyAOE (AOE) S->>C: ExplosionAt(center, radius, name) C->>C: spawnExplosion + sound Note over C,S: GRENADE (Throwable / Fuse) C->>S: ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir) S->>S: cooldown gate + origin tolerance; ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable (Rest="Bounce") S->>S: task.delay(FuseTime) -> CombatService.ApplyAOE (AOE) S->>C: ExplosionAt(center, radius, name) Note over C,S: C4 (Throwable / Manual) C->>S: ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir) S->>S: MaxActive check; spawnThrowable (Rest="Stick"); WeaponState.AddActive(player, part) C->>S: ReqDetonate() S->>S: WeaponState.TakeAllActive; per charge: CombatService.ApplyAOE, part:Destroy() S->>C: ExplosionAt per charge

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: WeaponConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/WeaponConfig.luau. Edit stats here — never in handler or server code.Config module: AmmoConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/AmmoConfig.luau.  Common fields (all weapons): Category ("Melee"|"Gun"|"Throwable"), DisplayName, ToolName (must match the in-game Tool's Name exactly), Damage (base per-step/per-bullet; 0 for throwables, AOE only), DamageType ("Melee"|"Bullet"|"AOE"), HeadshotMultiplier? (gun only, applied on a ray hit against a part named "Head").  Melee fields: Range (forward reach/hitbox depth), HitboxSize (Vector3 width × height, Z ignored), SwingSound/ImpactSound (SoundConfig.Sfx keys), SwingAnimId?, Combos — map keyed by input ("Primary" = left-click; "Secondary" reserved). Each ComboDef has Steps[] (ordered ComboSteps; combo length = #Steps; each step has Recovery, ChainWindow, and optional overrides Damage?/Range?/HitboxSize?/AnimId?/SwingSound?/ImpactSound?) and ResetCooldown (lockout after the finisher before restarting at hit 1).  Gun fields: FireMode ("Hitscan"|"Projectile"), RPM (fire interval = 60/RPM), Automatic (hold-to-fire vs. semi), MagazineSize (reserve pool lives in AmmoManager, keyed by AmmoType), AmmoType ("Light"|"Heavy"|"Rocket"), ReloadTime, Spread (max cone half-angle, degrees), MaxDistance, FireSound/ReloadSound/DrySound/ImpactSound. Projectile-only additions: ProjectileSpeed, Gravity (Vector3), AOERadius, AOEDamage (center damage, linear falloff to 0 at radius), CosmeticTemplate (name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets).  Throwable fields: Detonation ("Fuse" auto after FuseTime | "Manual" all charges on ReqDetonate), Rest ("Bounce"|"Stick"), ThrowSpeed, FuseTime (Fuse only), MaxActive (Manual only, max simultaneous charges per player), AOERadius/AOEDamage, CooldownTime, CosmeticTemplate, ThrowSound/ExplodeSound.  Note: CarryCount has been removed. How many throwables a player carries is determined by how many matching Tool instances are in their Backpack (crafted or spawned); AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount reads this count at runtime.
